_about: Answers written for this test by AI agents that saw only the lesson and the question, never the keywords or model answers (Oct 2026). Not student text. 'right' answers must pass; 'wrong' answers (from _review/french/BATCH2-FINDINGS.md) must fail.

en: John 1:1 makes three claims about the Word. First, the Word already existed when the beginning began, so He is eternal and was never created. Second, the Word was with God, face to face, a distinct Person and not just an idea in God's mind. Third, the Word was God Himself, not 'a god' or a lesser creature, so this verse holds together full deity and distinct personhood and plants the seed of the Trinity.
The Word is eternal, is a distinct Person who was with God, and is fully God Himself, not a created or lesser god.
es: Juan 1:1 enseña tres cosas sobre el Verbo. Primero, el Verbo ya era cuando comenzó el principio; no llegó a existir, es eterno. Segundo, el Verbo era con Dios, cara a cara, una Persona distinta y no solo una idea en la mente de Dios. Tercero, el Verbo era Dios mismo, no 'un dios' ni una criatura superior, de modo que el versículo une plena deidad y Persona distinta y siembra la doctrina de la Trinidad.

en: John 1:3 says that all things were made through the Word and nothing that exists was made without Him. That means the Word is the Creator, not part of creation, from atoms to angels to galaxies. It matters because the same Jesus who grew tired and slept in a boat is the One who made the sea; the Maker entered His own creation. It confirms His deity and shows how astonishing the incarnation is.
Everything that exists was made through the Word, so He is the Creator and not a creature, which confirms that He is God.
es: Juan 1:3 enseña que todas las cosas fueron hechas por el Verbo y que sin Él nada de lo creado fue hecho. Por eso el Verbo es el Creador y no una criatura: hizo cada átomo, cada ángel y cada galaxia. Importa porque el mismo Jesús que se cansó y durmió en una barca es quien hizo el mar; el Hacedor entró en su propia obra. Esto confirma su deidad y muestra lo asombroso de la encarnación.

en: John 1:14 says the eternal Word, who is God and made all things, actually became a human being; He did not just visit or send a message. The word for 'dwelt' means He pitched His tent or tabernacled among us, recalling how God's glory filled the tabernacle in the wilderness. Now that glory was wrapped in a real human body living on the earth He made. The infinite became an infant, fully God and fully man in one Person.
The eternal God took on real human nature, and 'dwelt' means He tabernacled or pitched His tent among us, as God's glory once filled the wilderness tabernacle.
es: Juan 1:14 enseña que el Verbo eterno, que es Dios y creó todo, realmente se hizo hombre; no solo visitó el mundo ni mandó un mensaje. La palabra 'habitó' significa que plantó su tienda, que tabernaculó entre nosotros, recordando cómo la gloria de Dios llenó el tabernáculo en el desierto. Ahora esa gloria se envolvió en piel y hueso y vivió sobre el polvo que Él había hecho. El infinito se hizo infante, plenamente Dios y plenamente hombre.

en: John the Baptist was a man sent from God to bear witness to the Light, and the Gospel is careful to say he was not the Light himself. Though he was great and drew crowds, he kept pointing past himself, saying the One coming after him was before him because He existed from the beginning. When his followers worried about losing people to Jesus, he said, 'He must increase, but I must decrease.' A true witness does not draw attention to himself but directs people to Christ, like a finger pointing to the moon.
John was sent to testify to the Light but was not the Light; a true witness points away from himself to Christ, as in 'He must increase, but I must decrease.'
es: Juan el Bautista fue un hombre enviado de Dios para dar testimonio de la Luz, y el Evangelio aclara que él no era la Luz. Aunque era grande y las multitudes lo seguían, siempre señalaba más allá de sí mismo, diciendo que el que venía después de él era antes de él porque existía desde el principio. Cuando sus discípulos se inquietaron, respondió: 'A él conviene crecer, mas a mí menguar.' Un verdadero testigo no atrae la mirada hacia sí, sino hacia Cristo, como un dedo que señala la luna.

en: John 1:11 is the sad line: the Creator came to His own world and His own people, and they did not receive Him. But verse 12 opens a door: to as many as received Him, those who believe in His name, He gave the right to become children of God. The contrast is between rejection by those who should have known Him and the free gift given to anyone who receives Him. It is not based on deserving, earning, or religious standing but on receiving Christ by faith.
His own people rejected Him, yet anyone who receives Him by believing in His name is given the right to become a child of God, not by merit.
es: Juan 1:11 es la frase triste: el Hacedor vino a lo suyo, a su propio mundo y pueblo, y los suyos no le recibieron. Pero el versículo 12 abre la puerta: a todos los que le recibieron, a los que creen en su nombre, les dio potestad de ser hechos hijos de Dios. El contraste es entre el rechazo de quienes debían conocerle y el don gratuito para cualquiera que le recibe. No depende de merecerlo ni de ser religioso, sino de recibir a Cristo por la fe.

en: Being born of God means a second, spiritual birth that comes from above. John says it is not of blood, not of the will of the flesh, and not of the will of man, so it does not come from ancestry, human effort, or human decision alone. It is God's own work that makes a person His child. This prepares for Jesus' teaching to Nicodemus in John 3 about being born again.
It is a new spiritual birth from above, produced by God rather than by heritage or human will, making believers His children.
es: Ser engendrado de Dios significa un segundo nacimiento, espiritual, que viene de lo alto. Juan dice que no es de sangre, ni de voluntad de carne, ni de voluntad de varón, así que no viene de la descendencia ni del esfuerzo humano. Es obra de Dios mismo que hace a la persona hija suya. Esto prepara la enseñanza de Jesús a Nicodemo en Juan 3 sobre nacer de nuevo.

en: John 1:18 says no one has ever seen God, but the only begotten Son, who is in the Father's bosom, has declared Him. The Greek word behind 'declared' is the root of our word 'exegesis,' so Jesus is the explanation or interpretation of God. If we want to know what God is like, we should not guess or only look at nature; we look at Jesus. He makes the invisible Father known.
Though no one has seen God, the Son has explained Him; 'declared' is related to 'exegesis,' so Jesus is the explanation of the Father.
es: Juan 1:18 dice que nadie ha visto jamás a Dios, pero el Hijo unigénito, que está en el seno del Padre, le ha dado a conocer. La palabra detrás de 'dar a conocer' es la raíz de 'exégesis', así que Jesús es la explicación de Dios. Si queremos saber cómo es Dios, no debemos adivinar ni solo mirar al cielo, sino mirar a Jesús. Él nos revela al Padre invisible.

en: Matthew goes back to Abraham and Luke to Adam, but John reaches before creation to show who Jesus really is from the start. He deliberately echoes Genesis 1:1, 'In the beginning,' to present Jesus as the eternal God. John had walked with Jesus and come to know that the carpenter of Nazareth was God, so he announces it in the first line rather than building to it. Everything else in the Gospel, the signs, I AM sayings, and witnesses, depends on getting that identity right.
John starts in eternity, echoing Genesis 1:1, to declare from the first line that Jesus is the eternal God, which the rest of the Gospel proves.
es: Mateo se remonta a Abraham y Lucas a Adán, pero Juan va más allá de la creación para mostrar desde el principio quién es realmente Jesús. Hace eco deliberado de Génesis 1:1, 'En el principio', para presentar a Jesús como el Dios eterno. Juan había conocido a Jesús de cerca y sabía que el carpintero de Nazaret era Dios, así que lo anuncia en la primera línea en vez de llegar a ello al final. Todo lo demás del Evangelio depende de entender bien esta identidad.

en: The lesson shows Christ through pairs: as a man He grew tired, slept in the storm, hungered, wept, and died, but as God He upholds all things, walked on the waves, is the bread of life and the resurrection, and rose from death. These pairs show that He is fully God and fully man at the same time. He is not half of each, not God in a costume, and not a man promoted to God, but both natures joined forever in one Person. This mystery is meant to lead us to worship.
Christ shows real human weakness and real divine power at once, because He is fully God and fully man in one Person.
es: La lección presenta a Cristo con pares: como hombre se cansó, durmió en la tormenta, tuvo hambre, lloró y murió, pero como Dios sostiene todas las cosas, caminó sobre las olas, es el pan de vida y la resurrección, y salió de la tumba. Estos pares muestran que es plenamente Dios y plenamente hombre a la vez. No es mitad y mitad, ni Dios disfrazado, ni un hombre ascendido a Dios, sino ambas naturalezas unidas para siempre en una sola Persona. Este misterio nos lleva a adorar.

en: John 20:31 states the purpose: these things are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in His name. The Prologue serves that aim by declaring at the start who Jesus is: the eternal Word who is God, the Creator, who became flesh and revealed the Father. It also introduces the theme of witness and of receiving Him to become God's children. With that foundation, the signs, I AM sayings, and witnesses that follow make sense.
The Gospel is written so people will believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life; the Prologue lays the foundation by declaring His deity first.
es: Juan 20:31 da el propósito: estas cosas se escribieron para que creáis que Jesús es el Cristo, el Hijo de Dios, y para que creyendo tengáis vida en su nombre. El Prólogo sirve a ese fin al declarar desde el inicio quién es Jesús: el Verbo eterno que es Dios, el Creador, que se hizo carne y reveló al Padre. También introduce el tema del testimonio y de recibirle para ser hijos de Dios. Con ese fundamento, las señales, los 'YO SOY' y los testigos cobran todo su peso.

en: Jesus told Nicodemus that unless a person is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God. The word translated 'again' also means 'from above,' so this is a second, spiritual birth that comes down from God, not a natural one. It is necessary because being a son of Abraham and keeping the law, which Nicodemus trusted, was not enough. Without this new birth no one can enter God's kingdom.
It is a second, spiritual birth from above worked by God, and without it no one can see or enter the kingdom of God.
es: Jesús le dijo a Nicodemo que el que no naciere de nuevo no puede ver el reino de Dios. La palabra 'de nuevo' también significa 'de lo alto', así que es un segundo nacimiento espiritual que viene de Dios, no un nacimiento natural. Es necesario porque ser hijo de Abraham y guardar la ley, en lo cual confiaba Nicodemo, no bastaba. Sin este nuevo nacimiento nadie puede entrar en el reino de Dios.

en: Nicodemus took Jesus literally and asked how an old man could enter his mother's womb a second time. He was thinking about the flesh while Jesus was speaking about the Spirit. This shows the blindness of the natural mind: even a learned teacher of Israel could not grasp what a child can receive by faith. Spiritual truth is not understood by human reasoning alone but must be revealed by God's Spirit.
He thought Jesus meant a second physical birth, showing that the natural mind cannot grasp spiritual things without the Spirit.
es: Nicodemo entendió a Jesús de forma literal y preguntó cómo un hombre viejo podía entrar otra vez en el vientre de su madre. Él pensaba en la carne, mientras Jesús hablaba del Espíritu. Esto muestra la ceguera de la mente natural: un docto maestro de Israel no podía ver lo que un niño puede recibir. Las verdades espirituales no se entienden solo con la razón humana; el Espíritu tiene que revelarlas.

en: Jesus said the wind blows where it wishes; you hear its sound but cannot tell where it comes from or where it goes, and so is everyone born of the Spirit. We cannot see, command, or schedule the wind, yet we know it is real by its effects. In the same way, the Spirit works sovereignly and invisibly, and we recognize His work by the changed life it produces. Our part is to open our hearts and receive what He does.
Like the wind, the Spirit is unseen and cannot be controlled, but His work in the new birth is real and known by its effects.
es: Jesús dijo que el viento sopla de donde quiere; oyes su sonido pero no sabes de dónde viene ni a dónde va, y así es todo el que es nacido del Espíritu. No podemos ver, mandar ni programar el viento, pero sabemos que es real por lo que hace. De igual modo, el Espíritu obra de manera soberana e invisible, y reconocemos su obra por la vida transformada. Nuestra parte es abrir el corazón y recibir lo que Él obra.

en: The first birth is our natural, physical birth, which every person has and which we did not choose. Flesh can only produce more flesh and can never lift itself up into the things of God. The second birth is spiritual, produced by the Holy Spirit, and it gives a new nature that is alive to God. Jesus' words 'born of water and the Spirit' can be read as pointing to these two births, natural and spiritual.
Natural birth only produces natural life; only the Spirit can produce spiritual life, so a second birth by the Spirit is needed.
es: El primer nacimiento es el natural, físico, que todos tenemos y que no elegimos. La carne solo puede producir carne y nunca puede elevarse a las cosas de Dios. El segundo nacimiento es espiritual, producido por el Espíritu Santo, y da una nueva naturaleza viva para Dios. Las palabras 'nacer de agua y del Espíritu' pueden entenderse como estos dos nacimientos, el natural y el espiritual.

en: The new birth is the supernatural work of the Holy Spirit; nothing less than God can accomplish it. Jesus said no one can come to Him unless the Father who sent Him draws him. This means we cannot produce spiritual life by our own decision, effort, or religious ceremony. The new birth is God's work before it is ever our choice, and our role is to receive it.
God by His Spirit produces the new birth, and the Father must draw us, so human ability alone cannot achieve it.
es: El nuevo nacimiento es obra sobrenatural del Espíritu Santo; nada menos que Dios puede lograrlo. Jesús dijo que nadie puede venir a Él si el Padre que lo envió no lo trae. Esto significa que no podemos producir vida espiritual por nuestra propia decisión, esfuerzo o ceremonia religiosa. El nuevo nacimiento es obra de Dios antes de ser nuestra elección, y nuestra parte es recibirlo.

en: Jesus does not present the new birth as an option but as an absolute: 'You must be born again,' and unless one is born of water and the Spirit he cannot enter the kingdom. Every person faces death and then judgment, so we must be prepared to meet God. The lesson pictures the kingdom as a locked door with only one key, or a border that requires a passport; the new birth is that key or passport. Without it there is no entry, no matter one's church, heritage, or intentions.
Jesus says we 'must' be born again; it is the only way into God's kingdom, and everyone will face death and judgment.
es: Jesús no presenta el nuevo nacimiento como una opción sino como un absoluto: 'Os es necesario nacer de nuevo', y el que no naciere de agua y del Espíritu no puede entrar en el reino. Todos enfrentaremos la muerte y luego el juicio, así que debemos prepararnos para encontrarnos con Dios. La lección lo compara con una puerta cerrada que tiene una sola llave, o con un pasaporte para cruzar una frontera; esa llave es el nuevo nacimiento. Sin él no hay entrada, sin importar la iglesia o la herencia.

en: In the wilderness, Israelites were dying from snake bites, and God told Moses to lift up a bronze serpent on a pole; whoever looked at it lived. Jesus said the Son of Man must be lifted up in the same way so that whoever believes in Him will have eternal life. This foretells the cross. Just as the dying did not have to earn or even understand but only look, sinners are saved by looking in faith to the crucified Savior.
As those bitten looked at the lifted serpent and lived, sinners who look in faith to Christ lifted up on the cross receive eternal life.
es: En el desierto los israelitas morían por mordeduras de serpiente, y Dios mandó a Moisés levantar una serpiente de bronce sobre un asta; todo el que la miraba vivía. Jesús dijo que así es necesario que el Hijo del Hombre sea levantado, para que todo aquel que en Él cree tenga vida eterna. Esto anuncia la cruz. Como los moribundos no tenían que ganar nada sino solo mirar, el pecador es salvo al mirar con fe al Salvador crucificado.

en: John 3:16 says God loved the world so much that He gave His only begotten Son, so that whoever believes in Him will not perish but have everlasting life. It shows that salvation flows from God's love and His gift of His Son. The word 'whoever' means the offer is open to anyone, not just the worthy, the clean, or the Jews. The door to salvation is as wide as that word, and the condition is believing in Him.
God's love gave His Son so believers have eternal life, and 'whoever' means the offer is open to anyone who believes.
es: Juan 3:16 dice que de tal manera amó Dios al mundo que dio a su Hijo unigénito, para que todo aquel que en Él cree no se pierda, mas tenga vida eterna. Muestra que la salvación nace del amor de Dios y del don de su Hijo. 'Todo aquel' significa que la oferta es para cualquiera, no solo para los dignos, los limpios o los judíos. La puerta es tan ancha como esas palabras, y la condición es creer en Él.

en: John 3:17 says God did not send His Son to condemn the world but so the world might be saved through Him; He came with a cross, not a gavel. Yet verse 19 explains why people still face condemnation: the light has come, but men loved darkness rather than light because their deeds were evil. The problem is never that the light is too dim but that people close their eyes to it. Whoever comes to the light shows that he is born of God.
es: Juan 3:17 dice que Dios no envió a su Hijo para condenar al mundo, sino para que el mundo sea salvo por Él; vino con una cruz, no con un mazo de juez. Pero el versículo 19 explica la condenación: la luz vino al mundo y los hombres amaron más las tinieblas que la luz, porque sus obras eran malas. El problema no es que la luz sea débil, sino que los hombres cierran los ojos. El que viene a la luz muestra que es nacido de Dios.

en: The new birth is not a touch-up or turning over a new leaf but a change from the inside out. The lesson uses the caterpillar, which enters a cocoon and comes out not as a better caterpillar but as a creature with wings. In the same way, the old nature is put to death and a new nature alive to God is given. R. A. Torrey's conversion, from despair and unbelief to a life that led thousands to Christ, illustrates this Spirit-worked change.
It is an inward change in which the old nature dies and a new nature alive to God is given, like a caterpillar becoming a butterfly.
es: El nuevo nacimiento no es un retoque ni simplemente dar vuelta a la hoja, sino una transformación de adentro hacia afuera. La lección usa la oruga que entra en un capullo y sale no como una oruga mejor, sino como una criatura con alas. Así la vieja naturaleza muere y se nos da una nueva naturaleza viva para Dios. La conversión de R. A. Torrey, de la desesperación y la incredulidad a guiar a miles a Cristo, ilustra este cambio obrado por el Espíritu.

en: The woman thought only of the water in Jacob's well, but Jesus was offering the gift of God, which is ultimately Himself and eternal life. Well water satisfies for a few hours and then you are thirsty again. The water Christ gives becomes a fountain inside the person, springing up into everlasting life, so the one who drinks it will never thirst again. It does not run out or need to be rationed; it overflows.
Living water is the gift of eternal life in Christ Himself; unlike well water, which leaves you thirsty again, it becomes an endless fountain within.
es: La mujer solo pensaba en el agua del pozo de Jacob, pero Jesús le ofrecía el don de Dios, que es Él mismo y la vida eterna. El agua del pozo satisface unas horas y luego vuelve la sed. El agua que Cristo da se vuelve en el creyente una fuente que salta para vida eterna, de modo que el que la bebe no tendrá sed jamás. No se acaba ni se raciona; se desborda.

en: Jesus crossed three walls that a respectable rabbi would not climb. She was a Samaritan, and Jews and Samaritans despised each other; she was a woman, and teachers did not speak with women in public; and she was known as a great sinner, with five past husbands and living with a man who was not her husband. Yet Jesus started the conversation Himself by asking for a drink. This shows that His grace reaches outsiders and those others consider hopeless cases.
He crossed ethnic, gender, and moral barriers to speak with a Samaritan woman known as a sinner, showing His grace reaches even the outcast.
es: Jesús cruzó tres muros que un rabí respetable no escalaría. Ella era samaritana, y judíos y samaritanos se despreciaban; era mujer, y los maestros no hablaban con mujeres en público; y era conocida como gran pecadora, con cinco maridos y viviendo con un hombre que no era su esposo. Aun así, Jesús inició la conversación pidiéndole agua. Esto muestra que su gracia alcanza a los marginados y a los que otros consideran casos perdidos.

en: The woman raised the old dispute over whether the right place to worship was the Samaritans' mountain or Jerusalem. Jesus lifted the question higher: because God is Spirit, true worship is not finally about the right mountain or building. It must come from the heart, by the Spirit, and according to the truth God has revealed. Worship is a matter of inward reality and truth, not location or ritual.
Since God is Spirit, true worship depends not on a place but on a heart worshiping by the Spirit and according to God's truth.
es: La mujer planteó la vieja disputa sobre si se debía adorar en el monte de los samaritanos o en Jerusalén. Jesús elevó la cuestión: porque Dios es Espíritu, la verdadera adoración no depende del monte ni del edificio correcto. Debe salir del corazón, por el Espíritu, y conforme a la verdad de Dios. La adoración es una realidad interior y verdadera, no cuestión de lugar ni de rito.

en: When the woman spoke of the coming Messiah, Jesus told her plainly, 'I who speak to you am He.' He had not said this so openly to anyone else. It is striking because she was a Samaritan, a woman, an outsider, and a sinner, meeting Him at a well at noon. The first person to hear Jesus openly name Himself Messiah was someone society rejected, showing His grace toward the least likely.
He told her directly, 'I who speak to you am He,' and the first to hear this was an outcast Samaritan woman, which highlights His grace.
es: Cuando la mujer habló del Mesías que vendría, Jesús le dijo claramente: 'Yo soy, el que habla contigo.' No lo había dicho tan abiertamente a nadie más. Es notable porque ella era samaritana, mujer, marginada y pecadora, y lo encontró junto a un pozo al mediodía. La primera persona en oír a Jesús declararse Mesías abiertamente fue alguien a quien la sociedad rechazaba, lo cual muestra su gracia hacia los menos esperados.

en: After meeting Jesus, the woman left her waterpot and ran into town to the very people who knew her reputation. She said, 'Come, see a Man who told me all things that I ever did. Could this be the Christ?' She had no training or method, just a personal testimony and an invitation. Many Samaritans believed because of her word, and then many more believed after hearing Jesus for themselves and called Him the Savior of the world.
She left her waterpot, went to her town, and simply invited people to 'come and see' Jesus, and many believed through her testimony.
es: Después de conocer a Jesús, la mujer dejó su cántaro y corrió al pueblo, a la misma gente que conocía su reputación. Dijo: 'Venid, ved un hombre que me ha dicho todo cuanto he hecho. ¿No es éste el Cristo?' No tenía preparación ni método, solo su testimonio y una invitación. Muchos samaritanos creyeron por su palabra, y luego muchos más creyeron al oír a Jesús mismo y lo llamaron el Salvador del mundo.

en: The Divine Partnership means God provides salvation and the power of His Spirit, and then works through His people to accomplish His purpose. Philippians 2:13 says it is God who works in us both to will and to do. The lesson compares this to a garden: God gives life, sun, and rain, but the gardener must tend it. In John 4, Jesus sowed in one woman, and she carried the message to her village; one sows and another reaps, and both rejoice together while God gives the increase.
God supplies salvation and His Spirit's power, and then works through believers to accomplish His purposes, so both sower and reaper share the harvest.
es: La Asociación Divina significa que Dios provee la salvación y el poder de su Espíritu, y luego obra a través de su pueblo para cumplir su propósito. Filipenses 2:13 dice que Dios produce en nosotros así el querer como el hacer. La lección lo compara con un jardín: Dios da la vida, el sol y la lluvia, pero el jardinero debe cuidarlo. En Juan 4, Jesús sembró en una mujer y ella llevó el mensaje a su pueblo; uno siembra y otro siega, ambos se gozan, y Dios da el crecimiento.

en: When the disciples urged Jesus to eat, He said His food was to do the Father's will and finish His work. Then He pointed to the Samaritans coming out of town toward Him and told the disciples to look at the fields already white for harvest. He meant people were ready to receive the gospel now, not at some later season. Because He had sown in one woman, a whole village was ripening, and the disciples were called to reap and share the joy.
People were ready to believe right then, as the Samaritans coming to Jesus showed, so the disciples should see the urgent opportunity and reap.
es: Cuando los discípulos le rogaron que comiera, Jesús dijo que su comida era hacer la voluntad del Padre y acabar su obra. Luego señaló a los samaritanos que salían del pueblo hacia Él y dijo que miraran los campos ya blancos para la siega. Quería decir que la gente estaba lista para recibir el evangelio ahora, no en otro tiempo. Por haber sembrado en una mujer, toda una aldea maduraba, y los discípulos debían segar y compartir el gozo.

en: The disciples were trained men who had been with Jesus, yet they went into the same town and came back with food but no converts; there is no sign they spoke to anyone. The woman had no training and a bad reputation, yet her excited testimony brought many to Jesus. The contrast shows that God uses grateful, willing witnesses more than qualifications. A person who has truly tasted the living water naturally overflows with it.
The trained disciples brought back only bread, while the untrained woman brought a town to Jesus, showing God uses willing, grateful witnesses.
es: Los discípulos eran hombres entrenados que habían estado con Jesús, pero fueron al mismo pueblo y volvieron con pan y sin convertidos; no hay señal de que hablaran con nadie. La mujer no tenía preparación y sí mala fama, pero su testimonio entusiasta llevó a muchos a Jesús. El contraste muestra que Dios usa testigos agradecidos y dispuestos más que credenciales. Quien de verdad ha bebido del agua viva rebosa de ella.

en: The lesson lists several kinds of evangelists: the mass evangelist like Billy Graham, the apologist or defender of the faith like Lee Strobel, Josh McDowell, and Nabeel Qureshi, and the serving evangelist like Barnabas. There is the tract evangelist like the paralyzed J. D. Fore, the timid evangelist like the man on George Street in Sydney asking one question, and the invitational evangelist like the Samaritan woman. The truth is that every believer is on the team; there is not just one kind of witness. Anyone who has tasted the living water can at least say 'come and see.'
There are mass, apologetic, serving, tract, timid, and invitational evangelists, which shows every believer has a part in sharing the gospel.
es: La lección menciona varios tipos de evangelistas: el masivo como Billy Graham, el apologista o defensor de la fe como Lee Strobel, Josh McDowell y Nabeel Qureshi, y el de servicio como Bernabé. También está el de folletos, como el paralítico J. D. Fore, el tímido, como el hombre de George Street en Sídney que hacía una sola pregunta, y el invitador, como la mujer samaritana. La verdad es que cada creyente forma parte del equipo; no hay un solo tipo de testigo. Todo el que ha bebido del agua viva puede decir 'ven y ve'.

en: Every person is made with a thirst that the world's wells, such as money, pleasure, approval, or relationships, cannot fill; they satisfy for a moment and then the dryness returns. The Samaritan woman had tried those wells many times. Jesus offered her Himself, and in Him alone are found both salvation and a real purpose for living. Like Niagara Falls that never stops pouring, His supply never runs dry.
Only Christ satisfies the soul's deep thirst; the world's sources run dry, but He gives salvation and lasting purpose that never fail.
es: Cada persona fue hecha con una sed que los pozos del mundo, como el dinero, el placer, la aprobación o las relaciones, no pueden llenar; satisfacen un momento y luego vuelve la sequedad. La mujer samaritana había probado esos pozos muchas veces. Jesús se ofreció a sí mismo, y solo en Él se hallan la salvación y un verdadero propósito para vivir. Como las Cataratas del Niágara que nunca se detienen, su provisión jamás se seca.

en: The feeding of the five thousand is the only miracle that all four Gospel writers recorded, which shows how important it was considered. It recalls Israel in the wilderness, when a huge crowd of former slaves had no food and no human solution, a God-sized problem. God answered then with manna, bread from heaven. In John 6 there is again a great crowd in an empty place with no food, and the same God provides, but this time Jesus goes on to say that He Himself is the Bread.
It is the only miracle in all four Gospels, and like the manna God gave Israel in the wilderness, God provided bread for a hungry crowd with no human solution.
es: La alimentación de los cinco mil es el único milagro que registraron los cuatro evangelistas, lo que muestra su importancia. Nos recuerda a Israel en el desierto, cuando una multitud de antiguos esclavos no tenía comida ni solución humana, un problema del tamaño de Dios. Entonces Dios respondió con maná, pan del cielo. En Juan 6 vuelve a haber una gran multitud en un lugar desierto sin comida, y el mismo Dios provee, pero esta vez Jesús dice que Él mismo es el Pan.

en: Philip calculated the cost and gave up, saying that even two hundred denarii, about eight months' wages, would not buy enough for each person to have a little. Andrew found a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish, the poor man's food, but asked what that was among so many. John notes that Jesus already knew what He would do. He let the problem grow in the disciples' eyes so they would learn that the answer was not in their arithmetic but in their Lord.
Philip despaired over the cost, Andrew found a boy's small lunch but doubted it; Jesus already knew His plan and was teaching them to look to Him, not their math.
es: Felipe hizo la cuenta y se rindió: ni doscientos denarios, unos ocho meses de salario, alcanzarían para que cada uno comiera un poco. Andrés encontró a un muchacho con cinco panes de cebada y dos pececillos, comida de los pobres, pero preguntó qué era eso entre tantos. Juan señala que Jesús ya sabía lo que iba a hacer. Dejó que el problema creciera ante los discípulos para que aprendieran que la respuesta no estaba en su aritmética sino en su Señor.

en: Jesus was moved with compassion for the crowd and healed their sick; the Gospels mention His compassion six times, and it was a flood in Him. The lesson rejects the idea that the Old Testament God is harsh while Jesus is kind, as if they were two different Gods. There is no difference between the Father and the Son; the Old Testament repeatedly speaks of God's compassion, and God was in Christ reconciling the world. The same heart that gave Israel manna fed the crowd by Galilee, and that compassion should now flow through us as His body.
Compassion moved Him, and the lesson says the Father and the Son are not different; the same compassionate God who gave manna fed the crowd in Christ.
es: Jesús tuvo compasión de la multitud y sanó a sus enfermos; los Evangelios mencionan su compasión seis veces, y en Él era un torrente. La lección rechaza la idea de que el Dios del Antiguo Testamento es duro y Jesús bondadoso, como si fueran dos dioses distintos. No hay diferencia entre el Padre y el Hijo; el Antiguo Testamento habla a menudo de la compasión de Dios, y Dios estaba en Cristo reconciliando al mundo. El mismo corazón que dio el maná alimentó a la multitud, y esa compasión ahora debe fluir por nosotros.

en: Mary Reed was born in Ohio in 1858 and went to India, where she could not forget a forsaken colony of about five hundred lepers in the Himalayas. When she learned she had leprosy herself, she accepted it as a strange gift from God that would let her live among them. She served those outcasts for fifty-three years until she died among them in 1943. Her story shows Christ's compassion flowing through a surrendered life to people no one else would touch.
Mary Reed contracted leprosy and served a leper colony in India for 53 years, showing Christ's compassion working through a surrendered life.
es: Mary Reed nació en Ohio en 1858 y fue a la India, donde no pudo olvidar a una colonia abandonada de unos quinientos leprosos en el Himalaya. Cuando supo que ella misma tenía lepra, lo aceptó como un extraño don de Dios que le permitiría vivir entre ellos. Sirvió a esos marginados durante cincuenta y tres años hasta morir entre ellos en 1943. Su historia muestra la compasión de Cristo fluyendo a través de una vida entregada hacia personas que nadie quería tocar.

en: After everyone was full, the disciples gathered twelve baskets of leftovers from five loaves, more than there was at the beginning; this shows grace upon grace that never runs out. It also shows that God takes a small gift surrendered to Him and multiplies it. The widow of Zarephath gave her last flour and oil to the prophet first and never ran empty. Dr. Cook says he was not a natural preacher, but he offered God his small gift and learned that God multiplies it, so the work is for God's glory, not his own.
The leftovers show God's abundant grace and that He multiplies small gifts given to Him, as with the widow's flour and oil and Dr. Cook's modest preaching gift.
es: Después de que todos se saciaron, recogieron doce cestas de sobras de cinco panes, más de lo que había al principio; esto muestra gracia sobre gracia que nunca se acaba. También enseña que Dios toma un pequeño don entregado a Él y lo multiplica. La viuda de Sarepta dio su última harina y aceite al profeta primero y nunca quedó vacía. El Dr. Cook cuenta que no era predicador natural, pero entregó su pequeño don y aprendió que Dios lo multiplica, para la gloria de Dios y no la suya.

en: The crowd wanted to force Jesus to be king because He could fill their stomachs and end every shortage. Jesus withdrew to the mountain alone because He would not be crowned on human terms or for human appetites; His kingdom comes from the Father, and He will reign in God's time. 'The Creator is no man's debtor' means God gives because He is good, not because we can corner or control Him. It warns against wanting Jesus for what He gives rather than for Himself.
He refused to be made king on man's terms; the saying warns against seeking Jesus for His gifts and treating God as if He owed us.
es: La multitud quería hacer rey a Jesús por la fuerza porque podía llenar sus estómagos y acabar con la escasez. Jesús se retiró solo al monte porque no sería coronado en los términos del hombre ni para sus apetitos; su reino viene de la mano del Padre, y reinará a su tiempo. 'El Creador no es deudor de nadie' significa que Dios da porque es bueno, no porque lo podamos acorralar. Advierte contra querer a Jesús por lo que da y no por Él mismo.

en: That evening the disciples were rowing across the lake in the dark against a storm, getting nowhere, when they saw Jesus walking on the water. They were terrified until He said, 'It is I; do not be afraid.' In Greek His words are literally 'I AM,' the name of God, showing that He is Lord over the sea He created. As soon as they received Him into the boat, they were immediately at the land where they were going.
Jesus walked on the stormy sea and said 'I AM,' the divine name; when they took Him into the boat, they immediately reached land.
es: Esa tarde los discípulos remaban en la oscuridad contra una tormenta sin avanzar, cuando vieron a Jesús caminando sobre el agua. Se aterraron hasta que Él dijo: 'Yo soy; no temáis.' En griego sus palabras son 'YO SOY', el nombre de Dios, mostrando que es Señor del mar que Él mismo creó. En cuanto lo recibieron en la barca, enseguida llegaron a la tierra adonde iban.

en: Jesus told the crowd they were not seeking Him because of the signs but because they had eaten the loaves and were full. He urged them not to labor for food that perishes but for food that lasts to eternal life. When they pointed to Moses and the manna, He said the manna was only a shadow and that the true Bread from heaven had now come and was standing before them. Then He declared, 'I am the bread of life.'
es: Jesús dijo a la multitud que no lo buscaban por las señales sino porque habían comido los panes y se habían saciado. Les exhortó a trabajar no por la comida que perece sino por la que permanece para vida eterna. Cuando le mencionaron a Moisés y el maná, respondió que el maná era solo una sombra y que el verdadero Pan del cielo había llegado y estaba delante de ellos. Entonces declaró: 'Yo soy el pan de vida.'

en: The real hunger of our time is a spiritual hunger for God. People try to fill that emptiness with food, sex, money, and recognition, but each leaves the soul as hollow as before. Augustine chased those things in his early years and was still starving. He finally concluded that God made us for Himself and our hearts are restless until they find their rest in Him.
Our deepest hunger is for God; people try money, pleasure, and fame, but Augustine learned our hearts are restless until they rest in God.
es: El verdadero hambre de nuestra época es hambre espiritual de Dios. La gente intenta llenar ese vacío con comida, sexo, dinero y reconocimiento, pero cada cosa deja el alma tan hueca como antes. Agustín persiguió esas cosas en su juventud y siguió hambriento. Finalmente concluyó que Dios nos hizo para sí y que nuestro corazón está inquieto hasta que descansa en Él.

en: In John 6:51 Jesus said the bread He would give is His flesh, given for the life of the world, pointing to the cross and to feeding on Him by faith. Many disciples found this too hard, turned back, and stopped following Him. When Jesus asked the Twelve if they would leave too, Peter answered, 'Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.' The lesson says that just as the boy gave his loaves and the disciples passed them on, we must carry the Bread we have received to a hungry, perishing world.
Jesus said He would give His flesh for the world's life; many left, but Peter said there was no one else to go to, and we must share this Bread with the world.
es: En Juan 6:51 Jesús dijo que el pan que daría es su carne, entregada por la vida del mundo, señalando la cruz y alimentarse de Él por la fe. A muchos discípulos les pareció demasiado duro, volvieron atrás y ya no andaban con Él. Cuando Jesús preguntó a los doce si también se irían, Pedro respondió: 'Señor, ¿a quién iremos? Tú tienes palabras de vida eterna.' La lección dice que, como el muchacho dio sus panes y los discípulos los repartieron, debemos llevar el Pan recibido a un mundo hambriento que perece.

en: Jesus did not say He would show us a light or teach about it; He said He Himself is the light, greater than the sun because He lights the depths of the soul. He promised that whoever follows Him will not walk in darkness but have the light of life. Following Him means being a disciple, a learner under His discipline and trained in the truth by the Master, not just an admirer. The early believers called themselves followers of 'the Way' because they fixed their eyes on Him and walked by His light.
Jesus Himself is the light who gives life to the soul, and following Him means being His disciple, a learner who walks by His light rather than a mere admirer.
es: Jesús no dijo que nos mostraría una luz ni que enseñaría acerca de ella; dijo que Él mismo es la luz, mayor que el sol porque alumbra lo hondo del alma. Prometió que el que le sigue no andará en tinieblas sino que tendrá la luz de la vida. Seguirle significa ser discípulo, un aprendiz bajo su disciplina, entrenado en la verdad por el Maestro, no un mero admirador. Los primeros creyentes se llamaban seguidores del 'Camino' porque fijaron los ojos en Él y andaban en su luz.

en: Light and darkness cannot share a room; one match in a cellar drives the dark away. When Jesus came, His light exposed people's hearts, but the darkness did not comprehend it, and people loved darkness because their deeds were evil and they hated having them exposed. The religious leaders thought keeping and tightening rules made them righteous, but the Light showed how far short their hearts fell. The Light also kindles: those who follow Christ reflect His light to others, like a small lighthouse flame magnified by mirrors.
Christ's light exposes sin and the darkness of human hearts, which is why those who love evil hate and reject it.
es: La luz y las tinieblas no pueden compartir un cuarto; un fósforo en un sótano hace ceder la oscuridad. Cuando Jesús vino, su luz expuso los corazones, pero las tinieblas no la comprendieron, y los hombres amaron más las tinieblas porque sus obras eran malas y no querían ser expuestos. Los líderes religiosos creían que guardar y apretar reglas los hacía justos, pero la Luz reveló cuán cortos quedaban sus corazones. La Luz también enciende: quienes siguen a Cristo reflejan su luz, como la pequeña llama de un faro multiplicada por espejos.

en: No one can see God, but in Jesus the invisible God is made visible. In Him the holiness known from the Old Testament is joined with a love and mercy people had hardly dared to see. Regarding the law, He did not come to abolish it but to fulfill it. He also exposed the leaders' mistaken idea that a list of rules could contain God's whole will.
In Jesus the invisible God's holiness and mercy are seen, and He came not to abolish the law but to fulfill it.
es: Nadie puede ver a Dios, pero en Jesús el Dios invisible se hace visible. En Él la santidad que conocíamos del Antiguo Testamento se une a un amor y una misericordia que apenas habíamos osado ver. En cuanto a la ley, no vino a abolirla sino a cumplirla. También expuso el error de los líderes, que pensaban que una lista de reglas podía contener toda la voluntad de Dios.

en: When the leaders mocked that He was not yet fifty and could not have seen Abraham, Jesus said, 'Before Abraham was, I AM.' He did not say 'I was,' but used 'I AM,' the name God revealed to Moses at the burning bush, the name of the eternal, self-existent God. So He claimed both to exist before Abraham and to bear the divine name. The leaders understood He was claiming to be God, and since they would not bow, they picked up stones to kill Him for blasphemy. They were right about the claim but wrong about the Man.
Jesus claimed eternal existence and the divine name 'I AM' from the burning bush; the leaders understood He was claiming to be God and tried to stone Him.
es: Cuando los líderes se burlaron de que aún no tenía cincuenta años y no podía haber visto a Abraham, Jesús dijo: 'Antes que Abraham fuese, yo soy.' No dijo 'yo era', sino 'YO SOY', el nombre que Dios reveló a Moisés en la zarza ardiente, el nombre del Dios eterno que existe por sí mismo. Así afirmó existir antes de Abraham y llevar el Nombre divino. Los líderes entendieron que se declaraba Dios, y como no querían inclinarse, tomaron piedras para matarlo. Acertaron sobre la afirmación pero se equivocaron sobre el Hombre.

en: In John 8 Jesus is the monogenes, the one unique Son who shares the Father's very nature, unlike believers who are adopted into God's family. From His mother He took a true humanity, so He could grow weary, thirst, and die. From the Father He has wisdom and power no man ever had, so He astonished teachers as a boy, knew strangers' secret lives, healed, walked on the sea, and rose from the dead. He is fully God and fully man in one Person, and His claim to equality with God, including 'before Abraham was, I AM,' is what made the leaders want to kill Him.
es: En Juan 8 Jesús es el monogenes, el Hijo único que comparte la naturaleza misma del Padre, a diferencia de los creyentes, que somos adoptados. De su madre tomó una verdadera humanidad, y por eso se cansó, tuvo sed y pudo morir. Del Padre tiene una sabiduría y un poder que ningún hombre tuvo: asombró a los maestros de niño, conocía la vida secreta de extraños, sanó, caminó sobre el mar y resucitó. Es plenamente Dios y plenamente hombre en una Persona, y su afirmación de igualdad con Dios, como 'antes que Abraham fuese, yo soy', provocó que quisieran matarlo.

en: The disciples assumed, as their culture did, that suffering like blindness from birth must be punishment for someone's sin, either the man's or his parents'. Jesus rejected that assumption and said neither had sinned, but the blindness existed so that the works of God would be revealed in him. Not every sorrow is a sentence for sin. God can use suffering as a stage for displaying His glory and power.
They assumed the blindness was punishment for sin; Jesus said it was not, but that God's works would be shown in him.
es: Los discípulos suponían, como toda su cultura, que un sufrimiento como la ceguera de nacimiento debía ser castigo por el pecado de alguien, del hombre o de sus padres. Jesús rechazó esa idea y dijo que ni él ni sus padres pecaron, sino que era para que las obras de Dios se manifestaran en él. No todo dolor es sentencia por pecado. Dios puede usar el sufrimiento como escenario para mostrar su gloria y su poder.

en: Saying 'As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world,' Jesus spat on the ground, made clay, anointed the blind man's eyes, and sent him to wash in the pool of Siloam, which means 'Sent.' The man went down in darkness and came back seeing. The sign shows Jesus doing literally what He claimed: as the Light of the world He gave sight to a man who had never seen. It echoes the Creator who once said, 'Let there be light.'
Jesus made clay, anointed the man's eyes, and sent him to wash in Siloam ('Sent'); he came back seeing, showing Jesus is truly the Light of the world.
es: Diciendo 'Entre tanto que estoy en el mundo, luz soy del mundo', Jesús escupió en tierra, hizo lodo, ungió los ojos del ciego y lo envió a lavarse al estanque de Siloé, que significa 'Enviado'. El hombre bajó en tinieblas y volvió viendo. La señal muestra a Jesús haciendo literalmente lo que afirmaba: como Luz del mundo dio vista a quien nunca había visto. Recuerda al Creador que una vez dijo: 'Sea la luz.'

en: At first the healed man simply calls Jesus 'a man called Jesus' and holds to what he knows: 'though I was blind, now I see.' Under pressure from the Pharisees he says, 'He is a prophet.' Then, despite their threats, he insists that if this Man were not from God He could do nothing. After he is thrown out of the synagogue, Jesus finds him and asks if he believes in the Son of God; he says, 'Lord, I believe,' and worships Him. His eyes opened in an instant, but his heart came into the light step by step.
He moves from 'a man called Jesus' to 'a prophet' to 'from God,' and finally believes in Him as Son of God and worships Him.
es: Al principio el hombre sanado llama a Jesús 'un hombre llamado Jesús' y se aferra a lo que sabe: 'habiendo yo sido ciego, ahora veo'. Presionado por los fariseos, dice: 'es un profeta'. Luego, a pesar de las amenazas, afirma que si no fuera de Dios nada podría hacer. Después de ser expulsado de la sinagoga, Jesús lo encuentra y le pregunta si cree en el Hijo de Dios; responde 'Creo, Señor' y le adora. Sus ojos se abrieron en un instante, pero su corazón llegó a la luz por grados.

en: The man born blind gained physical sight instantly and spiritual sight gradually, ending in worship, while the Pharisees, who had perfectly good eyes, grew darker the more they resisted. Jesus said He came so that those who do not see may see and those who see may become blind. When the Pharisees asked if they were blind too, He said that if they admitted blindness they would have no sin, but because they claimed to see, their sin remained. The only people the Light cannot help are those who insist they need no help.
Real sight is spiritual; the Pharisees could see physically but stayed in sin because they proudly claimed to see and would not admit their need.
es: El ciego de nacimiento recibió la vista física en un instante y la espiritual poco a poco, hasta adorar, mientras que los fariseos, con ojos sanos, se volvían más oscuros al resistir. Jesús dijo que vino para que los que no ven, vean, y los que ven, sean cegados. Cuando los fariseos preguntaron si ellos también eran ciegos, respondió que si fueran ciegos no tendrían pecado, pero porque decían 'vemos', su pecado permanecía. Las únicas personas a quienes la Luz no puede ayudar son las que insisten en que no necesitan ayuda.

en: The 'I AM' sayings echo the divine name God gave Moses, so each one is a claim to deity as well as a picture of what Jesus gives. In John He says He is the bread of life, the light of the world, the door, the good shepherd, the resurrection and the life, the way, the truth and the life, and the true vine. Together they show He alone satisfies, enlightens, gives access to God, protects and lays down His life, conquers death, is the only way to the Father, and gives fruitful life to those joined to Him. The absolute 'before Abraham was, I AM' makes the claim to be God explicit.
Using God's name 'I AM,' Jesus reveals He is God and the only source of life, light, and salvation for those who believe.
es: Las declaraciones 'YO SOY' hacen eco del nombre divino que Dios dio a Moisés, así que cada una es una afirmación de deidad y a la vez una imagen de lo que Jesús da. En Juan dice que Él es el pan de vida, la luz del mundo, la puerta, el buen pastor, la resurrección y la vida, el camino, la verdad y la vida, y la vid verdadera. Juntas muestran que solo Él satisface, ilumina, da acceso a Dios, protege y da su vida, vence la muerte y da fruto a los unidos a Él. El 'antes que Abraham fuese, yo soy' hace explícita su afirmación de ser Dios.

en: John's Gospel is built like a trial: the claim on the table is that Jesus is God in the flesh, and John calls witness after witness so the reader, like a juror, can weigh the evidence and reach a verdict. John 20:31 says he wrote so that we may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in His name. Under Jewish law a matter had to be established by two or three witnesses, since a single witness can be mistaken. Jesus offers far more than two, and they all agree, which leaves the reader without excuse.
John presents Jesus' claim like a court case with many agreeing witnesses, so readers can weigh the evidence and believe He is the Christ and have life.
es: El Evangelio de Juan está construido como un juicio: la afirmación es que Jesús es Dios en carne, y Juan llama testigo tras testigo para que el lector, como un jurado, pese la evidencia y dicte un veredicto. Juan 20:31 dice que escribió para que creamos que Jesús es el Cristo, el Hijo de Dios, y tengamos vida en su nombre. Según la ley judía, un asunto se establecía por dos o tres testigos, porque uno solo puede equivocarse. Jesús presenta muchos más de dos, y todos concuerdan, de modo que el lector queda sin excusa.

en: At the pool of Bethesda a man had been an invalid for thirty-eight years, and Jesus healed him with a word on the Sabbath. Instead of rejoicing, the leaders were furious. John 5:18 says they sought all the more to kill Him because He not only broke the Sabbath but also called God His Father, making Himself equal with God. Jesus did not deny that charge; He answered it by calling His witnesses.
Jesus healed a man sick 38 years on the Sabbath and called God His Father, so the leaders charged Him with making Himself equal with God.
es: En el estanque de Betesda un hombre había estado enfermo treinta y ocho años, y Jesús lo sanó con una palabra en sábado. En vez de alegrarse, los líderes se enfurecieron. Juan 5:18 dice que procuraban aún más matarle porque no solo quebrantaba el sábado, sino que decía que Dios era su Padre, haciéndose igual a Dios. Jesús no negó la acusación; la respondió llamando a sus testigos.

en: Jesus said He had a greater witness than John the Baptist: the works the Father gave Him to finish testify that the Father sent Him. His signs were not just wonders but sworn evidence of His identity. Beyond the works, the Father Himself who sent Him has testified of Him. The Father is the second witness the Law required and the highest witness of all.
His miracles are evidence that the Father sent Him, and the Father Himself also testifies, providing the highest witness.
es: Jesús dijo que tenía un testimonio mayor que el de Juan el Bautista: las obras que el Padre le dio para cumplir dan testimonio de que el Padre le envió. Sus señales no eran meras maravillas, sino evidencia jurada de su identidad. Además, el Padre mismo que le envió ha dado testimonio de Él. El Padre es el segundo testigo que la Ley exigía y el más alto de todos.

en: The leaders searched the Scriptures thinking that in them they had eternal life, but Jesus said those very Scriptures testify about Him. They had the witness in their hands and refused to hear it. He also said that He would not need to accuse them before the Father, because Moses, whom they trusted, accuses them, since Moses wrote about Him. So the lawgiver they relied on was actually a witness against their unbelief.
The Scriptures they studied point to Jesus, and Moses wrote about Him, so their own trusted authorities testify against their unbelief.
es: Los líderes escudriñaban las Escrituras pensando que en ellas tenían vida eterna, pero Jesús dijo que esas mismas Escrituras dan testimonio de Él. Tenían el testimonio en sus manos y no quisieron oírlo. También dijo que no necesitaba acusarlos ante el Padre, porque Moisés, en quien confiaban, los acusa, ya que él escribió de Jesús. El legislador en quien se apoyaban era testigo contra su incredulidad.

en: The Law required two witnesses, and Jesus named Himself and the Father, but Dr. Cook adds a third for today: the Holy Spirit. Jesus promised that the Helper, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, would testify of Him (John 15:26). The Spirit has never stopped testifying of Christ, both through the Scriptures He inspired and in the heart of every believer He has made alive. The same Spirit who convinced us that Jesus is Lord is a living witness today.
The Holy Spirit, the Spirit of truth, keeps testifying of Christ through Scripture and in believers' hearts, a living witness today.
es: La Ley exigía dos testigos, y Jesús nombró a sí mismo y al Padre, pero el Dr. Cook añade un tercero para hoy: el Espíritu Santo. Jesús prometió que el Consolador, el Espíritu de verdad que procede del Padre, daría testimonio de Él (Juan 15:26). El Espíritu nunca ha dejado de testificar de Cristo, en las Escrituras que inspiró y en el corazón de cada creyente que ha vivificado. El mismo Espíritu que nos convenció de que Jesús es Señor es hoy un testigo vivo.

en: When the Pharisees said His self-testimony was not valid, Jesus said it was true because He knew where He came from and where He was going, while they did not. A liar can be caught because he is inventing, but the Son speaks from firsthand knowledge of heaven, the Father, and His own eternal origin. He also said He did not stand alone: He and the Father together are the two witnesses the Law requires. So His testimony rests on a Son who cannot be mistaken about Himself and a Father who confirms every word.
He speaks from firsthand knowledge of His heavenly origin and destiny, and the Father also testifies, meeting the Law's two-witness requirement.
es: Cuando los fariseos dijeron que su testimonio de sí mismo no era válido, Jesús respondió que era verdadero porque sabía de dónde venía y a dónde iba, y ellos no. A un mentiroso se le atrapa porque inventa, pero el Hijo habla desde el conocimiento de primera mano del cielo, del Padre y de su origen eterno. Además, no estaba solo: Él y el Padre juntos son los dos testigos que la Ley exige. Su testimonio descansa en un Hijo que no puede equivocarse sobre sí mismo y un Padre que confirma cada palabra.

en: The Samaritan woman, after Jesus told her everything she had done, ran into her town and said, 'Come, see a Man who told me all that I ever did. Could this be the Christ?' Many believed because of her word. The man born blind, brought before the council and pressured to deny his Healer, said, 'One thing I know: that though I was blind, now I see.' His parents dodged the question out of fear, but he testified anyway and was cast out of the synagogue. Neither was a trained theologian; each simply told what they had seen of Christ.
The woman invited her town to 'come, see' Jesus, and the healed blind man boldly testified 'now I see' even though he was thrown out of the synagogue.
es: La mujer samaritana, después de que Jesús le dijo todo lo que había hecho, corrió a su pueblo diciendo: 'Venid, ved un hombre que me ha dicho todo cuanto he hecho. ¿No es éste el Cristo?' Muchos creyeron por su palabra. El hombre que nació ciego, llevado ante el concilio y presionado a negar a su Sanador, dijo: 'Una cosa sé: que habiendo yo sido ciego, ahora veo.' Sus padres esquivaron la pregunta por miedo, pero él testificó y fue expulsado de la sinagoga. Ninguno era teólogo; cada uno contó lo que había visto de Cristo.

en: The nobleman's son was dying, and Jesus healed him from a distance. The father did not keep that mercy to himself; he believed, and his whole household believed with him (John 4:53). Mary Magdalene, a woman from whom seven demons had gone out, was weeping at the empty tomb when she met the risen Lord. She became the first witness of the resurrection, running to the disciples to say, 'I have seen the Lord!'
The nobleman believed with his whole household after Jesus healed his son from afar, and Mary Magdalene became the first witness of the resurrection: 'I have seen the Lord!'
es: El hijo del noble estaba muriendo, y Jesús lo sanó a distancia. El padre no se guardó esa misericordia: creyó él con toda su casa (Juan 4:53). María Magdalena, de quien habían salido siete demonios, lloraba ante la tumba vacía cuando encontró al Señor resucitado. Llegó a ser la primera testigo de la resurrección, corriendo a los discípulos para decir: '¡He visto al Señor!'

en: After so many sure witnesses, Jesus told the leaders, 'You are not willing to come to Me that you may have life.' The tragedy is that the problem was never a lack of evidence. It was an unwilling will; they simply refused to come. Unbelief, then, is often a moral and volitional refusal rather than an intellectual difficulty.
It shows unbelief is not caused by lack of evidence but by an unwillingness to come to Christ for life.
es: Después de tantos testigos seguros, Jesús dijo a los líderes: 'No queréis venir a mí, para que tengáis vida.' La tragedia es que el problema nunca fue falta de evidencia. Fue una voluntad que no quería; sencillamente se negaron a venir. La incredulidad, entonces, suele ser un rechazo de la voluntad más que una dificultad intelectual.

en: Having set all the witnesses before us, the Baptist, the works, the Father, the Scriptures, Moses, the Spirit, and many changed lives, John asks for our verdict. The only honest verdict is that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and by believing we have life in His name. Then believers are called to take the stand themselves, for Jesus said, 'You shall be witnesses to Me' (Acts 1:8). Like the Samaritan woman and the blind man, we do not need cleverness, only firsthand knowledge of Christ to say 'come and see' or 'now I see.'
The verdict is to believe Jesus is the Christ and have life, and every believer is then called to be a witness of what Christ has done.
es: Después de presentar todos los testigos, el Bautista, las obras, el Padre, las Escrituras, Moisés, el Espíritu y muchas vidas cambiadas, Juan pide nuestro veredicto. El único veredicto honesto es que Jesús es el Cristo, el Hijo de Dios, y que al creer tenemos vida en su nombre. Luego cada creyente es llamado a subir al estrado, pues Jesús dijo: 'Me seréis testigos' (Hechos 1:8). Como la samaritana y el ciego, no necesitamos astucia, sino haber conocido a Cristo para decir 'ven y ve' o 'ahora veo'.

en: Isaiah 53:6 says all of us like sheep have gone astray, each turning to his own way. Sheep need more care than any other farm animal: they are timid, stubborn, quick to wander, and a lost sheep cannot find its way home. Phillip Keller's restless fence-crawling ewe, who led other sheep out to barren ground, pictures how we wander and lead others astray. Because we are helpless and lost on our own, we desperately need a shepherd to guide, protect, and bring us home.
Like sheep we are prone to wander and cannot find our way back on our own, so we need a shepherd to lead and protect us.
es: Isaías 53:6 dice que todos nosotros nos descarriamos como ovejas, cada cual por su camino. Las ovejas necesitan más cuidado que cualquier otro animal: son tímidas, tercas, se extravían fácilmente y una oveja perdida no sabe volver a casa. La oveja inquieta de Phillip Keller, que se escabullía por la cerca y llevaba a otras al terreno yermo, ilustra cómo nos desviamos y arrastramos a otros. Como somos indefensos y perdidos, necesitamos un pastor que nos guíe, proteja y lleve a casa.

en: In the warm season, shepherds kept the flock at night in a rough hillside fold, a space surrounded by a low stone wall with one opening but no gate. The shepherd lay down across that opening, so no sheep could get out and no wolf could get in except over his body; he literally was the door. Jesus said, 'I am the door. If anyone enters by Me, he will be saved, and will go in and out and find pasture.' The sheep go in for safety at night and out to pasture in the morning, and both ways are through Him.
The shepherd slept across the gateless opening of the fold, becoming the door; likewise Jesus is the one entrance to salvation, safety, and pasture.
es: En la estación cálida, el pastor guardaba el rebaño de noche en un redil rudo en la ladera, un espacio con un muro bajo y una sola abertura sin puerta. El pastor se acostaba atravesado en la abertura, de modo que ninguna oveja salía ni ningún lobo entraba sino por encima de su cuerpo; él era literalmente la puerta. Jesús dijo: 'Yo soy la puerta; el que por mí entrare, será salvo; y entrará, y saldrá, y hallará pastos.' Las ovejas entran de noche para estar seguras y salen de mañana a los pastos, y siempre por Él.

en: Jesus said the thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy, but He came so His sheep may have life and have it more abundantly. The thieves and robbers were the false leaders who set themselves up as gatekeepers to God and shut people out of the kingdom they claimed to guard. The thief takes from the sheep for his own benefit. The Shepherd gives, and gives overflowing life.
The thief takes and destroys, but Jesus gives life to the full, abundant and overflowing.
es: Jesús dijo que el ladrón no viene sino para hurtar, matar y destruir, pero Él vino para que sus ovejas tengan vida y la tengan en abundancia. Los ladrones y salteadores eran los falsos líderes que se erigían en jueces de quién podía llegar a Dios y cerraban a la gente el reino que decían guardar. El ladrón quita a las ovejas para su propio beneficio. El Pastor da, y da una vida que desborda.

en: Jesus says He is the door, not one of many doors, and Ephesians 2:18 says it is through Him that we have access to the Father. The lesson's dream of searching for hours around a house in the freezing cold and finding only one open door pictures this: there is only one way in. Any road that claims to reach God while going around this Door falls short. That is why He called false leaders thieves and robbers, because they offered other ways and actually kept people out.
es: Jesús dice que Él es la puerta, no una de muchas, y Efesios 2:18 dice que por medio de Él tenemos acceso al Padre. El sueño de la lección, de rodear una casa en el frío buscando por horas y hallar solo una puerta abierta, ilustra esto: hay un solo modo de entrar. Todo camino que pretende llegar a Dios rodeando esta Puerta se queda corto. Por eso llamó ladrones y salteadores a los falsos líderes, que ofrecían otros caminos y en realidad dejaban fuera a la gente.

en: In Israel a shepherd stayed with his flock for years and gave each sheep a descriptive name like 'Brown-leg' or 'Black-ear,' calling each by its own name. Jesus says He knows His sheep and is known by them. Throughout Scripture God called people by name, like Abraham, Moses, and Samuel. This means believers are not numbers or faces in a crowd but are personally known by the God who placed the stars.
Like shepherds who named each sheep, Jesus knows each believer personally and calls them by name.
es: En Israel el pastor permanecía con su rebaño por años y daba a cada oveja un nombre descriptivo como 'Pata-parda' u 'Oreja-negra', llamando a cada una por su nombre. Jesús dice que conoce a sus ovejas y que ellas le conocen. A lo largo de la Escritura Dios llamó a personas por nombre, como Abraham, Moisés y Samuel. Esto significa que el creyente no es un número ni un rostro en la multitud, sino alguien conocido personalmente por el Dios que puso las estrellas.

en: Sheep learn their shepherd's voice by living with him day after day, and they will not follow a stranger. A traveler near Bethlehem saw two flocks sheltered in one cave; in the morning one shepherd simply gave his call, and only his sheep came running after him. Jesus says, 'My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me.' Believers learn to recognize God's voice, as the man freed from drink and drugs did when he heard an inner voice tell him to turn from the world and knew it was God.
Through relationship the sheep recognize and follow their own shepherd's voice, not a stranger's, and believers likewise learn to hear and follow Christ.
es: Las ovejas aprenden la voz de su pastor al vivir con él día tras día, y no siguen a un extraño. Un viajero cerca de Belén vio dos rebaños guarecidos en una cueva; en la mañana un pastor solo dio su llamado y únicamente sus ovejas corrieron tras él. Jesús dice: 'Mis ovejas oyen mi voz, y yo las conozco, y me siguen.' Los creyentes aprenden a reconocer la voz de Dios, como el hombre atado a la bebida y las drogas que oyó una voz interior decirle que se apartara del mundo y supo que era Dios.

en: The hireling works only for wages; the sheep are not his, so when he sees the wolf coming he leaves them and runs because he does not care about them. The good shepherd owns the sheep and was born to the task, so he puts himself between them and danger. Some shepherds in the Holy Land actually fought to the death defending their flocks from raiders. Jesus is the good shepherd who gives His life for the sheep.
The hireling flees danger because he works for pay and doesn't care, but the good shepherd protects his own sheep even at the cost of his life.
es: El asalariado trabaja solo por la paga; las ovejas no son suyas, así que cuando ve venir al lobo las deja y huye porque no le importan. El buen pastor es dueño de las ovejas y nació para la tarea, así que se pone entre ellas y el peligro. Algunos pastores en Tierra Santa lucharon literalmente hasta la muerte defendiendo su rebaño. Jesús es el buen pastor que da su vida por las ovejas.

en: The word 'good' here means more than skilled or kind; it means good in the very nature of the thing, beautiful and ideal, the model others can safely follow. That goodness is not something Jesus achieved but what He is, so calling Him good in this full sense amounts to calling Him God. He gives His life for the sheep, and He said no one takes it from Him; He lays it down of Himself. His death was not an accident or a defeat but a deliberate sacrifice that shows how far the Father would go to gather His sheep.
'Good' means intrinsically good and ideal, pointing to His deity, and He voluntarily laid down His life for His sheep on the cross.
es: La palabra 'buen' aquí significa más que hábil o amable; significa bueno en la naturaleza misma, lo hermoso e ideal, el modelo que otros pueden seguir con seguridad. Esa bondad no es algo que Jesús logró sino lo que Él es, de modo que llamarle bueno en ese sentido es llamarle Dios. Da su vida por las ovejas, y dijo que nadie se la quita, sino que Él mismo la pone. Su muerte no fue accidente ni derrota, sino un sacrificio deliberado que muestra cuán lejos llegaría el Padre para reunir a sus ovejas.

en: Jesus gives His sheep eternal life, they will never perish, and no one can snatch them out of His hand. Their security does not depend on their weak grip on Him but on His almighty grip on them. What He bought at so great a price He does not lose. He then said, 'I and My Father are one,' which the leaders understood as a claim to be God, so they picked up stones again.
Believers have eternal life and are held securely by Christ's almighty hand, not their own grip, and no one can snatch them away.
es: Jesús da a sus ovejas vida eterna, no perecerán jamás y nadie las arrebatará de su mano. Su seguridad no depende de su débil agarre de Él, sino de su agarre todopoderoso sobre ellas. Lo que compró a tan alto precio no lo pierde. Luego dijo: 'Yo y mi Padre uno somos', lo cual los líderes entendieron como una afirmación de ser Dios, y tomaron piedras otra vez.

en: Christ does not keep His sheep; they can be snatched from His hand

A trained orator recited Psalm 23 so beautifully that the audience applauded, but when an old man recited the same words, the room fell silent in prayer. The orator admitted that the difference was that he knew the Psalm, but his friend knew the Shepherd. The point is that admiring the Shepherd from outside the fold is not enough. We must enter through the Door and have a personal relationship with Christ, knowing Him and being known by Him.
Knowing about Jesus or His words is not the same as personally knowing Him; we must actually know the Shepherd.
es: Un orador entrenado recitó el Salmo 23 tan bellamente que el público aplaudió, pero cuando un anciano recitó las mismas palabras, la sala quedó en silencio y en oración. El orador confesó que la diferencia era que él sabía el Salmo, pero su amigo conocía al Pastor. La lección es que no basta admirar al Pastor desde fuera del redil. Debemos entrar por la Puerta y tener una relación personal con Cristo, conociéndole y siendo conocidos por Él.

en: The tragedy: Lazarus, a man loved by Jesus and in the prime of life, fell sick and died, and the loss was real for his family. The trial: Jesus deliberately stayed two more days, saying the sickness was for God's glory, so the family and disciples had to trust Him in the dark without understanding. The tears: at Bethany, surrounded by mourning, Jesus wept, entering into the grief of those He loved. The triumph: He declared, 'I am the resurrection and the life,' and called Lazarus out of the tomb after four days, showing His power over death.
Lazarus died (tragedy), Jesus delayed and asked for trust (trial), Jesus wept with the mourners (tears), and He raised Lazarus as the Resurrection and the Life (triumph).
es: La tragedia: Lázaro, amado por Jesús y en la flor de la vida, enfermó y murió, y la pérdida fue real para su familia. La prueba: Jesús se quedó dos días más, diciendo que la enfermedad era para la gloria de Dios, y todos tuvieron que confiar en Él en la oscuridad sin entender. Las lágrimas: en Betania, rodeado de llanto, Jesús lloró, entrando en el dolor de los que amaba. El triunfo: declaró 'Yo soy la resurrección y la vida' y llamó a Lázaro fuera de la tumba después de cuatro días, mostrando su poder sobre la muerte.

en: Cook says death is a tragedy even when we are sure we will see the person again, because the loss is real and the absence hurts. He speaks from experience: he had almost two years to say goodbye to his first wife, and it was still perhaps the hardest thing he ever faced, and he remembers his mother's cry when his baby niece died. Death is a real enemy, and Scripture never asks us to pretend otherwise. Hope in the resurrection does not erase the pain of separation.
Even with hope of reunion, the loss and absence are real and painful; death remains a real enemy that Scripture does not ask us to deny.
es: Cook dice que la muerte es una tragedia aun cuando estamos seguros de volver a ver a la persona, porque la pérdida es real y la ausencia duele. Habla por experiencia: tuvo casi dos años para despedirse de su primera esposa y aun así fue quizá lo más difícil que enfrentó, y recuerda el grito de su madre cuando murió su sobrinita. La muerte es un enemigo real, y la Escritura nunca nos pide fingir lo contrario. La esperanza de la resurrección no borra el dolor de la separación.

en: When Jesus heard Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was two more days instead of hurrying. He said the sickness was not unto death but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God would be glorified through it. Lazarus died within God's permissive will, allowed for a purpose no one could yet see. The delay set the stage for a far greater display of His power, raising a man four days dead, so that God would be glorified and faith strengthened.
He delayed so that Lazarus' death, allowed by God, would become an occasion to display God's glory and the Son's power by raising him.
es: Cuando Jesús supo que Lázaro estaba enfermo, se quedó dos días más en vez de apresurarse. Dijo que la enfermedad no era para muerte sino para la gloria de Dios, para que el Hijo de Dios fuera glorificado por ella. Lázaro murió dentro de la voluntad permisiva de Dios, permitido para un propósito que nadie podía ver todavía. La demora preparó una manifestación mucho mayor de su poder, resucitar a un hombre de cuatro días muerto, para que Dios fuera glorificado y la fe fortalecida.

en: Trials ask us to trust God in the dark before we can see the reason, and it is only when faith is tested that it grows. Paul prayed three times for his thorn to be removed, but God answered, 'My grace is sufficient for you.' William Sangster could not explain to his three-year-old son why he had to have a painful surgery, so he said, 'You must trust my love.' God often leaves us in that place, unable to see why, called simply to trust the love of a Father who will make it plain one day.
Trials test faith and make it grow as we trust God's love without understanding, like Paul with his thorn and Sangster's son before surgery.
es: Las pruebas nos piden confiar en Dios en la oscuridad antes de ver la razón, y solo cuando la fe es probada crece. Pablo oró tres veces para que le quitara el aguijón, pero Dios respondió: 'Bástate mi gracia.' William Sangster no pudo explicar a su hijo de tres años por qué necesitaba una cirugía dolorosa, así que le dijo: 'Debes confiar en mi amor.' Dios a menudo nos deja ahí, sin ver el porqué, llamados a confiar en el amor de un Padre que un día lo aclarará todo.

en: 'Jesus wept' is the shortest verse in the Bible but one of the fullest. Jesus knew He would raise Lazarus within the hour, yet He still wept, not for Lazarus but for the grief of those He loved and for a world under the shadow of death. He did not stand above their sorrow but entered into it. This shows that God is not a stranger to our grief and models Romans 12:15, weeping with those who weep.
Though He was about to raise Lazarus, Jesus shared the mourners' grief, showing that God enters our sorrow and teaching us to weep with those who weep.
es: 'Jesús lloró' es el versículo más corto de la Biblia y uno de los más plenos. Jesús sabía que pronto resucitaría a Lázaro, y aun así lloró, no por Lázaro sino por el dolor de los que amaba y por un mundo bajo la sombra de la muerte. No se quedó por encima de su tristeza, sino que entró en ella. Esto muestra que Dios no es ajeno a nuestro dolor y nos enseña Romanos 12:15: llorar con los que lloran.

en: Martha believed Lazarus would rise at the last day, a distant future hope. Jesus brought the resurrection into the present and into His own Person: 'I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in Me, though he may die, he shall live, and whoever lives and believes in Me shall never die.' Resurrection is not first an event or a doctrine but Christ Himself. To have Him is to have a life that death cannot end, and He asks each of us, 'Do you believe this?'
Resurrection is found in Christ Himself, not only at the last day; whoever believes in Him has a life that death cannot end.
es: Marta creía que Lázaro resucitaría en el día postrero, una esperanza lejana. Jesús trajo la resurrección al presente y a su propia Persona: 'Yo soy la resurrección y la vida; el que cree en mí, aunque esté muerto, vivirá, y todo aquel que vive y cree en mí, no morirá eternamente.' La resurrección no es primero un evento ni una doctrina, sino Cristo mismo. Tenerle a Él es tener una vida que la muerte no puede terminar, y nos pregunta: '¿Crees esto?'

en: After the stone was removed, despite Martha's protest that the body would smell after four days, Jesus cried with a loud voice, 'Lazarus, come forth!' and Lazarus came out still bound in grave clothes. It shows Jesus' absolute authority over death; it has been said that if He had not named Lazarus, every grave might have emptied at His voice. In that moment every doubt was buried. It also foreshadows the day when the same voice will call every believer out of the grave by name.
His command raised a man four days dead, proving His power over death and foreshadowing His calling all believers from the grave.
es: Después de quitar la piedra, a pesar de que Marta protestó que ya hedía, Jesús clamó a gran voz: '¡Lázaro, ven fuera!', y Lázaro salió atado con las vendas. Muestra la autoridad absoluta de Jesús sobre la muerte; se ha dicho que si no lo hubiera llamado por nombre, todas las tumbas se habrían vaciado. En ese momento toda duda quedó sepultada.
