También anticipa el día en que la misma voz llamará por nombre a cada creyente fuera de la tumba.

en: After raising Lazarus, Jesus told the people to unbind him and let him go. Only Christ can give life, but He let the community remove the grave clothes and welcome Lazarus back. The church's part is similar: we help those newly alive in Christ get free of the bindings of their past by teaching, encouraging, and walking with them. Christ gives the life; we help the new believer live it out.
Christ alone gives life, but He calls the church to help new believers get free from old bindings by teaching and encouraging them.
es: Después de resucitar a Lázaro, Jesús dijo a la gente que lo desataran y lo dejaran ir. Solo Cristo puede dar la vida, pero dejó que la comunidad quitara las vendas y recibiera a Lázaro. La parte de la iglesia es semejante: ayudamos a los que acaban de recibir vida en Cristo a librarse de las ataduras del pasado, enseñándoles, animándoles y caminando con ellos. Cristo da la vida; nosotros ayudamos al nuevo creyente a vivirla.

en: Everyone secretly fears death, but this sign shows that Jesus has power over the grave itself, and the One who can conquer death can take away every fear. Jesus pictured death as sleep. Like a tired child who falls asleep on the couch and wakes in his own bed because his father carried him there, the believer falls asleep in death and wakes safe where the Father has carried him. The grave becomes a doorway rather than a wall, as shown by the man buried with his finger on John 3:16.
By showing His power over death, Jesus removes its terror; for believers death is like sleep, from which the Father carries us to wake safely with Him.
es: Todos tememos en secreto la muerte, pero esta señal muestra que Jesús tiene poder sobre la tumba misma, y el que puede vencer la muerte puede quitar todo temor. Jesús comparó la muerte con un sueño. Como un niño cansado que se duerme en el sofá y despierta en su cama porque su padre lo llevó, el creyente se duerme en la muerte y despierta a salvo donde el Padre lo ha llevado. La tumba ya no es un muro sino una puerta, como lo mostró el hombre sepultado con su dedo sobre Juan 3:16.

en: The raising of Lazarus is the greatest sign because it is greater than water into wine, feeding the five thousand, or opening blind eyes: Lazarus had been dead and buried four days, and Jesus showed power over death itself. Death is the deepest question any religion must answer, and here Jesus answers it. When Martha hesitated about opening the tomb, Jesus said, 'Did I not say that if you would believe you would see the glory of God?' This calls us to trust and obey Him even when it seems hopeless, so that we too will see His glory.
It shows Christ's power over death itself after four days in the tomb, and calls us to believe Him even when things look hopeless, so we see God's glory.
es: La resurrección de Lázaro es la mayor señal porque supera al agua en vino, a la alimentación de los cinco mil y a abrir ojos ciegos: Lázaro llevaba cuatro días muerto y sepultado, y Jesús mostró poder sobre la muerte misma. La muerte es la pregunta más profunda que toda religión debe responder, y aquí Jesús la responde. Cuando Marta dudó en abrir la tumba, Jesús dijo: '¿No te he dicho que si crees, verás la gloria de Dios?' Esto nos llama a confiar y obedecerle aun cuando todo parece perdido, para ver su gloria.

en: Throughout John, Jesus' enemies could not seize Him because His hour had not yet come. In John 12 some Greeks who came to worship at the feast asked Philip, 'Sir, we would see Jesus,' and when Jesus heard it He said the hour had come for the Son of Man to be glorified. Their request expresses the deep human longing for a Person, not a doctrine or a debate. The arrival of Gentile seekers signaled that the world was beginning to seek Him, and that the hour of His death and glory had arrived.
When Gentile Greeks came wanting to see Jesus, He announced that His long-awaited hour of glorification had come, as the world began seeking Him.
es: A lo largo de Juan, sus enemigos no podían prenderle porque aún no había llegado su hora. En Juan 12 unos griegos que habían subido a adorar en la fiesta dijeron a Felipe: 'Señor, querríamos ver a Jesús', y cuando Jesús lo supo dijo que había llegado la hora de que el Hijo del Hombre fuera glorificado. Su petición expresa el anhelo humano por una Persona, no por una doctrina o un debate. La llegada de buscadores gentiles señaló que el mundo comenzaba a buscarle y que la hora de su muerte y gloria había llegado.

en: Jesus said that unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it remains alone, but if it dies it produces much grain. A seed kept safe on a shelf stays a single lonely seed; only by being buried and broken does it become a harvest. In the same way, the road to Jesus' glory and to a world full of redeemed people went through His death. The cross was not the failure of His hour but the very means of His glory.
Just as a seed must die to produce a harvest, Jesus' death was the means of His glory and of bringing many to salvation.
es: Jesús dijo que si el grano de trigo no cae en la tierra y muere, queda solo, pero si muere lleva mucho fruto. Una semilla guardada en un estante sigue siendo una semilla solitaria; solo al ser enterrada y partida se convierte en cosecha. Así, el camino a la gloria de Jesús y a un mundo lleno de redimidos pasaba por su muerte. La cruz no fue el fracaso de su hora sino el medio mismo de su gloria.

en: Jesus applied the same principle to His followers: whoever loves his life will lose it, and whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life. A clenched fist keeps nothing, but the open, surrendered hand bears fruit. We naturally want glory without a cross and a crown without surrender, but there is no shortcut around the buried seed. The French Christian widow who took a Jewish woman's papers and died in a camp in her place, saying it was the least she could do since Christ had done more for her, shows a life laid down that bore fruit in someone else.
es: Jesús aplicó el mismo principio a sus seguidores: el que ama su vida la perderá, y el que la aborrece en este mundo la guardará para vida eterna. El puño cerrado no guarda nada; la mano abierta y entregada lleva fruto. Naturalmente queremos gloria sin cruz y corona sin entrega, pero no hay atajo alrededor de la semilla enterrada. La viuda cristiana en Francia que tomó los papeles de una mujer judía y murió en un campo en su lugar, diciendo que era lo menos que podía hacer porque Cristo había hecho más por ella, muestra una vida entregada que dio fruto en otra persona.

en: Jesus admitted His soul was troubled, but instead of asking to be saved from the hour, He prayed, 'Father, glorify Your name.' A voice came from heaven saying, 'I have both glorified it and will glorify it again.' The crowd heard it differently: some said it thundered, others that an angel spoke, showing that hearts hear God according to their openness to Him. The voice revealed that the Father would be glorified in the Son, both through the signs already done and through the coming cross.
The Father answered Jesus' prayer audibly, affirming He had glorified and would again glorify His name through the Son, though the crowd heard it differently.
es: Jesús reconoció que su alma estaba turbada, pero en lugar de pedir ser librado de esa hora, oró: 'Padre, glorifica tu nombre.' Vino una voz del cielo: 'Lo he glorificado, y lo glorificaré otra vez.' La multitud la oyó de distintas maneras: unos decían que había tronado, otros que un ángel le habló, lo cual muestra que cada corazón oye a Dios según su apertura. La voz reveló que el Padre sería glorificado en el Hijo, en las señales ya hechas y en la cruz cercana.

en: Glory is the holiness of God made visible. No one could look at it directly; even Moses saw only its afterglow. But John 1:14 says the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory as of the only begotten of the Father. In Jesus, and most of all in His self-giving death, God's hidden glory comes out into the open where people can see it.
Glory is God's holiness made visible, and Jesus reveals it in His life and especially in His self-giving death.
es: La gloria es la santidad de Dios hecha visible. Nadie podía mirarla directamente; aun Moisés vio solo su resplandor posterior. Pero Juan 1:14 dice que el Verbo fue hecho carne y habitó entre nosotros, y vimos su gloria, como del unigénito del Padre. En Jesús, y sobre todo en su muerte entregada, la gloria escondida de Dios sale a la luz donde los ojos humanos pueden verla.

en: On the night He was betrayed, while the disciples argued about who was the greatest, no servant was there to wash their dusty feet and none of them would do it. Jesus, knowing He had come from God and was going to God, got up from supper, took off His outer garment, tied a towel around Himself, and washed their feet. The Son of God knelt at the dirty feet of fishermen just hours before the cross. This shows that true greatness is humble service, and it is the very glory the Greeks had asked to see.
Jesus took a servant's towel and washed His disciples' dirty feet, showing that true greatness is humble service.
es: La noche en que fue entregado, mientras los discípulos discutían quién era el mayor, no había siervo para lavarles los pies sucios y ninguno quería hacerlo. Jesús, sabiendo que había salido de Dios y a Dios iba, se levantó de la cena, se quitó el manto, se ciñó una toalla y lavó los pies de sus discípulos. El Hijo de Dios se arrodilló ante los pies sucios de unos pescadores a horas del Calvario. Esto muestra que la verdadera grandeza es el servicio humilde, y es la gloria que los griegos pedían ver.

en: The world measures greatness by how many people work for you, but the Lord measures it by how many people you serve. Jesus taught that the greatest among His followers must be their servant. Believers in China told a missionary that what won them to Christ was not miracles or teaching but Jesus washing feet, because they had never known a God who stooped with a towel and basin. So when we are tempted to stand on our dignity or rights, we should remember the Lord of glory on His knees.
The world counts how many serve you; God counts how many you serve, so the greatest is the servant of all.
es: El mundo mide la grandeza por cuántas personas trabajan para ti, pero el Señor la mide por cuántas personas sirves tú. Jesús enseñó que el mayor entre sus seguidores debe ser su siervo. Unos creyentes en China dijeron a un misionero que lo que los ganó a Cristo no fueron los milagros ni la enseñanza, sino Jesús lavando pies, porque nunca habían conocido a un Dios que se agachara con toalla y palangana. Cuando somos tentados a defender nuestra dignidad o derechos, debemos recordar al Señor de la gloria de rodillas.

en: Jesus said that since He, their Lord and Teacher, had washed their feet, they ought to wash one another's feet, because He had given them an example. It is a command to humble, practical service toward others. Today we wash feet when we care for the sick, feed the poor, honor aging parents, drive a neighbor to the doctor, or open our homes. Greatness in the kingdom wears an apron.
Following His example, we must humbly serve one another, such as caring for the sick, feeding the poor, and helping neighbors.
es: Jesús dijo que si Él, el Señor y Maestro, les había lavado los pies, ellos también debían lavarse los pies unos a otros, porque les había dado ejemplo. Es un mandato de servicio humilde y práctico. Hoy lavamos pies cuando cuidamos al enfermo, alimentamos al pobre, honramos a los padres ancianos, llevamos a un vecino al médico o abrimos nuestra casa. La grandeza en el reino lleva delantal.

en: Jesus gave a new commandment: love one another as I have loved you. The standard is His own love, which laid down His life and took up the towel. By this love everyone will know that we are His disciples. The world that wants to see Jesus will see Him most clearly not in our arguments or buildings but in a people who lay down their lives for one another.
We must love one another as Christ loved us, and that love is the sign by which the world recognizes His disciples.
es: Jesús dio un mandamiento nuevo: que os améis unos a otros como yo os he amado. La medida es su propio amor, que entregó su vida y tomó la toalla. En esto conocerán todos que somos sus discípulos, si tenemos amor unos con otros. El mundo que quiere ver a Jesús lo verá con más claridad no en nuestros argumentos ni edificios, sino en un pueblo que entrega su vida unos por otros.

en: In this hour God's glory is shown not by an army or throne but by a grain of wheat that dies, a voice from heaven, and a towel and basin. Jesus is glorified through His death on the cross and through humble service like washing feet. This reverses the world's idea of glory. It calls us first to look to the grain that died for us, and then to take up the towel: surrender our lives, serve others, and love one another as He loved us.
Jesus' glory is revealed in His death and humble service, and it calls us to surrender ourselves, serve others, and love one another.
es: En esta hora la gloria de Dios no se muestra por un ejército ni un trono, sino por un grano de trigo que muere, una voz del cielo, y una toalla y una palangana. Jesús es glorificado por su muerte en la cruz y por el servicio humilde, como lavar pies. Esto invierte la idea del mundo sobre la gloria. Nos llama primero a mirar al grano que murió por nosotros y luego a tomar la toalla: entregar nuestra vida, servir a otros y amarnos como Él nos amó.

en: On the night before the cross the disciples' hearts were breaking, so Jesus told them not to be troubled but to believe in God and in Him. He said that in His Father's house are many dwelling places, that He was going to prepare a place for them, and that He would come again and take them to be with Him. Heaven is a real place, the believer's true home, not wishful thinking. Like the boy in the attic who received his grandfather's letter saying 'Come home,' believers can look forward to the day Christ calls them home.
He promised He was going to prepare a real place for them in the Father's house and would come back to take them to be with Him.
es: La noche antes de la cruz los corazones de los discípulos se rompían, así que Jesús les dijo que no se turbaran, sino que creyeran en Dios y en Él. Dijo que en la casa de su Padre hay muchas moradas, que iba a preparar lugar para ellos y que vendría otra vez para tomarlos consigo. El cielo es un lugar real, el verdadero hogar del creyente, no una ilusión. Como el niño del ático que recibió la carta de su abuelo diciendo 'Vuelve a casa', el creyente espera el día en que Cristo lo llame a casa.

en: When Thomas asked how they could know the way, Jesus did not give him a map but a Person: 'I am the way.' The opposite of the way is being lost, and not every road reaches God no matter how sincerely it is traveled. Jesus taught that there are only two roads, the broad one leading to destruction and the narrow one that few find. He said no one comes to the Father except through Him, so every road that tries to go around Him falls short.
Jesus Himself is the way to God, and no one reaches the Father except through Him; sincerity on another road is not enough.
es: Cuando Tomás preguntó cómo podían saber el camino, Jesús no le dio un mapa sino una Persona: 'Yo soy el camino.' Lo opuesto del camino es estar perdido, y no todo camino llega a Dios por sincero que sea quien lo recorre. Jesús enseñó que hay solo dos caminos: el ancho que lleva a la destrucción y el angosto que pocos hallan. Dijo que nadie viene al Padre sino por Él, así que todo camino que intenta rodearlo se queda corto.

en: Jesus is not merely a teacher of true things; He is the Truth in person, so to know Him is to know what is real. He is also the Life. A person without Him is not just uninformed or unlucky but spiritually dead, alive to the world yet dead to God. Only Christ can make such a person truly alive, giving abundant life now and eternal life forever. Josh McDowell's story shows the point: the answer was not religion but Jesus Christ Himself.
Jesus is truth in person, so knowing Him is knowing reality, and He is the life who makes spiritually dead people alive now and forever.
es: Jesús no es meramente un maestro de cosas verdaderas; es la Verdad en persona, de modo que conocerle es conocer lo real. También es la Vida. La persona sin Él no es solo ignorante o desafortunada, sino que está espiritualmente muerta, viva al mundo pero muerta para Dios. Solo Cristo puede darle vida verdadera, abundante ahora y eterna para siempre. La historia de Josh McDowell lo muestra: la respuesta no era la religión sino Jesucristo mismo.

en: This is the last of the seven I AM sayings. Even the Great Vine near London, centuries old with huge branches and many grapes, is only a picture; Jesus is the true vine, the real source of spiritual life. The Father is the vinedresser, who is much more than a farmer. He knows each vine intimately, what it needs and when, and exactly where and at what angle to cut, so that it bears fruit.
Jesus is the real source of life for believers, and the Father is the caring gardener who tends and prunes the branches.
es: Esta es la última de las siete declaraciones 'YO SOY'. Aun la Gran Vid cerca de Londres, de siglos de edad y con ramas enormes, es solo una imagen; Jesús es la vid verdadera, la fuente real de la vida espiritual. El Padre es el labrador, mucho más que un granjero. Conoce cada vid íntimamente, sabe qué necesita y cuándo, y exactamente dónde y en qué ángulo cortar para que lleve fruto.

en: Every branch that bears fruit the Father prunes so that it will bear more fruit. Pruning is not punishment but love with a knife. Sometimes He cuts away what is clearly dead, but often He cuts away even good and better things so we can have the best. It hurts but it helps, as with Paul's thorn, which God did not remove but used, saying, 'My grace is sufficient for you,' to make him more fruitful.
The Father lovingly cuts away even good things from fruitful branches so they will bear more fruit; pruning hurts but helps.
es: Todo pámpano que lleva fruto, el Padre lo limpia para que lleve más fruto. La poda no es castigo, sino amor con un cuchillo. A veces corta lo que está claramente muerto, pero a menudo corta aun lo bueno y lo mejor para que tengamos lo mejor de todo. Duele pero ayuda, como el aguijón de Pablo, que Dios no quitó sino usó, diciendo 'Bástate mi gracia', para hacerlo más fructífero.

en: 'Abide' is the verb behind the word 'abode,' a dwelling place. To abide in Christ is more than knowing facts about Him or even praying; it is living with Him in a close, family relationship, aware of Him beside us every moment. Like a phone that must stay plugged in to charge, we receive life and power only while we stay connected to the Vine. The Polish believers who stayed on their knees after Stuart Briscoe's sermon show the seriousness of making sure we are abiding.
To abide is to make our home in Christ, living in constant close fellowship with Him so His life keeps flowing into us.
es: 'Permanecer' es el verbo detrás de 'morada', un lugar donde se habita. Permanecer en Cristo es más que saber datos de Él o incluso orar; es vivir con Él en una relación estrecha, de familia, conscientes de su presencia cada momento. Como un teléfono que debe seguir conectado para cargarse, recibimos vida y poder solo mientras permanecemos conectados a la Vid. Los creyentes polacos que siguieron de rodillas tras el sermón de Stuart Briscoe muestran la seriedad de asegurarnos de permanecer en Él.

en: Jesus said He is the vine and we are the branches, and without Him we can do nothing. A branch cut off from the vine cannot produce anything by itself. Apart from Christ we can do nothing of eternal value, no matter how busy we are. But when we abide in Him, His life flows through us and fruit comes.
Cut off from Christ we can produce nothing of eternal worth; all real fruit comes from His life flowing through us.
es: Jesús dijo que Él es la vid y nosotros los pámpanos, y que sin Él nada podemos hacer. Una rama separada de la vid no puede producir nada por sí misma. Aparte de Cristo no podemos hacer nada de valor eterno, por muy ocupados que estemos. Pero cuando permanecemos en Él, su vida fluye a través de nosotros y el fruto viene.

en: Many assume a real Christian will produce fruit automatically, but Jesus says fruit comes only by abiding in Him. Abiding itself is not automatic either, or He would not have needed to command it; that same night all the disciples, especially Peter, failed to abide. Fruit comes as we stay connected to the Vine and His life flows through us. When there is no fruit, it is an attachment problem, and the cure is not to quit but to clear away sin and abide afresh.
es: Muchos suponen que un verdadero cristiano llevará fruto automáticamente, pero Jesús dice que el fruto viene solo al permanecer en Él. Y permanecer tampoco es automático, o no habría tenido que mandarlo; esa misma noche todos los discípulos, sobre todo Pedro, fallaron. El fruto viene cuando seguimos conectados a la Vid y su vida fluye por nosotros. Cuando no hay fruto, es un problema de conexión, y el remedio no es rendirse sino quitar el pecado y permanecer de nuevo.

en: Fruit includes evangelism and winning souls, but it is more than that. Believers bear fruit by using the gifts God has given them, such as teaching, hospitality, mercy, and prayer. Above all they bear the fruit of the Spirit from Galatians 5: love, joy, peace, and the rest. When the world sees people marked by this fruit, it sees something it cannot explain or produce, and all of it is for the Father's glory.
Fruit includes winning souls, using spiritual gifts like teaching and mercy, and especially the fruit of the Spirit such as love, joy, and peace.
es: El fruto incluye la evangelización y ganar almas, pero es más que eso. Los creyentes llevan fruto al usar los dones que Dios les ha dado, como enseñar, hospedar, tener misericordia y orar. Sobre todo llevan el fruto del Espíritu de Gálatas 5: amor, gozo, paz y los demás. Cuando el mundo ve a un pueblo marcado por este fruto, ve algo que no puede explicar ni producir, y todo es para la gloria del Padre.

en: The two sayings answer the soul's two deepest questions. 'I am the way' tells us how to get home to the Father: only through Christ. 'I am the true vine' tells us how to live until we get there: by abiding in Him so His life makes us fruitful. They call us first to come to the Father through the one Way, and then to stay close to the Vine and let His life bear fruit through us for the Father's glory.
The Way brings us to the Father and the Vine keeps us alive and fruitful on the journey, so we must come through Christ and then abide in Him.
es: Las dos declaraciones responden las dos preguntas más hondas del alma. 'Yo soy el camino' nos dice cómo llegar a casa, al Padre: solo por Cristo. 'Yo soy la vid verdadera' nos dice cómo vivir hasta llegar: permaneciendo en Él para que su vida nos haga fructíferos. Nos llaman primero a venir al Padre por el único Camino, y luego a permanecer cerca de la Vid y dejar que su vida lleve fruto en nosotros para la gloria del Padre.

en: The disciples saw His leaving as pure loss, but Jesus said that unless He went away the Helper would not come, and if He went He would send Him. While on earth Jesus could be in only one place at a time, but through the Spirit He would be with every believer everywhere, always. So their grief had a purpose they could not yet see. Like a woman in labor, their sorrow would turn to joy.
If He left, He would send the Spirit, who would be with every believer everywhere at all times, not limited to one place as Jesus was in the flesh.
es: Los discípulos veían su partida como pura pérdida, pero Jesús dijo que si no se iba, el Consolador no vendría, y que si se iba, lo enviaría. En la tierra Jesús solo podía estar en un lugar a la vez, pero por el Espíritu estaría con cada creyente en todas partes y siempre. Así que su tristeza tenía un propósito que aún no veían. Como la mujer de parto, su dolor se convertiría en gozo.

en: Jesus calls the Spirit the Paraclete, which means Helper, Comforter, Advocate, literally 'one called alongside' to stand with us. He is 'another' Helper of the same kind as Jesus, God come close, and He is given not for a visit but to abide forever, dwelling with and in believers. He is the Spirit of truth, who teaches us all things and brings to remembrance what Jesus said. He is a divine Person, not a force or a feeling, who knows us, loves us, and never leaves.
The Paraclete is one called alongside to help, comfort, and advocate; He lives in believers forever and teaches them, reminding them of Jesus' words.
es: Jesús llama al Espíritu el Paracleto, que significa Consolador, Ayudador, Abogado, literalmente 'uno llamado al lado' para estar con nosotros. Es 'otro' Consolador de la misma clase que Jesús, Dios cercano, y es dado no para una visita sino para siempre, morando con y en los creyentes. Es el Espíritu de verdad que nos enseña todas las cosas y nos recuerda lo que Jesús dijo. Es una Persona divina, no una fuerza ni un sentimiento, que nos conoce, nos ama y nunca nos deja.

en: Jesus said the Spirit of truth would testify of Him, and He has never stopped doing so, through the Scriptures He inspired and in believers' hearts. The Spirit also convicts the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment, awakening consciences that are dead to God. He empowers ordinary believers to bear bold witness even when the world hates them as it hated Jesus. That is why the church has often grown fastest where it has suffered most.
The Spirit bears witness to Jesus and convicts the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment, awakening dead consciences and empowering believers to testify.
es: Jesús dijo que el Espíritu de verdad daría testimonio de Él, y nunca ha dejado de hacerlo, en las Escrituras que inspiró y en el corazón de los creyentes. El Espíritu también convence al mundo de pecado, de justicia y de juicio, despertando conciencias muertas para Dios. Da poder a creyentes comunes para testificar con denuedo aun cuando el mundo los odia como odió a Jesús. Por eso la iglesia a menudo ha crecido más donde más ha sufrido.

en: Jesus said the Spirit would guide His people into all truth and would glorify Him. The Spirit does not advertise Himself; His work is to point to Christ. This is the key to recognizing the Spirit's true work. A life truly filled with the Spirit will not draw attention to itself or to spectacular signs but will point others to Jesus.
es: Jesús dijo que el Espíritu guiaría a los suyos a toda la verdad y que lo glorificaría a Él. El Espíritu no se anuncia a sí mismo; su obra es señalar a Cristo. Esta es la clave para reconocer la verdadera obra del Espíritu. Una vida de veras llena del Espíritu no llamará la atención sobre sí misma ni sobre señales espectaculares, sino que señalará a Jesús.

en: Jesus told the disciples they would weep and mourn while the world rejoiced, but their grief would turn to joy. He compared it to a woman in labor whose pain is real but turns to joy when the child is born. The joy He promised is one no one can take away. This reflects the pattern of faith: we are often asked to trust the Father in the dark before the reason is shown, as Dr. Cook learned in his own losses and in following God to a small, poor church that turned out to be the right path.
Like a mother's labor pains turning to joy at birth, their grief would give way to a joy no one could take from them.
es: Jesús dijo a los discípulos que llorarían y lamentarían mientras el mundo se alegraba, pero que su tristeza se convertiría en gozo. Lo comparó con una mujer de parto, cuyo dolor es real pero se vuelve gozo cuando nace el niño. El gozo que prometió es uno que nadie puede quitar. Esto refleja el patrón de la fe: a menudo debemos confiar en el Padre en la oscuridad antes de ver la razón, como aprendió el Dr. Cook en sus pérdidas y al seguir a Dios a una iglesia pequeña y pobre que resultó ser el camino correcto.

en: We often want God to lay out His whole plan at once, like a machine giving an instant answer, but He rarely works that way. Jesus told the disciples He had many things to say that they could not bear yet, so He gave them light for the next step. God is not training slaves who follow blind orders but sons and daughters who grow into the mind of Christ. The process of seeking His will over time shapes us, as God works in us to will and to do for His good pleasure.
God reveals only what we can bear for the next step, because seeking Him over time forms us as His children rather than blind servants.
es: A menudo queremos que Dios despliegue todo su plan de una vez, como una máquina que da una respuesta instantánea, pero rara vez obra así. Jesús dijo a los discípulos que tenía muchas cosas que decirles que aún no podían sobrellevar, así que les dio luz para el siguiente paso. Dios no forma esclavos que obedecen órdenes ciegas, sino hijos e hijas que crecen hacia la mente de Cristo. El proceso de buscar su voluntad con el tiempo nos forma, pues Dios produce en nosotros el querer y el hacer.

en: In John 17, on the eve of His sacrifice, Jesus lifts His eyes to heaven and intercedes for His people, which is the work of a high priest. He prays first for Himself, that the Father would glorify the Son so the Son may glorify Him. Then He prays for His disciples, asking the Father to keep them from the evil one and sanctify them. Finally He prays for all future believers. He still intercedes for us before the Father's throne.
Before His sacrifice Jesus intercedes for Himself, His disciples, and all future believers, acting as our High Priest who still prays for us.
es: En Juan 17, en vísperas de su sacrificio, Jesús alza los ojos al cielo e intercede por su pueblo, que es la obra de un sumo sacerdote. Primero ora por sí mismo, para que el Padre glorifique al Hijo y el Hijo glorifique al Padre. Luego ora por sus discípulos, pidiendo que el Padre los guarde del maligno y los santifique. Finalmente ora por todos los que creerían. Aún hoy intercede por nosotros ante el trono del Padre.

en: Jesus defined eternal life as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom He sent. Eternal life is not first a place or a long span of days but a relationship of knowing God. For His disciples He did not ask that they be taken out of the world but kept from the evil one. He prayed, 'Sanctify them by Your truth; Your word is truth,' meaning they would be set apart and made holy through God's word.
Eternal life is knowing God and Jesus Christ, and Jesus asked the Father to sanctify the disciples through His word, which is truth.
es: Jesús definió la vida eterna como conocer al único Dios verdadero y a Jesucristo, a quien Él envió. La vida eterna no es primero un lugar ni una larga cantidad de días, sino una relación de conocer a Dios. Por sus discípulos no pidió que fueran quitados del mundo, sino guardados del maligno. Oró: 'Santifícalos en tu verdad; tu palabra es verdad', es decir, que fueran apartados y hechos santos por la palabra de Dios.

en: Jesus said He was praying not only for the eleven but for all who would believe in Him through their word, so every believer since was included in that prayer. He asked that they all be one, just as the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father. This unity is not forced uniformity or a mere organization but a shared life that reflects the oneness of the Father and Son. Its purpose is evangelistic: so that the world may believe the Father sent Him.
Jesus prayed for all future believers, asking that they be one as the Father and Son are one, so the world would believe.
es: Jesús dijo que no rogaba solo por los once sino por todos los que creerían en Él por la palabra de ellos, de modo que todo creyente desde entonces fue incluido en esa oración. Pidió que todos fueran uno, como el Padre está en el Hijo y el Hijo en el Padre. Esta unidad no es uniformidad forzada ni mera organización, sino una vida compartida que refleja la unidad del Padre y el Hijo. Su propósito es evangelístico: para que el mundo crea que el Padre lo envió.

en: Jesus promised, 'I will not leave you orphans,' and gave two gifts to prove it. The first is the Spirit, the Helper, God with us and in us, who teaches, convicts, comforts, and glorifies Christ through us. The second is His High-Priestly Prayer, in which He holds His people before the Father and continues to intercede for us. Together they mean that no matter our confusion, sorrow, or the world's hostility, we are not alone and not forgotten.
The Spirit lives within us and Jesus intercedes for us before the Father, so believers are never alone or forgotten.
es: Jesús prometió: 'No os dejaré huérfanos', y dio dos regalos para probarlo. El primero es el Espíritu, el Consolador, Dios con nosotros y en nosotros, que enseña, convence, consuela y glorifica a Cristo a través de nosotros. El segundo es su Oración Sumosacerdotal, en la que presenta a su pueblo ante el Padre y sigue intercediendo por nosotros. Juntos significan que, sea cual sea nuestra confusión, tristeza o la hostilidad del mundo, no estamos solos ni olvidados.

en: After the supper Jesus went to Gethsemane, prayed in agony, and yielded to the Father's will. Judas, one of His own, led soldiers with torches and weapons to arrest Him, a deep betrayal by a trusted friend. But when they said they were looking for Jesus of Nazareth, He answered, 'I am He,' and they drew back and fell to the ground. When Peter drew a sword, Jesus told him to put it away, asking, 'Shall I not drink the cup which My Father has given Me?' He went to the cross by His own choice, not because He was overpowered.
Betrayed by Judas, Jesus showed His power when soldiers fell at His 'I am He,' and He stopped Peter's sword, choosing to drink the Father's cup willingly.
es: Después de la cena Jesús fue a Getsemaní, oró en agonía y se entregó a la voluntad del Padre. Judas, uno de los suyos, guió a soldados con antorchas y armas para arrestarlo, una traición profunda de un amigo de confianza. Pero cuando dijeron que buscaban a Jesús de Nazaret, Él respondió 'Yo soy', y retrocedieron y cayeron a tierra. Cuando Pedro sacó la espada, Jesús le dijo que la guardara: '¿La copa que el Padre me ha dado, no la he de beber?' Fue a la cruz por su propia decisión, no porque lo vencieran.

en: The soldiers mocked the idea that this beaten man could be a king by giving Him cruel versions of royal symbols: a crown of thorns, a faded purple robe thrown over His flogged back, and a reed for a scepter. Pilate then brought Him out and said, 'Behold the Man!' What looked like the humiliation of a criminal, John wants us to see as a coronation. The mockery unknowingly told the truth that Jesus is the King.
The soldiers mocked Him with a thorn crown, purple robe, and reed, and Pilate presented Him saying 'Behold the Man,' yet John shows it as a true King's coronation.
es: Los soldados se burlaron de la idea de que este hombre golpeado fuera rey dándole versiones crueles de las insignias reales: una corona de espinas, un manto púrpura descolorido sobre su espalda azotada y una caña como cetro. Luego Pilato lo sacó y dijo: '¡He aquí el hombre!' Lo que parecía la humillación de un criminal, Juan quiere que lo veamos como una coronación. La burla, sin saberlo, decía la verdad: Jesús es el Rey.

en: When Pilate asked, 'Shall I crucify your King?', the chief priests answered, 'We have no king but Caesar,' and Jesus was led to Golgotha. Pilate fastened a sign over the cross in three languages, 'Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews,' and refused to change it: 'What I have written, I have written.' The deepest irony became the deepest truth: the cross was His throne. By not saving Himself, as the mockers demanded, He saves us, reigning from the cross for sinners like Rembrandt, who painted himself among the crucifiers.
Though meant as mockery, Pilate's sign 'King of the Jews' told the truth: Jesus reigned from the cross, saving others by not saving Himself.
es: Cuando Pilato preguntó: '¿A vuestro Rey he de crucificar?', los principales sacerdotes respondieron: 'No tenemos más rey que César', y Jesús fue llevado al Gólgota. Pilato puso sobre la cruz un letrero en tres lenguas, 'Jesús Nazareno, Rey de los Judíos', y se negó a cambiarlo: 'Lo que he escrito, he escrito.' La ironía más honda se volvió la verdad más honda: la cruz era su trono. Al no salvarse a sí mismo, como exigían los burladores, nos salva, reinando desde la cruz por pecadores como Rembrandt, que se pintó entre los que crucificaban.

en: 'It is finished' was not the gasp of a defeated man saying 'I am finished,' but the shout of a victor. The word, tetelestai, was what a merchant stamped on a settled bill: Paid in Full. It means the entire work of redemption Jesus came to do was complete, with nothing to add and nothing still owed. From that finished work flows every forgiveness we will ever receive, sufficient even for someone like R. A. Torrey in his darkest hour.
Tetelestai means 'paid in full': Jesus completed the work of redemption, so nothing remains to be added or owed for our sins.
es: 'Consumado es' no fue el jadeo de un hombre vencido que dice 'estoy acabado', sino el grito de un vencedor. La palabra, tetelestai, era lo que un comerciante estampaba en una cuenta saldada: Pagado por completo. Significa que toda la obra de redención que Jesús vino a hacer estaba completa, sin nada que añadir ni nada pendiente. De esa obra consumada fluye cada perdón que recibiremos, suficiente aun para alguien como R. A. Torrey en su hora más oscura.

en: John says Jesus bowed His head and gave up His spirit, which shows that no one took His life from Him. As the Good Shepherd had said, He laid it down of Himself. His death was not something done to Him against His will but a deliberate, voluntary act. This matches His willingness in the garden, where He chose to drink the Father's cup.
It shows Jesus died voluntarily; no one took His life, but He laid it down Himself, as the Good Shepherd promised.
es: Juan dice que Jesús inclinó la cabeza y entregó el espíritu, lo que muestra que nadie le quitó la vida. Como el Buen Pastor había dicho, la puso de sí mismo. Su muerte no fue algo que le hicieron contra su voluntad, sino un acto deliberado y voluntario. Esto concuerda con su disposición en el huerto, donde escogió beber la copa del Padre.

en: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and found the stone rolled away. Weeping and thinking the body had been stolen, she did not recognize the risen Lord standing before her until He spoke her name, 'Mary.' She was a woman whose life He had rescued, and she became the first witness of the resurrection. Jesus sent her to carry the news to the apostles themselves.
Mary found the empty tomb, recognized the risen Jesus when He said her name, and was sent as the first witness to tell the apostles.
es: Temprano el primer día de la semana, siendo aún oscuro, María Magdalena vino a la tumba y halló la piedra quitada. Llorando y pensando que habían robado el cuerpo, no reconoció al Señor resucitado que estaba ante ella hasta que Él dijo su nombre: 'María.' Era una mujer cuya vida Él había rescatado, y llegó a ser la primera testigo de la resurrección. Jesús la envió a llevar la noticia a los apóstoles mismos.

en: Thomas refused to believe the other disciples, saying that unless he saw the nail marks he would not believe. Eight days later the risen Christ appeared among them and offered Thomas His wounded hands. Thomas fell before Him and confessed, 'My Lord and my God!', the great confession of the whole Gospel. Jesus answered that Thomas believed because he saw, but blessed are those who have not seen and yet believe, a blessing that reaches us today.
Thomas doubted until he saw the risen Jesus' wounds, then confessed 'My Lord and my God!'; Jesus blessed those who believe without seeing.
es: Tomás se negó a creer a los demás discípulos, diciendo que si no veía las marcas de los clavos no creería. Ocho días después el Cristo resucitado apareció entre ellos y ofreció a Tomás sus manos heridas. Tomás cayó ante Él y confesó: '¡Señor mío, y Dios mío!', la gran confesión de todo el Evangelio. Jesús respondió que Tomás creyó porque vio, pero bienaventurados los que no vieron y creyeron, una bendición que nos alcanza hoy.

en: Peter had denied Jesus three times beside a fire, and by the Sea of Galilee he met Him again beside another fire. Three times Jesus asked, 'Do you love Me?', and three times Peter, grieved and humbled, said yes. Each time Jesus gave back his calling: 'Feed My sheep.' The public failure was answered by a public restoration, showing that the risen Lord restores those who fail Him and makes them pillars of His church.
Matching Peter's three denials, Jesus asked three times 'Do you love Me?' and recommissioned him to 'feed My sheep.'
es: Pedro había negado a Jesús tres veces junto a un fuego, y junto al mar de Galilea lo encontró de nuevo junto a otro fuego. Tres veces Jesús preguntó: '¿Me amas?', y tres veces Pedro, dolido y humillado, respondió que sí. Cada vez Jesús le devolvió su llamado: 'Apacienta mis ovejas.' El fracaso público fue respondido con una restauración pública, mostrando que el Señor resucitado restaura a los que le fallan y los hace columnas de su iglesia.

en: The resurrection shows that in Christ failure is not fatal, life is not futile, and death is not final. Peter's restoration and the story of George Smith, a Moravian missionary who won only one woman, was expelled, and died praying, yet whose ministry led to over thirteen thousand believers a century later, show that God redeems apparent failure. The empty tomb, Jesus' many appearances including to more than five hundred, and the disciples' willingness to die for what they saw answer Job's question 'If a man dies, shall he live again?' with a resounding yes.
Because Christ rose, failure is not fatal, life is not futile, and death is not final; believers will live again.
es: La resurrección muestra que en Cristo el fracaso no es fatal, la vida no es vana y la muerte no es final. La restauración de Pedro y la historia de George Smith, misionero moravo que ganó a una sola mujer, fue expulsado y murió orando, pero cuyo ministerio produjo más de trece mil creyentes un siglo después, muestran que Dios redime el aparente fracaso. La tumba vacía, las apariciones de Jesús, incluso a más de quinientos, y la disposición de los discípulos a morir por lo que vieron responden la pregunta de Job, '¿Si el hombre muere, volverá a vivir?', con un rotundo sí.

en: John 20:31 says these things were written so that we may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing we may have life in His name. The whole Gospel has worked like a courtroom, calling witness after witness: John the Baptist, the signs, the Father, the Scriptures, the Spirit, and the empty tomb. Having shown the King crowned, crucified, finished, and risen, John places the verdict in each reader's hands. To all who receive Him and believe, He gives the right to become children of God and eternal life.
John wrote so we would believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life; having presented all the evidence, he asks each reader for a verdict of faith.
es: Juan 20:31 dice que estas cosas se escribieron para que creamos que Jesús es el Cristo, el Hijo de Dios, y para que creyendo tengamos vida en su nombre. Todo el Evangelio ha funcionado como un tribunal, llamando testigo tras testigo: Juan el Bautista, las señales, el Padre, las Escrituras, el Espíritu y la tumba vacía. Después de mostrar al Rey coronado, crucificado, consumado y resucitado, Juan pone el veredicto en manos de cada lector. A todos los que le reciben y creen, les da potestad de ser hijos de Dios y vida eterna.

en: Matthew starts with a genealogy because he wants to settle who Jesus is before telling anything He did; the list shows that God had been working toward this child for two thousand years, arranged in three sets of fourteen generations. Calling Him Son of David means He is the rightful heir to David's throne, the promised King whose kingdom will never end. Calling Him Son of Abraham means He is the one through whom God's promise to bless all the families of the earth comes true, so His blessing reaches the Gentile nations and not only Israel.
The genealogy lays a foundation for Jesus' identity by showing God's long plan; 'Son of David' marks Him as the rightful King, and 'Son of Abraham' as the one through whom all nations are blessed.
es: Mateo comienza con una genealogía porque quiere establecer primero quién es Jesús; la lista, ordenada en tres grupos de catorce, muestra que Dios estuvo obrando hacia este niño durante dos mil años. Llamarlo hijo de David significa que es el Rey legítimo, el heredero del trono de David cuyo reino no tendrá fin. Llamarlo hijo de Abraham significa que en Él se cumple la promesa de que todas las familias de la tierra serían bendecidas, de modo que la bendición alcanza también a los gentiles.

en: Matthew names four women, which was unusual since Jewish genealogies normally traced only fathers, and he skips the great matriarchs. He names Tamar, who deceived Judah; Rahab, the Gentile harlot of Jericho; Ruth, a Moabite from a people with a troubled history with Israel; and Bathsheba, 'the wife of Uriah,' which recalls David's sin. Their presence shows that grace runs through the Messiah's family line: the Savior was not ashamed to be born among sinners and outsiders. No one's past puts them beyond the reach of His family.
Tamar, Rahab, Ruth and Bathsheba, outsiders or women linked to scandal, show that the King came through a line of sinners and foreigners, so grace has room for anyone.
es: Mateo nombra a cuatro mujeres, algo raro porque las genealogías judías trazaban solo a los padres, y no menciona a las grandes matriarcas. Nombra a Tamar, que engañó a Judá; a Rahab, la ramera gentil de Jericó; a Rut, la moabita de un pueblo con historia tensa con Israel; y a Betsabé, 'la mujer de Urías', que recuerda el pecado de David. Su inclusión enseña que la gracia corre por la línea del Mesías: el Salvador no se avergonzó de nacer entre pecadores y extranjeros, y hay lugar en su familia para el que ha fallado.

en: The name Jesus means 'the LORD saves,' and the angel explains that He will save His people from their sins, which tells us His mission: not only to teach or be admired, but to rescue from the deepest bondage, sin. Immanuel, from Isaiah 7:14, means 'God with us,' and it declares His identity as God Himself come to dwell among His people. Together the names say who He is and what He came to do: God in the flesh who has come near in order to save.
'Jesus' means 'the LORD saves,' pointing to His mission of saving people from sin; 'Immanuel' means 'God with us,' declaring His deity.
es: El nombre Jesús significa 'el SEÑOR salva', y el ángel explica que Él salvará a su pueblo de sus pecados; así se revela su misión, no solo enseñar sino librar de la esclavitud del pecado. Emanuel, tomado de Isaías 7:14, significa 'Dios con nosotros' y afirma su deidad: el Creador ha entrado en su propia creación. Juntos, los nombres dicen quién es Él y para qué vino: Dios cercano a nosotros que viene a salvar.

en: Isaiah 7:14 was first spoken to King Ahaz, who was threatened by an enemy alliance and was tempted to rely on Assyria instead of the LORD; when he hypocritically refused to ask for a sign, God gave one anyway. That sign had a real fulfillment in Ahaz's own day, probably in the birth of a child whose growth marked God's deliverance, since a sign seven hundred years off would have meant little to him. Yet the words reached further to their full fulfillment in Jesus, conceived by the Holy Spirit of a virgin, who alone is truly Immanuel, God with us. This is the typological, double-fulfillment reading many evangelicals hold.
The sign was fulfilled first in Ahaz's day by a child marking God's deliverance, and fully in Jesus, born of a virgin by the Spirit, the true Immanuel.
es: Isaías 7:14 fue dado primero al rey Acaz, amenazado por una alianza de enemigos y tentado a confiar en Asiria en lugar del SEÑOR; aunque se negó hipócritamente a pedir una señal, Dios se la dio. Hubo un cumplimiento en su propio día, probablemente el nacimiento de un niño cuyo crecimiento marcó la liberación de Dios. Pero las palabras alcanzan su cumplimiento pleno en Jesús, concebido por el Espíritu Santo en una virgen, el único verdadero Emanuel, Dios con nosotros. Es la lectura tipológica del doble cumplimiento.

en: Hosea 11:1 originally looked back to the Exodus, when God called the nation of Israel, His son, out of Egypt. Matthew sees it fulfilled again when the child Jesus returns from Egypt after Herod's death, because Jesus is the true Son who retraces Israel's path. This is recapitulation: Jesus relives Israel's story and gets it right. Israel wandered and failed in the wilderness for forty years, but Jesus in His forty days of temptation resisted the tempter exactly where the nation had fallen.
Hosea 11:1 refers to Israel's Exodus and is fulfilled again in Jesus coming out of Egypt; as the true Israel, He succeeds in His 40 days of temptation where Israel failed in its 40 years.
es: Oseas 11:1 miraba atrás al Éxodo, cuando Dios sacó a Israel, su hijo, de Egipto. Mateo lo ve cumplido de nuevo cuando el niño Jesús es sacado de Egipto tras la muerte de Herodes, porque Él es el verdadero Hijo que recorre otra vez el camino de Israel. Esto es la recapitulación: Jesús revive la historia de Israel y la hace bien. Israel vagó cuarenta años en el desierto y falló, pero Jesús, en sus cuarenta días de tentación, resistió al tentador justo donde la nación cayó.

en: The Magi were wise men from the East, Gentile foreigners, who followed a star to Bethlehem seeking the one born King of the Jews so they could worship Him. Their visit shows that Jesus is the Son of Abraham through whom the nations are blessed, since outsiders are the first to seek Him while Jerusalem stays indifferent. It also shows He is a King worthy of worship, as their gifts declare. Already at His birth the nations are being drawn to Him.
They were Gentile wise men from the East who came to worship Him, revealing that Jesus is the King whose blessing reaches the nations.
es: Los magos eran sabios del oriente, extranjeros gentiles, que siguieron una estrella buscando al rey de los judíos que había nacido para adorarle. Su visita muestra que Jesús es el hijo de Abraham en quien las naciones son bendecidas, pues los de afuera son los primeros en buscarle mientras Jerusalén permanece indiferente. También revela que es un Rey digno de adoración, como lo anuncian sus regalos.

en: Matthew puts two kings next to each other. Jesus is the King who comes to save His people, while Herod is the king who, troubled by the news, guards his throne at any cost. Herod tries to use the Magi as informants and, when outwitted, orders the slaughter of Bethlehem's baby boys, fulfilling Jeremiah's words about Rachel weeping. The contrast shows that from the start the true King's coming is met by the violence of a world that loves its own power.
Jesus is the King who comes to save, while Herod is a king who kills Bethlehem's children to protect his own power.
es: Mateo pone a dos reyes lado a lado. Jesús es el Rey que viene a salvar a su pueblo; Herodes es el rey que, turbado por la noticia, protege su trono a cualquier precio. Intenta usar a los magos como informantes y, al ser burlado, ordena matar a los niños varones de Belén, cumpliendo las palabras de Jeremías sobre Raquel que llora. El contraste muestra que desde el principio la venida del verdadero Rey choca con la violencia de un mundo que ama su propio poder.

en: The Magi brought gold, frankincense and myrrh, and the lesson says each gift preaches a small sermon. Gold is tribute fit for a king, honoring Jesus as King. Frankincense is incense used in worship offered to God, pointing to His deity. Myrrh was a spice used to anoint the dead, foreshadowing His death on the cross even at the cradle.
Gold honors Him as King, frankincense as God to be worshiped, and myrrh, used for burial, foreshadows His death.
es: Los magos trajeron oro, incienso y mirra, y la lección dice que cada regalo predica un pequeño sermón. El oro es el tributo digno de un rey y honra a Jesús como Rey. El incienso es la adoración ofrecida a Dios y apunta a su deidad. La mirra era una especia para ungir a los muertos, una sombra de la cruz ya desde la cuna.

en: Matthew repeatedly says events happened so that Scripture might be fulfilled: the virgin birth fulfills Isaiah 7:14, the birth in Bethlehem and flight to Egypt fulfill the prophets and Hosea 11:1, the slaughter of the children echoes Jeremiah, and the move to Nazareth fulfills 'He shall be called a Nazarene.' Each fulfillment ties Jesus' early life to the Old Testament story. Together they form one message: the long history from Abraham through David has reached its goal in this child, the promised Messiah and true Israel.
Each event in chapters 1-2 fulfills an Old Testament prophecy, so together they show Jesus is the promised Messiah in whom Israel's story reaches its goal.
es: Mateo repite que los hechos sucedieron para que se cumpliese la Escritura: el nacimiento virginal cumple Isaías 7:14, la huida a Egipto cumple Oseas 11:1, la matanza de los niños recuerda a Jeremías y la vida en Nazaret cumple que sería llamado nazareno. Cada cumplimiento enlaza la infancia de Jesús con el Antiguo Testamento. Juntos forman un solo mensaje: la historia que comenzó con Abraham y pasó por David llega a su meta en este niño, el Mesías prometido y verdadero Israel.

en: Before any preaching or miracle, Unit 1 establishes that Jesus is the promised King and God Himself come among us. He is the Son of David, the rightful King; the Son of Abraham, through whom the nations are blessed; Jesus, who saves His people from their sins; and Immanuel, God with us. He is also the true Israel who fulfills His people's story. Because of this identity everyone must decide, like the Magi or like Herod, what they will do with Him.
That Jesus is the promised Messiah-King, the Savior from sin, and Immanuel, God with us.
es: Antes de su predicación o de un solo milagro, la Unidad 1 establece que Jesús es el Rey prometido y Dios mismo venido a nosotros. Es el hijo de David, Rey legítimo; el hijo de Abraham, en quien las naciones son bendecidas; Jesús, que salva a su pueblo de sus pecados; y Emanuel, Dios con nosotros. También es el verdadero Israel que cumple la historia de su pueblo, y por eso cada persona debe decidir qué hará con Él.

en: John the Baptist was the prophet who appeared in the wilderness of Judea, dressed in camel's hair and eating locusts and wild honey, and baptized people in the Jordan as they confessed their sins. His message was 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.' Matthew identifies him as the voice crying in the wilderness from Isaiah 40:3, the herald sent ahead to prepare the way of the LORD, just as a herald went before an ancient king. His whole purpose was to point people past himself to the One coming after him.
John was the wilderness prophet and herald who preached 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand,' fulfilling Isaiah 40:3 as the voice preparing the Lord's way.
es: Juan el Bautista fue el profeta que apareció en el desierto de Judea, vestido de pelo de camello y comiendo langostas y miel silvestre, y bautizaba en el Jordán a quienes confesaban sus pecados. Su mensaje era: 'Arrepentíos, porque el reino de los cielos se ha acercado.' Mateo lo identifica como la voz que clama en el desierto de Isaías 40:3, el heraldo que prepara el camino del Señor, como el que iba delante de un rey antiguo. Toda su gloria era que la gente mirara más allá de él hacia el que venía.

en: The Pharisees and Sadducees trusted their descent from Abraham as if their pedigree secured them before God, but John insisted that a bloodline cannot repent; only a person can. True repentance is not just regret or a good resolution but a turning away from sin and back to God. Such turning shows itself in fruit, which is why John demanded 'fruits worthy of repentance' and warned that the axe was already at the root of fruitless trees. In the same way, a Christian upbringing or church membership cannot replace personal repentance, because God has no grandchildren.
Ancestry cannot repent for anyone; true repentance is a personal turning from sin to God that produces fruit.
es: Los fariseos y saduceos confiaban en ser descendientes de Abraham como si su linaje los asegurara ante Dios, pero Juan les dijo que una estirpe no puede arrepentirse; solo una persona puede. El verdadero arrepentimiento no es solo remordimiento o un buen propósito, sino un volverse: apartarse del pecado y volverse a Dios. Ese cambio se demuestra con frutos dignos de arrepentimiento, y Juan advirtió que la segur ya estaba puesta a la raíz de los árboles sin fruto. Igualmente, una crianza cristiana no reemplaza la conversión personal, porque Dios no tiene nietos.

en: John's baptism was with water unto repentance, a baptism of preparation in which people confessed that they needed cleansing. It could express the need but not meet it. The Coming One, mightier than John, would baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire, pouring out God's own life on His people. He also carries the winnowing fan of judgment, gathering the wheat and burning the chaff, so He both saves and judges.
John's water baptism prepared people by confessing their need; Jesus would baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire, giving God's life and bringing judgment.
es: El bautismo de Juan era en agua para arrepentimiento, un bautismo de preparación en el que la gente confesaba su necesidad de limpieza. Podía expresar esa necesidad, pero no suplirla. El que venía, más poderoso que Juan, bautizaría con el Espíritu Santo y con fuego, derramando la vida misma de Dios sobre su pueblo. Además tiene el aventador en la mano: recoge el trigo y quema la paja, de modo que salva y también juzga.

en: Jesus had no sin to confess, so His baptism was not an act of personal repentance. When John objected, Jesus said it was fitting 'to fulfill all righteousness,' meaning He was doing what God required and taking His place beside the sinners He came to save. By stepping into the river with the guilty He identified Himself with His people from the very start of His ministry. It was the first step on a road that would end at the cross, where He would bear their sin.
He was not confessing His own sin but identifying with sinners in obedience to God, the first step toward the cross.
es: Jesús no tenía pecado que confesar, así que su bautismo no fue un acto de arrepentimiento propio. Cuando Juan se resistió, Jesús dijo que convenía 'cumplir toda justicia', es decir, hacer lo que Dios pedía y tomar su lugar junto a los pecadores que vino a salvar. Al descender al río con los culpables, se identificó con su pueblo desde el comienzo de su ministerio. Fue el primer paso de un camino que terminaría en la cruz.

en: When Jesus came up out of the water, the heavens opened and the Spirit of God descended on Him like a dove. At the same time the Father's voice spoke from heaven: 'This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.' So in one moment the Son stood in the water, the Spirit descended, and the Father spoke. This shows one God in three Persons, not three gods, and it marks Jesus' anointing for His work.
The Son was baptized, the Spirit descended like a dove, and the Father spoke from heaven, showing one God in three Persons.
es: Cuando Jesús subió del agua, los cielos se abrieron y el Espíritu de Dios descendió sobre Él como paloma. Al mismo tiempo, la voz del Padre habló desde el cielo: 'Éste es mi Hijo amado, en quien tengo contentamiento.' Así, en un solo momento, el Hijo estaba en el agua, el Espíritu descendía y el Padre hablaba. Esto revela a un solo Dios en tres Personas, no a tres dioses, y marca la unción de Jesús para su obra.

en: Recapitulation means Jesus relives Israel's story and gets it right. Israel spent forty years in the wilderness and failed repeatedly by grumbling for bread, testing God and turning to idols; Jesus, led by the Spirit, fasts forty days in the wilderness and stands firm where the nation fell. That makes Him the true Israel, faithful where Israel was faithless. He is also the new Adam, because He does not yield to the tempter who ruined the first man.
In His 40 days Jesus succeeded where Israel failed in its 40 years and resisted the tempter Adam yielded to, making Him the true Israel and new Adam.
es: La recapitulación significa que Jesús revive la historia de Israel y la hace bien. Israel pasó cuarenta años en el desierto y falló una y otra vez, murmurando por pan, tentando a Dios y yendo tras ídolos; Jesús, llevado por el Espíritu, ayuna cuarenta días y permanece firme donde la nación cayó. Así es el verdadero Israel, fiel donde Israel fue infiel. También es el nuevo Adán, porque no cede ante el tentador que arruinó al primer hombre.

en: First the devil told the hungry Jesus to turn stones into bread, using His power for His own appetite; Jesus answered from Deuteronomy that man lives not by bread alone but by every word from God's mouth. Second, on the pinnacle of the temple, Satan urged Him to throw Himself down and force God to rescue Him; Jesus replied, 'You shall not tempt the LORD your God.' Third, Satan offered all the kingdoms of the world if Jesus would worship him, a crown without the cross; Jesus said, 'Away with you, Satan,' because only God is to be worshiped and served. Each time He answered with 'It is written.'
Stones to bread, jumping from the temple, and worshiping Satan for the world's kingdoms; Jesus answered each with Scripture, 'It is written.'
es: Primero el diablo le dijo a Jesús, que tenía hambre, que convirtiera las piedras en pan; Jesús respondió con Deuteronomio que no solo de pan vivirá el hombre, sino de toda palabra que sale de la boca de Dios. Segundo, en el pináculo del templo, lo incitó a echarse abajo para forzar a Dios a rescatarlo; Jesús dijo: 'No tentarás al Señor tu Dios.' Tercero, le ofreció todos los reinos del mundo si lo adoraba, la corona sin la cruz; Jesús respondió: 'Vete, Satanás', porque solo a Dios se adora y sirve. Cada vez contestó con 'Escrito está'.

en: After John was imprisoned, Jesus moved to Capernaum in Galilee by the sea. Matthew sees this as fulfilling Isaiah 9:1-2, which spoke of 'Galilee of the Gentiles,' where people sitting in darkness and the shadow of death would see a great light. Jesus Himself is that light, and it dawns in a region the world considered least important and close to the Gentiles. It again shows the King's reach to the nations.
Jesus settling in Capernaum fulfilled Isaiah 9:1-2: in 'Galilee of the Gentiles' people in darkness saw a great light.
es: Después de que Juan fue encarcelado, Jesús se fue a vivir a Capernaum, en Galilea, junto al mar. Mateo ve en esto el cumplimiento de Isaías 9:1-2, que hablaba de 'Galilea de los gentiles', donde el pueblo asentado en tinieblas y sombra de muerte vería una gran luz. Jesús mismo es esa luz, y resplandece en una región que el mundo tenía por menos. Así se muestra otra vez que el Rey alcanza a las naciones.

en: Jesus began preaching with exactly John's words: 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.' This shows that John was only the herald preparing the way, and now the herald's torch passes to the King Himself. It also shows continuity: the kingdom John announced as coming is now arriving in the person of Jesus. And it shows the kingdom requires the same response, a real turning to God.
es: Jesús comenzó a predicar con las mismas palabras de Juan: 'Arrepentíos, porque el reino de los cielos se ha acercado.' Esto muestra que Juan era solo el heraldo que preparaba el camino, y ahora la antorcha pasa al Rey mismo. También muestra continuidad: el reino que Juan anunciaba ya llega en la persona de Jesús. Y la respuesta que exige sigue siendo la misma: un verdadero arrepentimiento.

en: Walking by the Sea of Galilee, Jesus called the fishermen Simon Peter and Andrew, saying, 'Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men,' and they immediately left their nets. Then He called James and John, who immediately left their boat and their father Zebedee. Matthew stresses the word 'immediately,' echoing Joseph's ready obedience. It teaches that the King gathers His kingdom not by force but by His word that summons and hearts that respond, one call at a time.
Jesus called Peter, Andrew, James and John, who immediately left everything to follow; the kingdom is gathered by His call and obedient response, not by force.
es: Andando junto al mar de Galilea, Jesús llamó a los pescadores Simón Pedro y Andrés: 'Venid en pos de mí, y os haré pescadores de hombres', y ellos dejaron luego las redes. Después llamó a Jacobo y a Juan, que dejaron al instante la barca y a su padre Zebedeo. Mateo subraya que obedecieron de inmediato, como José. Esto enseña que el Rey reúne su reino no por la fuerza, sino por una palabra que llama y un corazón que responde, un llamado a la vez.

en: When the crowds gathered, Jesus went up on a mountain and sat down to teach, the posture of a teacher. Matthew wants us to remember Moses going up Sinai and bringing down the law that formed Israel; now one greater than Moses gives the law of the kingdom of heaven, a kind of constitution for it. The sermon opens not with rules but with the Beatitudes, which describe the character of those who belong to God's kingdom. That character is paradoxical, blessing the poor, the mourning and the meek, the reverse of what the world calls blessed.
On a mountain, like Moses at Sinai, Jesus gives the law of His kingdom; the Beatitudes describe the upside-down character of kingdom people.
es: Cuando se reunieron las multitudes, Jesús subió a un monte y se sentó a enseñar, como lo hacía un maestro. Mateo quiere que recordemos a Moisés subiendo al Sinaí y bajando con la ley que formó a Israel; ahora uno mayor que Moisés da la ley del reino de los cielos, una especie de constitución del reino. El sermón no comienza con reglas sino con las Bienaventuranzas, que describen el carácter de quienes pertenecen al reino. Ese carácter es paradójico: bendice al pobre, al que llora y al manso, lo contrario de lo que el mundo llama bienaventurado.

en: To be poor in spirit is to feel your deep spiritual destitution and to understand your nothingness before God, instead of leaning on your talents or education. Dr. Cook describes how, as a young Christian, his own abilities kept failing him until the Spirit showed him his real spiritual poverty and he began seeking the Lord Himself. The opposite is the Pharisee, who proudly thanked God that he was not like other men. There must be emptiness before fullness, and the kingdom belongs to the poor in spirit because only empty hands reach out to be filled.
It is recognizing our spiritual bankruptcy before God, the opposite of the Pharisee's proud self-sufficiency; only the empty can be filled.
es: Ser pobre en espíritu es sentir una profunda destitución espiritual y comprender nuestra nada delante de Dios, en vez de apoyarnos en nuestros talentos o educación. El Dr. Cook cuenta que, de joven cristiano, sus habilidades le fallaban hasta que el Espíritu le mostró su verdadera pobreza espiritual y comenzó a buscar al Señor mismo. Lo opuesto es el fariseo, que con orgullo daba gracias a Dios por no ser como los demás hombres. Tiene que haber vacío antes de plenitud, y el reino pertenece a los pobres en espíritu porque solo las manos vacías se extienden para ser llenadas.

en: Biblical meekness is strength under control, great power harnessed and laid at God's feet. It is not weakness or being a doormat, as the joke group DOORMATS with its timid motto suggests. Moses confronting Pharaoh and Jesus driving the moneychangers from the temple were both meek, yet clearly not weak. Churchill's 'but I am a great man' shows the pride and blindness to one's faults that meekness lacks, while the surgeon who asked God's help before every operation shows humble dependence. The meek are promised that they will inherit the earth.
Meekness is strength under God's control, not timid weakness; Moses and Jesus were meek yet bold, unlike proud Churchill.
es: La mansedumbre bíblica es fuerza bajo control, un gran poder dominado y puesto a los pies de Dios. No es debilidad ni ser un felpudo, como sugiere en broma el grupo DOORMATS con su lema tímido. Moisés confrontando a Faraón y Jesús echando a los cambistas del templo eran mansos, pero no débiles. La respuesta de Churchill, 'pero yo soy un gran hombre', muestra el orgullo ciego que la mansedumbre no tiene, mientras que el cirujano que pedía la ayuda de Dios antes de cada operación muestra dependencia humilde. A los mansos se les promete que heredarán la tierra.

en: On their failed march to the South Pole in 1908, Shackleton and his companions were so starved that they talked about food every waking hour; that consuming craving is the picture of hungering for righteousness. Our problem is that we are too easily satisfied, and earthly appetites only produce more hunger, as with the rich young ruler. The righteousness meant here is right standing with God through justification and right living toward the helpless in compassion and obedience. The promise is that such people shall be filled, because God never starves an appetite He has given.
It means craving right standing with God and right living as desperately as starving Shackleton craved food; the promise is that they will be filled.
es: En su fracasado viaje al Polo Sur en 1908, Shackleton y sus compañeros tenían tanta hambre que hablaban de comida cada hora del día; ese anhelo consumidor es el cuadro de tener hambre y sed de justicia. Nuestro problema es que nos contentamos demasiado fácilmente, y el hambre terrenal solo produce más hambre, como le pasó al joven rico. La justicia aquí es la recta posición delante de Dios por la justificación y el recto vivir hacia el desvalido con compasión y obediencia. La promesa es que serán saciados, porque Dios no deja sin saciar un apetito que Él mismo dio.

en: The unit defines mercy as refraining from harming or punishing those who are in our power and who deserve punishment. In the story, a mother begged Napoleon for her son's life even though he had twice committed a capital offense. When Napoleon said the son did not deserve mercy, she replied that it would not be mercy if he deserved it, and the emperor spared him. The lesson is that mercy is by nature undeserved; those who have received an ocean of mercy from God extend it to others and will themselves obtain mercy.
Mercy is withholding deserved punishment from someone in our power; as the mother told Napoleon, it would not be mercy if it were deserved.
es: La unidad define la misericordia como abstenerse de dañar o castigar a quienes están en nuestro poder y merecen castigo. En la historia, una madre rogó a Napoleón por la vida de su hijo, que dos veces había cometido una ofensa digna de muerte. Cuando Napoleón dijo que el hijo no merecía misericordia, ella respondió que no sería misericordia si la mereciera, y el emperador lo perdonó. Esto enseña que la misericordia es, por naturaleza, inmerecida; los que han recibido un océano de misericordia de Dios la extienden a otros y alcanzarán misericordia.

en: A little girl scrubbed a window but could not remove one dirty spot, because it was on the other side of the glass. Many people likewise work hard on the outside through education, fashion and cosmetics while the real dirt is inside, like the Pharisees who cleaned the outside of the cup. Being pure in heart means having an inner life that is cleansed and undivided, single-minded devotion to God. The promise, the greatest of the Beatitudes, is that they shall see God.
Like the spot on the inside of the window, real cleansing must happen within; the pure in heart have an undivided inner devotion to God and shall see God.
es: Una niña lavaba una ventana pero no podía quitar una mancha, porque estaba del otro lado del vidrio. Así muchos se esfuerzan en lo exterior con educación, moda y cosméticos, mientras la suciedad real está adentro, como los fariseos que limpiaban lo de fuera de la copa. Ser limpio de corazón es tener una vida interior purificada e indivisa, una devoción a Dios de un solo corazón. La promesa, la mayor de las Bienaventuranzas, es que verán a Dios.

en: A peacemaker actively steps into conflict, takes the cost on himself, and makes peace where there was none, as in the Argentina-Chile arbitration commemorated by the Christ of the Andes. A peacemaker is not merely a peace-lover like Neville Chamberlain, whose appeasement bought a worse war, nor someone who keeps peace at any price, since Jesus also brought a sword. Peacemakers are called sons of God because that is exactly what God did for us in Christ: He bore the cost to make peace with us.
A peacemaker actively and at personal cost makes peace, not a passive peace-lover or peace-at-any-price; they are God's sons because God made peace with us in Christ.
es: Un pacificador interviene activamente en el conflicto, toma el costo sobre sí mismo y hace la paz donde no la había, como en el arbitraje entre Argentina y Chile que recuerda el Cristo de los Andes. No es simplemente un amante de la paz como Neville Chamberlain, cuya concesión solo compró una guerra peor, ni alguien que guarda la paz a cualquier precio, pues Jesús también trajo espada. Son llamados hijos de Dios porque eso es lo que Dios hizo por nosotros en Cristo: pagó el costo para hacer la paz.

en: Salt preserves what would rot and gives flavor to what is bland, so believers are meant to hold back corruption and bring savor to the world. Light drives back darkness and shows the way, so believers make God's truth visible. But salt can lose its savor and a lamp can be hidden under a basket. Jesus therefore calls His people to let their light shine so others see their good works and glorify the Father in heaven; the kingdom character is not to be kept as private piety.
As salt preserves and flavors and light dispels darkness, His people must live visibly so others see their good works and glorify God.
es: La sal preserva lo que se pudriría y da sabor a lo insípido, así que los creyentes deben frenar la corrupción y dar sabor al mundo. La luz hace retroceder las tinieblas y muestra el camino, así que hacen visible la verdad de Dios. Pero la sal puede perder su sabor y la lámpara puede esconderse bajo un almud. Por eso Jesús llama a su pueblo a dejar que su luz alumbre, para que otros vean sus buenas obras y glorifiquen al Padre; el carácter del reino no es para una piedad escondida.

en: In Matthew 5:17 Jesus says He did not come to destroy the Law or the Prophets but to fulfill them. Dr. Cook teaches that the Law was given to point us toward God's will, but it could never capture that will completely, since God's will includes what we should do as well as what we must not do. The commandments were never a means of salvation but a pointer to God's heart. Because Jesus knew the Father's will intimately, He got behind the laws to their intent, as in His 'You have heard... but I say to you' teaching on anger and lust. So our righteousness must exceed the Pharisees' surface rule-keeping with a heart-level righteousness.
The Law pointed toward God's will but could not fully capture it and never saved; Jesus fulfilled it by revealing its heart-level intent.
es: En Mateo 5:17 Jesús dice que no vino para abrogar la ley o los profetas, sino para cumplirlos. El Dr. Cook enseña que la Ley fue dada para señalarnos la voluntad de Dios, pero nunca pudo capturarla por completo, pues esa voluntad incluye lo que debemos hacer y no solo lo prohibido. Los mandamientos nunca fueron medio de salvación sino una señal hacia el corazón de Dios. Como Jesús conocía íntimamente la voluntad del Padre, fue detrás de las leyes a su intención, como en el 'oísteis que fue dicho... pero yo os digo' sobre el enojo y la codicia. Por eso nuestra justicia debe exceder la de los fariseos, con una justicia del corazón.

en: Together the Beatitudes show that the kingdom's character is the reverse of the world's idea of the good life: poor in spirit, mourning, meek, hungry for righteousness, merciful, pure, peacemaking and willing to be persecuted. They are not eight entrance requirements we achieve to earn God's acceptance. Rather, they describe the character God's grace forms in those who already belong to Him. Feature by feature they are a portrait of Jesus Christ Himself, which the King is forming in His people.
They show an upside-down character produced by grace, not earned, and they portray Jesus Christ Himself.
es: En conjunto, las Bienaventuranzas muestran que el carácter del reino es lo contrario de lo que el mundo considera la buena vida: pobre en espíritu, que llora, manso, hambriento de justicia, misericordioso, limpio, pacificador y dispuesto a ser perseguido. No son ocho requisitos que cumplimos para ganarnos la entrada. Más bien describen el carácter que la gracia de Dios forma en quienes ya le pertenecen. Rasgo por rasgo, son un retrato de Jesucristo mismo, que el Rey va formando en su pueblo.

en: Chapter 5 described who the citizens of the kingdom are, with the Beatitudes and the call to be salt and light. Chapters 6 and 7 turn to how they live, working that righteousness out in giving, prayer and fasting, in the use of money, in freedom from worry, in how we treat others, and finally in the decision between two foundations. The sermon refuses to let us admire the Beatitudes from a distance and presses them into ordinary daily life. The King wants obedience that runs deepest where only God is watching.
After describing kingdom character in chapter 5, Jesus applies it in chapters 6-7 to daily life: devotion, money, worry, relationships and obedience.
es: El capítulo 5 describe quiénes son los ciudadanos del reino, con las Bienaventuranzas y el llamado a ser sal y luz. Los capítulos 6 y 7 pasan a cómo viven, aplicando esa justicia al dar, orar y ayunar, al uso del dinero, a la libertad del afán, al trato con otros y, finalmente, a la decisión entre dos fundamentos. El sermón no permite admirar las Bienaventuranzas desde lejos, sino que las lleva a la vida diaria. El Rey busca una obediencia que sea más profunda precisamente donde solo Dios ve.

en: Jesus takes the three main acts of Jewish devotion, giving to the needy, prayer and fasting, and contrasts the hypocrites with the disciple. Hypocrites do them to be seen, and the applause of people is the only reward they get. The disciple gives without sounding a trumpet, prays in a closed room, and fasts without looking gloomy, doing it before the Father who sees in secret and will reward him. The key question is our audience: are we living for people's praise or before God alone?
Do them in secret for the Father, not to be seen like the hypocrites; the key question is whose audience we live for, men's or God's.
