Isaiah 53 portrays the suffering Servant who dies like a lamb for others' sins, so it leads directly to preaching Jesus' death and resurrection.
es: Isaías 53 describe a un Siervo llevado como cordero al matadero, herido por nuestras rebeliones, y por cuya llaga fuimos curados. Es la imagen más clara del Antiguo Testamento de un sustituto que sufre y muere por los pecados de otros y luego es vindicado. Eso es precisamente la historia de la crucifixión y resurrección de Jesús. Cuando el eunuco preguntó si el profeta hablaba de sí mismo o de otro, Felipe pudo comenzar desde esa Escritura y anunciarle a Jesús, porque el pasaje apunta naturalmente a Él. Muestra que el evangelio es el cumplimiento de lo prometido por los profetas.

en: Glenn Chambers was flying to Ecuador to begin a missionary radio ministry when he scribbled a note to his mother on a scrap of advertising paper printed with the word WHY?, and then his plane crashed. His mother received the letter after his death, with that question staring at her. That is the same question the church must have asked when Stephen, so gifted and full of the Spirit, was killed early in his ministry. Acts 8:1 begins to answer it: right after Stephen's death a great persecution scattered the believers through Judea and Samaria, so his death became the spark that launched the next stage of Acts 1:8. God does not always explain His reasons, but He uses the deaths of His servants to advance His purposes.
Like Chambers's mother asking 'WHY?', the church grieved Stephen's early death; Acts 8:1 shows that his death triggered the persecution that spread the gospel into Judea and Samaria.
es: Glenn Chambers volaba a Ecuador para comenzar un ministerio misionero de radio cuando escribió una nota a su madre en un papel publicitario con la palabra WHY? ('¿Por qué?'), y luego su avión se estrelló. Su madre recibió la carta después de su muerte, con esa pregunta delante. Es la misma pregunta que la iglesia debió hacerse cuando Esteban, tan lleno del Espíritu, murió al comienzo de su ministerio. Hechos 8:1 empieza a responder: justo después de su muerte hubo una gran persecución que esparció a los creyentes por Judea y Samaria, así que su muerte encendió la siguiente etapa de Hechos 1:8. Dios no siempre explica sus razones, pero usa la muerte de sus siervos para avanzar sus propósitos.

en: Acts 1:8 promised witness in Jerusalem, then Judea and Samaria, then the end of the earth, but until Stephen the church stayed in Jerusalem. Stephen's Spirit-filled sermon and martyrdom provoked a persecution that scattered, or sowed, the believers through Judea and Samaria, preaching wherever they went. Philip carried the gospel to the despised Samaritans with great joy, and Peter and John came to confirm the work, while Simon's attempt to buy the Spirit warned that God's gift is not for sale. Then Philip was led to the Ethiopian treasurer, a Gentile from the edge of the known world, who went home rejoicing. In these chapters God uses a dying deacon, persecution, and obedient ordinary believers to push the gospel past Jerusalem and touch the end of the earth for the first time.

Stephen's martyrdom scattered the church into Judea and Samaria, Philip evangelized the Samaritans, and his meeting with the Ethiopian brought the gospel to the end of the earth, fulfilling Acts 1:8's second and third stages.
es: Hechos 1:8 prometía testimonio en Jerusalén, luego en Judea y Samaria y hasta lo último de la tierra, pero hasta Esteban la iglesia se quedó en Jerusalén. El sermón y el martirio de Esteban provocaron una persecución que esparció, o sembró, a los creyentes por Judea y Samaria, predicando por dondequiera que iban. Felipe llevó el evangelio a los despreciados samaritanos con gran gozo, y Pedro y Juan vinieron a confirmar la obra, mientras que Simón, al querer comprar el Espíritu, mostró que el don de Dios no se vende. Luego Felipe fue guiado al tesorero etíope, un gentil del extremo del mundo conocido, que volvió gozoso. En estos capítulos Dios usa a un diácono mártir, la persecución y creyentes comunes y obedientes para llevar el evangelio más allá de Jerusalén y tocar por primera vez lo último de la tierra.

en: Saul was a zealous Pharisee trained under Gamaliel, and he hunted believers believing he was defending God's honor. Yet in Acts 5:39 his own teacher had warned the Sanhedrin that if this movement was from God they might be found fighting against God, and that is exactly what Saul did. Later he admitted he was a blasphemer and persecutor who acted ignorantly in unbelief. This teaches that sincerity and zeal are not enough; religious passion directed against the truth is still rebellion against God. We need humility to let Christ correct us, because we can be completely convinced and completely wrong.
es: Saulo era un fariseo celoso formado a los pies de Gamaliel, y perseguía a los creyentes creyendo defender la honra de Dios. Pero en Hechos 5:39 su propio maestro había advertido al Sanedrín que si el movimiento era de Dios podrían hallarse luchando contra Dios, y eso fue exactamente lo que hizo Saulo. Más tarde reconoció que fue blasfemo y perseguidor, y que lo hizo por ignorancia en incredulidad. Esto enseña que la sinceridad y el celo no bastan; la pasión religiosa dirigida contra la verdad sigue siendo rebelión contra Dios. Necesitamos humildad para dejar que Cristo nos corrija, porque podemos estar totalmente convencidos y totalmente equivocados.

en: On the Damascus road Jesus asked, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?' even though Saul had never laid a hand on Jesus Himself, only on His followers. This shows that Christ is so identified with His people that an attack on them is an attack on Him. Believers are united to Christ as His body, so He feels every blow they suffer. This is a comfort to persecuted Christians, who are never alone, and a warning to anyone who mistreats the church, because they are dealing with the Lord Himself.
By saying 'Me,' Jesus showed He is so united with His people that persecuting them is persecuting Him; He shares and feels their suffering.
es: En el camino a Damasco Jesús preguntó: 'Saulo, Saulo, ¿por qué me persigues?', aunque Saulo nunca había tocado a Jesús, sino a sus seguidores. Esto muestra que Cristo está tan identificado con su pueblo que atacarlo a ellos es atacarlo a Él. Los creyentes están unidos a Cristo como su cuerpo, de modo que Él siente cada golpe que sufren. Es un consuelo para los cristianos perseguidos, que nunca están solos, y una advertencia para quien maltrata a la iglesia, porque está tratando con el Señor mismo.

en: Saul was only angry at some Christians; Jesus did not care about the church

Ananias was an ordinary disciple in Damascus, and the Lord sent him to the very man who had come to the city with letters to arrest believers like him. He knew Saul's reputation and objected, but when the Lord said Saul was His chosen vessel, he went anyway, laid hands on him, and called him 'Brother Saul.' Obedience cost him the risk of his freedom and his life, and he had to set aside fear and suspicion. Through it the church gained Saul's healing, baptism, and commissioning, and so gained Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles and writer of much of the New Testament.
Ananias obeyed God by going to the persecutor who came to arrest him, risking his life; his obedience welcomed Saul into the church and helped give the church the apostle Paul.
es: Ananías era un discípulo común en Damasco, y el Señor lo envió al mismo hombre que había llegado con cartas para arrestar a creyentes como él. Conocía la fama de Saulo y objetó, pero cuando el Señor le dijo que Saulo era instrumento escogido, fue de todos modos, le impuso las manos y lo llamó 'hermano Saulo'. Obedecer le costó arriesgar su libertad y su vida, y tuvo que vencer el miedo y la sospecha. Gracias a ello Saulo recobró la vista, fue bautizado y comisionado, y la iglesia ganó a Pablo, el apóstol de los gentiles y autor de gran parte del Nuevo Testamento.

en: Before Saul had preached a single sermon, the Lord called him a chosen vessel to bear His name before Gentiles, kings, and Israel, and in the same breath said He would show him how much he must suffer for His name. The calling came with the price printed on it. This means a true calling is not a promise of success or comfort but of faithful service that will include suffering. When Paul later listed his beatings and shipwrecks in 2 Corinthians 11, he was not complaining but accepting what was part of his calling. We should present Christ's call honestly, counting the cost, so believers are not surprised or shaken when hardship comes.
Saul's calling included suffering from the start, so a genuine calling from Christ promises faithfulness, not ease, and we should count the cost rather than expect comfort.
es: Antes de que Saulo predicara un solo sermón, el Señor lo llamó instrumento escogido para llevar su nombre ante gentiles, reyes e Israel, y al mismo tiempo dijo que le mostraría cuánto le era necesario padecer por su nombre. El llamado vino con el precio incluido. Esto significa que un verdadero llamado no promete éxito ni comodidad, sino servicio fiel que incluirá sufrimiento. Cuando Pablo después enumeró sus azotes y naufragios en 2 Corintios 11, no se quejaba, sino que aceptaba lo que era parte de su llamado. Debemos presentar el llamado de Cristo con honestidad, calculando el costo, para que los creyentes no se sorprendan cuando venga la dificultad.

en: The first human words Saul heard in his new life were 'Brother Saul,' spoken by a man he had come to arrest. Ananias called him brother before he was baptized, before he had preached, before he had even regained his sight, simply because Christ had received him. This shows that Christian fellowship is grounded in what God has done, not in our past record. Real reconciliation can turn an enemy into a family member in two words, and churches should welcome repentant people, even former opponents, as true brothers and sisters.
By calling his former persecutor 'brother,' Ananias showed that grace makes enemies into family, and the church should welcome new believers on the basis of Christ's work, not their past.
es: Las primeras palabras humanas que Saulo oyó en su nueva vida fueron 'hermano Saulo', dichas por un hombre al que había venido a arrestar. Ananías lo llamó hermano antes de que fuera bautizado, antes de que predicara y antes de recobrar la vista, simplemente porque Cristo lo había recibido. Esto muestra que la comunión cristiana se basa en lo que Dios ha hecho, no en nuestro pasado. La verdadera reconciliación puede convertir a un enemigo en familia con dos palabras, y la iglesia debe recibir a los arrepentidos, incluso a antiguos opositores, como hermanos verdaderos.

en: Ananias received Saul through obedience: he overcame his fear, went to him, touched him, prayed for him, called him brother, and saw him baptized, giving the new convert his first experience of Christian love. Barnabas received him through advocacy: when the Jerusalem disciples were afraid and suspicious, he took Saul, brought him to the apostles, and told his story, putting his own reputation on the line. Pastorally, this teaches that new believers need both personal care at the start and someone to vouch for them and bring them into the community. Leaders should not let fear or a person's past keep them from welcoming those God has saved, while still listening to God's guidance as both men did.

Ananias obeyed despite fear and welcomed Saul as a brother, and Barnabas vouched for him when others were afraid; new converts need people who personally care for them and who risk their reputation to bring them in.
es: Ananías recibió a Saulo por obediencia: venció su miedo, fue a verlo, le impuso las manos, oró por él, lo llamó hermano y lo bautizó, dándole su primera experiencia del amor cristiano. Bernabé lo recibió como defensor: cuando los discípulos en Jerusalén tenían miedo y desconfiaban, lo tomó, lo llevó a los apóstoles y contó su historia, arriesgando su propia reputación. Pastoralmente, enseña que los nuevos creyentes necesitan cuidado personal al principio y alguien que responda por ellos y los integre a la comunidad. Los líderes no deben permitir que el miedo o el pasado de alguien les impida recibir a quien Dios ha salvado.

en: Saul came to Damascus to arrest believers, but after his conversion he immediately preached in the synagogues that Jesus is the Christ, and within weeks the Jews plotted to kill him and watched the gates. He had to escape by night, lowered over the wall in a basket, and in Jerusalem the Hellenists tried to kill him too. This shows that identifying with Christ means sharing His rejection; the same world that once praised Saul now hated him. Following Jesus can cost reputation, safety, and former friendships, just as the Lord had told Ananias Saul would suffer for His name.
Saul quickly faced the same plots he once led, showing that following Christ means sharing His rejection and can cost status, safety, and old relationships.
es: Saulo vino a Damasco para arrestar creyentes, pero después de su conversión predicó enseguida en las sinagogas que Jesús es el Cristo, y en pocas semanas los judíos planearon matarlo y vigilaban las puertas. Tuvo que escapar de noche, descolgado por el muro en una canasta, y en Jerusalén los helenistas también intentaron matarlo. Esto muestra que identificarse con Cristo implica compartir su rechazo; el mismo mundo que antes lo admiraba ahora lo odiaba. Seguir a Jesús puede costar reputación, seguridad y amistades, tal como el Señor le dijo a Ananías que Saulo padecería por su nombre.

en: When Saul came to Jerusalem, all the disciples, including the apostles, were afraid of him and did not believe he was a disciple. Barnabas, the Son of Encouragement, was the one who took him, brought him to the apostles, and explained how he had met the Lord and preached boldly in Damascus. Without Barnabas's courage Saul might never have been received, and without Paul there would be no Pauline epistles. In churches today Barnabases are the people who stand beside new believers others whisper about, encourage leaders who have failed, mentor young workers, and lend their trust to those who have not yet earned it. There are far more Barnabas roles than pulpits, and the church depends on them.
Barnabas alone risked vouching for Saul when even the apostles feared him; today the church needs encouragers who welcome, vouch for, and restore new or struggling believers.
es: Cuando Saulo llegó a Jerusalén, todos los discípulos, incluso los apóstoles, le tenían miedo y no creían que fuera discípulo. Bernabé, el Hijo de consolación, fue quien lo tomó, lo llevó a los apóstoles y contó cómo había visto al Señor y predicado con valentía en Damasco. Sin el valor de Bernabé, quizá Saulo nunca habría sido recibido, y sin Pablo no tendríamos sus epístolas. Hoy los Bernabé son quienes se ponen al lado del nuevo creyente del que otros murmuran, animan al líder que ha fracasado, acompañan a los jóvenes y prestan su confianza a quien aún no la ha ganado. Hay muchos más lugares para un Bernabé que púlpitos, y la iglesia depende de ellos.

en: The irony is that the church's greatest persecutor became a member of the church, and so the persecution that had scattered believers quieted down; the churches throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace, were built up, and multiplied. God did not end the persecution by defeating Saul with force but by converting him. This shows that the Lord is sovereign over persecution: He used it to spread the gospel, and He could stop it by changing the heart of its leader. Believers can trust that no opponent is beyond His reach and that He sets the limits on the church's suffering.
The persecution ended not by defeating Saul but by converting him, showing that the Lord rules over persecution and can turn the church's worst enemy into its friend.
es: La ironía es que el mayor perseguidor de la iglesia se convirtió en miembro de ella, y así la persecución se calmó; las iglesias de Judea, Galilea y Samaria tuvieron paz, eran edificadas y se multiplicaban. Dios no terminó la persecución venciendo a Saulo por la fuerza, sino convirtiéndolo. Esto muestra que el Señor es soberano sobre la persecución: la usó para extender el evangelio y pudo detenerla cambiando el corazón de su líder. Los creyentes pueden confiar en que ningún opositor está fuera de su alcance y que Él pone límites al sufrimiento de la iglesia.

en: The Sauls in our streets are the people who openly oppose or mock the gospel: the angry relative, the hostile coworker, the activist who despises the church, or the prodigal we have given up on. Acts 9 says no one is too far gone, because Christ still meets hardened people and makes Pauls out of Sauls. The Ananiases and Barnabases are ordinary church members who obey God despite fear, welcome converts as brothers and sisters, and vouch for them when others are suspicious. On the road to Damascus the Lord is still converting enemies, calling them to costly service, and using ordinary disciples to receive them, so the church must pray for its Sauls, count the cost honestly, and be ready to welcome them.

Sauls are today's hostile unbelievers whom Christ can still convert; ordinary believers must be Ananiases and Barnabases who welcome and vouch for them, because the Lord is still turning enemies into brothers.
es: Los Saulos de nuestras calles son quienes se oponen o se burlan abiertamente del evangelio: el familiar enojado, el compañero hostil, el activista que desprecia a la iglesia o el pródigo por quien ya no oramos. Hechos 9 dice que nadie está demasiado lejos, porque Cristo sigue encontrando a personas endurecidas y convirtiendo Saulos en Pablos. Los Ananías y Bernabé son miembros comunes de la iglesia que obedecen a Dios a pesar del miedo, reciben a los convertidos como hermanos y responden por ellos cuando otros desconfían. En el camino a Damasco el Señor sigue convirtiendo enemigos, llamándolos a un servicio costoso y usando a discípulos sencillos para recibirlos; por eso debemos orar por nuestros Saulos, hablar con honestidad del costo y estar listos para acogerlos.

en: Simon the tanner worked with the hides of dead animals, so by traditional Jewish standards his trade kept him ceremonially unclean. By staying in his house, Peter was already crossing a purity boundary before God showed him the vision about clean and unclean. Luke uses this quiet detail to prepare readers for the bigger step of entering a Gentile's home. In the same way, he sets up the scene by showing God at work on both ends at once: Cornelius praying in Caesarea and Peter praying on the rooftop in Joppa, so that the meeting is clearly God's arrangement.
A tanner was ritually unclean, so Peter lodging with him was already a small step across purity lines, preparing for his bigger step into Cornelius's Gentile home.
es: Simón el curtidor trabajaba con pieles de animales muertos, y según la tradición judía su oficio lo hacía ceremonialmente inmundo. Al hospedarse en su casa, Pedro ya estaba cruzando una frontera de pureza antes de que Dios le mostrara la visión sobre lo limpio y lo inmundo. Lucas usa este pequeño detalle para preparar al lector para el paso mayor de entrar en la casa de un gentil. Del mismo modo, prepara la escena mostrando a Dios obrando en ambos extremos: Cornelio orando en Cesarea y Pedro orando en la azotea de Jope, de modo que el encuentro es claramente obra de Dios.

en: While praying on the roof at noon, Peter saw a sheet lowered from heaven full of animals the Mosaic law called unclean, and a voice told him to kill and eat. He refused, saying he had never eaten anything common or unclean, and the voice answered that what God has cleansed he must not call common. It happened three times, which stressed that the message was certain and from God and had to break through Peter's lifelong habits. Peter did not see at first that it was about people because the vision was literally about food and he was hungry; only when Gentile messengers arrived and the Spirit told him to go with them did he understand that he should call no person common or unclean.

The sheet of unclean animals and the command to eat taught that God had cleansed what was unclean; the threefold repetition emphasized it, and Peter only understood it meant Gentile people when Cornelius's men arrived.
es: Mientras oraba en la azotea al mediodía, Pedro vio un lienzo que bajaba del cielo lleno de animales que la ley de Moisés llamaba inmundos, y una voz le dijo: 'Mata y come'. Él se negó, diciendo que nunca había comido nada común o inmundo, y la voz respondió: 'Lo que Dios limpió, no lo llames tú común'. Sucedió tres veces, lo cual subrayó que el mensaje era seguro y venía de Dios, y tenía que romper hábitos de toda la vida. Pedro no entendió al principio que se trataba de personas porque la visión era literalmente sobre comida y él tenía hambre; solo cuando llegaron los mensajeros gentiles y el Espíritu le dijo que fuera con ellos entendió que a ningún hombre debía llamar común o inmundo.

en: Peter declared in Cornelius's house that God shows no partiality; the Greek literally says God is not a 'face-receiver.' He does not choose favorites by ethnicity, nationality, passport, or pedigree, and anyone in any nation who fears Him is accepted. This means the gospel is offered on the same terms to every person, and no group has an advantage at the foot of the cross. The church therefore cannot rank people by race or nation, build ethnic barriers in fellowship, or treat some peoples as less worth reaching; every nation is a mission field, and every believer is an equal member of God's family.
God is not a 'face-receiver,' so He accepts people of every nation on the same terms; the church must reject ethnic favoritism and reach and welcome all peoples equally.
es: En la casa de Cornelio Pedro declaró que Dios no hace acepción de personas; el griego dice literalmente que Dios no 'recibe rostros'. No elige favoritos por etnia, nacionalidad o linaje, y en toda nación se agrada del que le teme y hace justicia. Esto significa que el evangelio se ofrece en los mismos términos a todos, y ningún grupo tiene ventaja al pie de la cruz. Por lo tanto, la iglesia no puede clasificar a las personas por raza o nación, ni levantar barreras étnicas en la comunión, ni considerar a algunos pueblos menos dignos de ser alcanzados; todos son iguales en la familia de Dios.

en: The Jerusalem believers criticized Peter for going into the house of uncircumcised men and eating with them. Peter did not argue from his authority; he simply told the story in order: the vision, the messengers, the Spirit's command, and the Holy Spirit falling on the Gentiles just as on the apostles at the beginning. He concluded that if God gave them the same gift, who was he to withstand God? The church fell silent and glorified God, saying God had granted repentance to life to the Gentiles too. This teaches gospel humility: when God clearly acts, believers must lay aside their traditions and prejudices, submit to what He is doing, and rejoice rather than resist.
Peter explained that God gave the Gentiles the same Spirit, so he could not resist God; the church humbly accepted it and praised God, showing we must yield our prejudices to God's work.
es: Los creyentes de Jerusalén criticaron a Pedro por entrar en casa de incircuncisos y comer con ellos. Pedro no se defendió con su autoridad, sino que contó todo en orden: la visión, los mensajeros, la orden del Espíritu y cómo el Espíritu Santo cayó sobre los gentiles como sobre ellos al principio. Concluyó que si Dios les dio el mismo don, ¿quién era él para resistir a Dios? La iglesia calló y glorificó a Dios, diciendo que también a los gentiles había dado arrepentimiento para vida. Esto enseña humildad ante el evangelio: cuando Dios actúa claramente, debemos dejar nuestras tradiciones y prejuicios, someternos a lo que Él hace y alegrarnos en lugar de resistir.

en: The 'hand of the Lord' is a Hebrew way of speaking about God's active power, and at Antioch it produced three results. First, conversions: a great number of Greeks believed and turned to the Lord. Second, commissions: Jerusalem sent Barnabas, who saw the revival was bigger than one man and fetched Saul from Tarsus; they taught for a year, and from Antioch came the first organized missionary effort. Third, celebrations: Barnabas saw the grace of God and was glad, and joy marked the church. Where God's hand moves, people are saved, workers are sent, and the church rejoices.
When the Lord's hand moved at Antioch, many were converted, Barnabas and Saul were commissioned to teach and later sent out, and there was gladness and joy.
es: La 'mano del Señor' es una forma hebrea de hablar del poder activo de Dios, y en Antioquía produjo tres resultados. Primero, conversiones: gran número de griegos creyó y se convirtió al Señor. Segundo, comisiones: Jerusalén envió a Bernabé, quien vio que el avivamiento era demasiado grande para uno solo y fue a buscar a Saulo a Tarso; enseñaron un año entero, y de Antioquía salió el primer esfuerzo misionero organizado. Tercero, celebraciones: Bernabé vio la gracia de Dios y se regocijó, y el gozo marcó a la iglesia. Donde se mueve la mano de Dios, la gente se salva, se envían obreros y la iglesia se alegra.

en: In 1904 Joseph Jenkins asked his young people what Jesus meant to them, and after awkward silence a timid girl named Flory Evans, converted only weeks before, said she loved the Lord Jesus with all her heart. That simple confession set the village on fire, and through Evan Roberts the revival spread until about a hundred thousand came to Christ in months, with crime and drunkenness dropping sharply. Like Antioch, where unnamed scattered believers simply spoke to Greeks and the hand of the Lord was with them, revival did not start with famous leaders or marketing plans. It teaches that revival begins when God's hand moves through ordinary people with sincere, personal love for Jesus, and it is followed by conversions, commissions, and celebration.
Both Antioch and Wales began through ordinary, unnamed believers, not big programs; revival starts when God moves through simple, sincere love for Jesus.
es: En 1904 Joseph Jenkins preguntó a sus jóvenes qué significaba Jesús para ellos, y tras un silencio incómodo una muchacha tímida, Flory Evans, convertida hacía pocas semanas, dijo que amaba al Señor Jesús con todo su corazón. Esa confesión sencilla encendió el pueblo, y por medio de Evan Roberts el avivamiento se extendió hasta que unos cien mil vinieron a Cristo en pocos meses, y bajaron mucho el crimen y la embriaguez. Como en Antioquía, donde creyentes anónimos esparcidos hablaron a los griegos y la mano del Señor estuvo con ellos, el avivamiento no comenzó con líderes famosos ni campañas. Enseña que el avivamiento empieza cuando Dios obra por medio de personas sencillas con un amor sincero y personal por Jesús.

en: At Antioch outsiders gave the believers the name Christianoi, meaning something like 'Christ's people' or 'little Christs.' It was probably a slightly mocking label, the way people name the followers of a leader, because these believers talked about Christ constantly and their lives were so marked by Him. The believers accepted the name and wore it ever since. For us today, bearing the name means living in such a way that people who watch us naturally connect us with Jesus, and being willing to carry that label even when it brings scorn.
'Christians' was likely a mocking label from pagans meaning 'Christ's people'; today the name should describe lives so marked by Christ that others see Him in us.
es: En Antioquía los de afuera llamaron a los creyentes Christianoi, algo así como 'los de Cristo' o 'pequeños cristos'. Probablemente era una etiqueta algo burlona, porque estos creyentes hablaban siempre de Cristo y su vida estaba marcada por Él. Los creyentes aceptaron el nombre y lo llevan hasta hoy. Para nosotros, llevar ese nombre significa vivir de tal manera que quienes nos observan nos relacionen naturalmente con Jesús, y estar dispuestos a llevarlo aunque traiga desprecio.

en: Herod killed James, the brother of John, with the sword, making him the first apostle to be martyred, but when he arrested Peter an angel freed him from prison while the church prayed. Both men were faithful apostles, and the church surely prayed for both, yet God allowed one to die and rescued the other. This shows that God's providence is sovereign and not a reward system; deliverance does not mean greater faith, and death does not mean God has abandoned someone. Whether through suffering or rescue, God is working out His purposes, and in the end the persecutor Herod falls while the word of God grows.
es: Herodes mató a espada a Jacobo, hermano de Juan, el primer apóstol mártir, pero cuando arrestó a Pedro, un ángel lo libró de la cárcel mientras la iglesia oraba. Ambos eran apóstoles fieles, y sin duda la iglesia oró por los dos, pero Dios permitió que uno muriera y libró al otro. Esto muestra que la providencia de Dios es soberana y no un sistema de premios; la liberación no significa más fe, ni la muerte significa que Dios abandonó a alguien. Tanto en el sufrimiento como en el rescate Dios cumple sus propósitos, y al final el perseguidor Herodes cae mientras la palabra de Dios crece.

en: The church was praying earnestly for Peter at Mary's house, yet when Rhoda recognized his voice at the gate, she was so excited she forgot to open it, and the others told her she was out of her mind and said it must be his angel. Meanwhile Peter kept knocking in the street. Luke gently shows that believers often pray for something and then struggle to believe it when God answers. The lesson is not to mock them but to recognize ourselves: God answers prayer even when our faith is weak, and we should pray expecting Him to act.
The church prayed for Peter but didn't believe it when he showed up, a gentle reminder that we often pray without expecting God to answer, yet He answers anyway.
es: La iglesia oraba con fervor por Pedro en casa de María, pero cuando Rode reconoció su voz en la puerta, se alegró tanto que olvidó abrir, y los demás le dijeron que estaba loca y que sería su ángel. Mientras tanto Pedro seguía tocando en la calle. Lucas muestra con suavidad que los creyentes muchas veces oran por algo y luego les cuesta creer cuando Dios responde. La lección no es burlarse de ellos sino reconocernos: Dios responde aun cuando nuestra fe es débil, y debemos orar esperando que Él actúe.

en: Acts 12 opens with Herod killing James and arresting Peter, looking like the powerful king is winning against the church. At the end Herod accepts the crowd's praise as a god, an angel strikes him because he did not give glory to God, and he is eaten by worms and dies. The very next verse says, 'But the word of God grew and multiplied.' Placing these side by side summarizes the chapter: persecutors who exalt themselves fall, while God's word keeps advancing. It reminds us that earthly rulers come and go, but God buries His opponents and His gospel cannot be stopped.
Herod, who persecuted the church and took God's glory, dies under judgment while the word of God grows, summarizing that persecutors fall but the gospel keeps spreading.
es: Hechos 12 comienza con Herodes matando a Jacobo y encarcelando a Pedro, como si el rey poderoso estuviera venciendo a la iglesia. Al final Herodes acepta que el pueblo lo aclame como dios, un ángel lo hiere porque no dio la gloria a Dios, y muere comido de gusanos. El versículo siguiente dice: 'Pero la palabra del Señor crecía y se multiplicaba'. Ponerlos juntos resume el capítulo: los perseguidores que se exaltan caen, mientras la palabra de Dios sigue avanzando. Nos recuerda que los gobernantes vienen y van, pero Dios entierra a sus opositores y su evangelio no puede ser detenido.

en: The Antioch leaders were Barnabas, a Levite from Cyprus; Simeon called Niger, probably a black African; Lucius from Cyrene in North Africa; Manaen, raised in the court of Herod the tetrarch; and Saul, a former persecutor from Tarsus. It was the first multi-ethnic, multi-class leadership team in church history, and they worshiped, fasted, and listened to the Spirit together. This shows that in Christ ethnic and social barriers do not decide who leads; the Spirit unites diverse people. A diverse leadership also fits a church whose mission is to reach every nation, and it was from this team that the first missionaries were sent out.
Antioch's leaders came from different races, regions, and social classes, showing that the gospel unites diverse people in leadership and equips a church to reach all nations.
es: Los líderes de Antioquía eran Bernabé, levita de Chipre; Simón llamado Níger, probablemente africano negro; Lucio de Cirene, en el norte de África; Manaén, criado junto con Herodes el tetrarca; y Saulo, antiguo perseguidor de Tarso. Fue el primer equipo de liderazgo multiétnico y de distintas clases sociales en la historia de la iglesia, y juntos ministraban al Señor, ayunaban y escuchaban al Espíritu. Esto muestra que en Cristo las barreras étnicas y sociales no determinan quién dirige, porque el Espíritu une a personas diversas. Un liderazgo diverso también corresponde a una iglesia cuya misión es alcanzar a todas las naciones, y de este equipo salieron los primeros misioneros.

en: In Acts 13 the Holy Spirit said to set apart Barnabas and Saul, which is the vertical call from God, and the Antioch church fasted, prayed, laid hands on them, and sent them, which is the horizontal confirmation of the local church. Luke says both that the church sent them and that they were sent out by the Holy Spirit. Both are needed. A person who claims a private call from God but never lets the church test and confirm it may be acting on self-will or emotion without accountability. A church that sends people the Spirit has not called is running on human planning and may send the wrong people. Together the two confirmations act like a cornerstone for a sound missionary call.
A missionary call needs the Spirit's inner call and the church's outward confirmation; a private call alone lacks accountability, and church sending alone may lack God's leading.
es: En Hechos 13 el Espíritu Santo dijo: 'Apartadme a Bernabé y a Saulo', que es el llamado vertical de Dios, y la iglesia de Antioquía ayunó, oró, les impuso las manos y los despidió, que es la confirmación horizontal de la iglesia local. Lucas dice que la iglesia los envió y también que fueron enviados por el Espíritu Santo. Ambos son necesarios. Quien afirma un llamado privado de Dios sin dejar que la iglesia lo pruebe y confirme puede estar actuando por voluntad propia o emoción, sin rendir cuentas. Una iglesia que envía a quien el Espíritu no ha llamado depende solo de planes humanos y puede enviar a la persona equivocada. Juntas, las dos confirmaciones son como una piedra angular para un llamado misionero sano.

en: At first Luke names the pair 'Barnabas and Saul,' with Barnabas as the senior partner, but after the confrontation with Elymas on Cyprus he begins calling Saul by the name Paul and speaks of 'Paul and his party.' The protégé had become the leader, and Barnabas, the encourager who had once vouched for Saul, stepped back without jealousy. This shows that good mentoring aims to raise up others who may surpass us. Leaders need humility and grace to hand over leadership when God's gifting becomes clear in someone else, putting the mission ahead of their own position.
es: Al principio Lucas los llama 'Bernabé y Saulo', con Bernabé como líder, pero después del enfrentamiento con Elimas en Chipre comienza a llamarlo Pablo y habla de 'Pablo y sus compañeros'. El discípulo se había convertido en el líder, y Bernabé, el consolador que antes había respaldado a Saulo, dio un paso atrás sin celos. Esto muestra que un buen mentor busca levantar a otros que quizá lo superen. Los líderes necesitan humildad y gracia para ceder el liderazgo cuando Dios muestra sus dones en otro, poniendo la misión por encima de su propia posición.

en: John Mark went with Paul and Barnabas as their assistant but left them at Perga and returned to Jerusalem, for reasons Luke does not give. Later Paul refused to take him on the second journey, and the sharp disagreement split Paul and Barnabas; Barnabas took Mark to Cyprus and kept investing in him. Years later, from prison in Rome, Paul wrote 'Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for ministry,' and Mark wrote the second Gospel. This teaches that failure need not be final; people who quit can be restored when someone refuses to give up on them, and the church should be patient and redemptive with its Marks.
Mark quit at Perga, but Barnabas did not give up on him, and later Paul called him useful and he wrote a Gospel; those who fail can be restored when others patiently invest in them.
es: Juan Marcos acompañó a Pablo y Bernabé como ayudante, pero los dejó en Perge y volvió a Jerusalén, por razones que Lucas no explica. Después Pablo se negó a llevarlo en el segundo viaje, y la fuerte desavenencia separó a Pablo y Bernabé; Bernabé llevó a Marcos a Chipre y siguió invirtiendo en él. Años más tarde, desde la cárcel en Roma, Pablo escribió: 'Toma a Marcos y tráelo contigo, porque me es útil para el ministerio', y Marcos escribió el segundo Evangelio. Esto enseña que el fracaso no tiene que ser definitivo; quien abandona puede ser restaurado cuando alguien no se rinde con él, y la iglesia debe ser paciente con sus Marcos.

en: Paul's sermon in the synagogue at Pisidian Antioch follows a pattern much like Stephen's speech. He reviews Israel's history: the patriarchs, the Exodus, the wilderness, the judges, King Saul, and King David, then moves to David's descendant Jesus, His introduction by John the Baptist, His rejection and crucifixion, His burial, His resurrection, and His appearances. The climax in verses 38–39 announces that through Jesus forgiveness of sins is preached, and that everyone who believes in Him is justified from all things from which the law of Moses could not justify. Justification is presented as a gift received by believing in Christ, not earned by keeping the law, which could never open that door.

Paul surveys Israel's history up to David and Jesus' death and resurrection, then climaxes by offering forgiveness and justification to everyone who believes, something the law of Moses could never provide.
es: El sermón de Pablo en la sinagoga de Antioquía de Pisidia sigue un modelo parecido al de Esteban. Repasa la historia de Israel: los patriarcas, el éxodo, el desierto, los jueces, el rey Saúl y el rey David, y luego pasa a Jesús, descendiente de David, presentado por Juan el Bautista, rechazado y crucificado, sepultado, resucitado y aparecido a sus discípulos. El clímax en los versículos 38 y 39 anuncia que por medio de Jesús se predica el perdón de pecados, y que en Él es justificado todo aquel que cree de todo aquello de que la ley de Moisés no pudo justificar. La justificación se presenta como un don recibido por fe en Cristo, no ganado por cumplir la ley.

en: When Paul turned to the Gentiles in Pisidian Antioch and they rejoiced, Luke says that as many as had been appointed to eternal life believed. This shows that behind the preaching and the human response stands God's sovereign choice; the Lord knows His own and calls them when the gospel comes. The doctrine of election is part of the bedrock of Acts, not an add-on. Yet election does not replace preaching: those appointed believed when they heard the word, so it gives missionaries confidence that God has people to save and that their labor is not in vain.
The verse shows that God's sovereign appointment lies behind saving faith; those He chose believed when they heard the gospel, which encourages bold preaching rather than replacing it.
es: Cuando Pablo se volvió a los gentiles en Antioquía de Pisidia y ellos se regocijaron, Lucas dice que creyeron todos los que estaban ordenados para vida eterna. Esto muestra que detrás de la predicación y la respuesta humana está la elección soberana de Dios; el Señor conoce a los suyos y los llama cuando llega el evangelio. La doctrina de la elección forma parte del fundamento de Hechos. Sin embargo, la elección no sustituye la predicación: los ordenados creyeron al oír la palabra, y esto da confianza a los misioneros de que Dios tiene un pueblo que salvar y que su trabajo no es en vano.

en: Human choice alone decides eternal life; God has no sovereignty in it

After Paul healed a man lame from birth, the people of Lystra decided he and Barnabas were Hermes and Zeus, and the priest of Zeus brought oxen and garlands to sacrifice to them; the missionaries tore their clothes and could barely stop them. Then Jews from Antioch and Iconium arrived, the same crowd turned, stoned Paul, and dragged him out of the city for dead. Crowds are fickle: their admiration is shallow and can flip into hatred in an instant. Ministry built on popularity or applause is unreliable, so ministers should refuse worship, point people to the living God, and build on faithful disciples, like those who gathered around Paul, rather than on the crowd's mood.
The crowd that wanted to worship Paul soon stoned him, showing that popularity is fickle and ministry must rest on God and faithful disciples, not crowd approval.
es: Después de que Pablo sanó a un hombre cojo de nacimiento, los de Listra pensaron que él y Bernabé eran Mercurio y Júpiter, y el sacerdote de Júpiter trajo toros y guirnaldas para ofrecerles sacrificio; los misioneros rasgaron sus ropas y apenas lograron impedirlo. Luego llegaron judíos de Antioquía e Iconio, la misma multitud cambió, apedreó a Pablo y lo arrastró fuera de la ciudad creyéndolo muerto. Las multitudes son volubles: su admiración es superficial y puede convertirse en odio en un instante. Un ministerio basado en la popularidad no es confiable; el ministro debe rechazar la adoración, señalar al Dios vivo y edificar sobre discípulos fieles, como los que rodearon a Pablo.

en: At the Council, Peter reminded the leaders that God had chosen him to bring the gospel to Cornelius's household and that God, who knows hearts, gave them the Holy Spirit just as He did to the Jewish believers, making no distinction and purifying their hearts by faith. Then he asked why they would test God by putting on the disciples' neck a yoke that neither their fathers nor they themselves had been able to bear. He was admitting that even Jews never kept the Mosaic law perfectly, so demanding it of Gentiles as the price of salvation would charge them more than Jews had ever paid. He concluded that Jews and Gentiles alike are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus.
Peter argued that God gave Gentiles the Spirit without circumcision and that the law was a yoke even Jews could not bear, so both are saved only by the grace of Jesus.
es: En el Concilio, Pedro recordó que Dios lo escogió para llevar el evangelio a la casa de Cornelio, y que Dios, que conoce los corazones, les dio el Espíritu Santo igual que a los creyentes judíos, sin hacer diferencia y purificando sus corazones por la fe. Luego preguntó por qué tentaban a Dios poniendo sobre el cuello de los discípulos un yugo que ni sus padres ni ellos habían podido llevar. Reconocía que ni siquiera los judíos cumplieron perfectamente la ley de Moisés, así que exigirla a los gentiles como precio de la salvación sería cobrarles más de lo que los judíos jamás pagaron. Concluyó que judíos y gentiles son salvos por la gracia del Señor Jesús.

en: James, the Lord's brother, was the leading pastor in Jerusalem and the most strictly Torah-observant believer present, known as 'Old Camel Knees' for his constant prayer for Israel. If anyone would have insisted on circumcision for Gentiles, it would have been him. Instead, citing the prophet Amos, he ruled that the church should not trouble Gentiles who were turning to God, asking only that they avoid food offered to idols, blood, strangled meat, and sexual immorality so that table fellowship with Jewish believers was possible. Because the verdict came from him, the Judaizers lost their strongest possible champion, and it carried great weight in uniting the church around salvation by grace.
Because James was the most law-observant leader, his ruling that Gentiles need not be circumcised carried decisive weight and removed any claim that faithful Jews required it.
es: Jacobo, el hermano del Señor, era el pastor principal en Jerusalén y el creyente más estricto en guardar la Torá, conocido como 'rodillas de camello' por orar tanto por Israel. Si alguien iba a exigir la circuncisión a los gentiles, era él. Sin embargo, citando al profeta Amós, decidió que no se debía inquietar a los gentiles que se convertían a Dios, y solo les pidió abstenerse de lo sacrificado a ídolos, de sangre, de ahogado y de fornicación, para que fuera posible la comunión en la mesa con los judíos. Como el veredicto vino de él, los judaizantes perdieron a su posible defensor más fuerte, y la decisión tuvo gran peso para unir a la iglesia en la salvación por gracia.

en: In this section every form of opposition becomes a channel for advance. Bar-Jesus tried to turn the proconsul away, but his blinding led Sergius Paulus to believe. The Lystran mob stoned Paul, yet he rose, kept preaching in Derbe, and returned to strengthen the new churches, teaching that we enter the kingdom through many tribulations. The Judaizers' demand for circumcision forced the Jerusalem Council, which clearly affirmed salvation by grace through faith alone for Gentiles. Even the sharp split between Paul and Barnabas produced two missionary teams instead of one, with Barnabas restoring Mark and Paul gaining Silas and Timothy. The result, as Acts 16:5 says, was churches strengthened in the faith and increasing in number daily.

God used each opposition for growth: Elymas's blindness converted the proconsul, Paul's stoning didn't stop the mission, the Judaizers' challenge clarified grace, and the split doubled the missionary teams.
es: En esta sección cada oposición se convierte en un medio de avance. Barjesús intentó apartar al procónsul, pero su ceguera llevó a Sergio Paulo a creer. La turba de Listra apedreó a Pablo, pero él se levantó, siguió predicando en Derbe y volvió para fortalecer a las iglesias, enseñando que es necesario entrar al reino a través de muchas tribulaciones. La exigencia de circuncisión de los judaizantes provocó el Concilio de Jerusalén, que afirmó claramente la salvación por gracia mediante la fe para los gentiles. Incluso la separación entre Pablo y Bernabé produjo dos equipos misioneros en vez de uno, con Bernabé restaurando a Marcos y Pablo sumando a Silas y Timoteo. El resultado, como dice Hechos 16:5, fueron iglesias confirmadas en la fe que aumentaban en número cada día.

en: On the second journey Paul, Silas, and Timothy tried to preach in the province of Asia, but the Holy Spirit forbade them, and when they tried Bithynia the Spirit did not permit them. They ended up at Troas apparently without direction. These closed doors were not punishment or failure but God's steering: He was moving them away from one region so He could send them into Europe. That night Paul saw a man of Macedonia pleading, 'Come over and help us,' and they went immediately. This teaches that the Spirit sometimes says no to good plans in order to give a better yes, and faithful workers should wait, stay sensitive, and obey quickly when He shows the way.
The Spirit closed Asia and Bithynia to redirect Paul to Macedonia through the vision; closed doors are often God's detour toward a bigger opportunity, so we should wait and obey promptly.
es: En el segundo viaje, Pablo, Silas y Timoteo intentaron predicar en la provincia de Asia, pero el Espíritu Santo se lo prohibió, y cuando intentaron ir a Bitinia el Espíritu no se lo permitió. Llegaron a Troas aparentemente sin dirección. Esas puertas cerradas no eran castigo ni fracaso, sino la dirección de Dios, que los apartaba de una región para enviarlos a Europa. Esa noche Pablo vio a un varón macedonio que le rogaba: 'Pasa a Macedonia y ayúdanos', y partieron enseguida. Esto enseña que el Espíritu a veces dice no a buenos planes para dar un sí mejor, y los siervos fieles deben esperar, estar atentos y obedecer con prontitud.

en: Lydia, a seller of purple from Thyatira who worshiped God, heard Paul preach by the river at Philippi, and Luke says the Lord opened her heart to heed what Paul said. The emphasis is on God's gracious initiative: she did not pry her heart open by her own effort, but God worked inside her as she heard the word. Christians from Reformed and Arminian traditions explain the relationship between God's work and human response differently, but both should let Luke's point stand. A theology of conversion should therefore hold that preaching and hearing are necessary, yet conversion is ultimately the Lord's work, which keeps evangelists humble and prayerful.
Luke stresses that God took the initiative, opening Lydia's heart as she heard the gospel; conversion involves hearing the word but is finally the Lord's gracious work.
es: Lidia, vendedora de púrpura de Tiatira que adoraba a Dios, escuchó a Pablo junto al río en Filipos, y Lucas dice que el Señor abrió su corazón para que estuviera atenta a lo que Pablo decía. El énfasis está en la iniciativa de la gracia de Dios: ella no abrió su corazón por su propio esfuerzo, sino que Dios obró en ella mientras oía la palabra. Los cristianos reformados y arminianos explican de manera distinta la relación entre la obra de Dios y la respuesta humana, pero ambos deben respetar el énfasis de Lucas. Una teología de la conversión debe sostener que predicar y oír son necesarios, pero que la conversión es en última instancia obra del Señor, lo cual nos mantiene humildes y en oración.

en: The slave girl had a spirit of divination, a 'python' spirit linked to the oracle at Delphi, and for many days she followed the missionaries shouting that they were servants of the Most High God proclaiming the way of salvation. Her words were true, but the source was demonic, and Paul would not let the gospel be endorsed by an evil spirit or be associated with pagan fortune-telling. So he commanded the spirit in Jesus' name to come out. This teaches that discernment looks not only at whether a statement is accurate but at where it comes from and what it serves; the devil can use truth to confuse people, and Christians should not welcome every voice that says nice things about them.
Though her words were true, they came from a demonic spirit, so Paul refused that endorsement; discernment weighs the source and spirit behind a message, not just its words.
es: La muchacha esclava tenía un espíritu de adivinación, un espíritu 'pitón' relacionado con el oráculo de Delfos, y durante muchos días siguió a los misioneros gritando que eran siervos del Dios Altísimo que anunciaban el camino de salvación. Sus palabras eran verdaderas, pero la fuente era demoníaca, y Pablo no quiso que el evangelio fuera respaldado por un espíritu malo ni asociado con la adivinación pagana. Por eso mandó al espíritu en el nombre de Jesús que saliera de ella. Esto enseña que el discernimiento no solo pregunta si algo es exacto, sino de dónde viene y a qué sirve; el diablo puede usar la verdad para confundir, y no debemos aceptar toda voz que hable bien de nosotros.

en: When a string snapped during his concert, Itzhak Perlman, who already lives with the effects of polio, did not leave the stage but played the whole concerto on three strings, later saying that sometimes the artist's task is to find out how much music you can still make with what you have left. Paul and Silas in the Philippian jail had also lost much: their backs were torn from beatings, their feet were in stocks, and their mission looked ruined. Yet at midnight they prayed and sang hymns, making music with what was left, and the other prisoners listened. God answered with an earthquake and the jailer's salvation. The connection teaches that loss does not have to end our worship or usefulness; God can bring His greatest work out of what looks like defeat, as He did at the cross.
Like Perlman playing on three strings, Paul and Silas, beaten and chained, still sang praise with what they had left, and God used it to save the jailer; loss need not stop our worship or ministry.
es: Cuando se le rompió una cuerda durante un concierto, Itzhak Perlman, que vive con las secuelas de la polio, no se retiró, sino que tocó todo el concierto con tres cuerdas, y luego dijo que a veces la tarea del artista es descubrir cuánta música puede hacer con lo que le queda. Pablo y Silas en la cárcel de Filipos también habían perdido mucho: sus espaldas estaban heridas por los azotes, sus pies en el cepo y su misión parecía arruinada. Sin embargo, a medianoche oraban y cantaban himnos, haciendo música con lo que les quedaba, y los presos los escuchaban. Dios respondió con un terremoto y la salvación del carcelero. La conexión enseña que la pérdida no tiene que terminar nuestra adoración ni nuestra utilidad; Dios puede sacar su mayor obra de lo que parece derrota, como en la cruz.

en: Luke calls the Bereans more noble or fair-minded than the Thessalonians because they received the word eagerly and searched the Scriptures daily to see if what Paul said was true. They were neither gullible nor cynical; they were students who tested even an apostle by God's word. Local churches should follow this model by welcoming teaching with open hearts while checking it against Scripture. Being too credulous leaves a church open to false teachers and fads, since it accepts whatever a preacher says. Being too cynical closes people to the truth, so they reject sound teaching and never grow. The Bereans held both openness and testing together, and many believed.
The Bereans eagerly received Paul's message but checked it daily in Scripture; churches should be open yet test everything, since credulity invites error and cynicism rejects the truth.
es: Lucas dice que los de Berea eran más nobles que los de Tesalónica, porque recibieron la palabra con toda solicitud y escudriñaban cada día las Escrituras para ver si estas cosas eran así. No eran ni crédulos ni cínicos; eran estudiantes que examinaban aun a un apóstol con la palabra de Dios. Las iglesias locales deben seguir este modelo, recibiendo la enseñanza con corazón abierto pero comparándola con las Escrituras. Ser demasiado crédulos deja a la iglesia expuesta a falsos maestros y modas, porque acepta todo lo que dice un predicador. Ser demasiado cínicos cierra el corazón a la verdad, de modo que se rechaza la buena enseñanza. Los bereanos unieron apertura y examen, y muchos creyeron.

en: Paul was deeply provoked by the idols of Athens, yet on Mars Hill he began respectfully by noting that they were very religious and pointing to their altar 'To the Unknown God.' He used their own inscription and quoted their own poets, then proclaimed the true God they did not know: the Creator of the world, who does not live in temples made with hands, who sets the times and boundaries of nations so people might seek Him, and who will judge the world through a Man He raised from the dead. This is a model for engaging other cultures: start where people are, find points of contact in their own ideas and longings, but do not stop there; move clearly to repentance, judgment, and the resurrection of Jesus without compromising the message.

Paul started from the Athenians' own altar and poets to introduce the true Creator, then called them to repent in light of Christ's resurrection; we should begin where people are but still proclaim the full gospel.
es: A Pablo le dolió profundamente la idolatría de Atenas, pero en el Areópago comenzó con respeto, notando que eran muy religiosos y señalando su altar 'Al Dios no conocido'. Usó su propia inscripción y citó a sus poetas, y luego anunció al Dios verdadero que no conocían: el Creador del mundo, que no habita en templos hechos por mano, que fijó los tiempos y límites de las naciones para que lo buscaran, y que juzgará al mundo por medio de un Varón a quien levantó de los muertos. Es un modelo para alcanzar otras culturas: comenzar donde está la gente, buscar puntos de contacto en sus ideas y anhelos, pero no quedarse allí, sino llegar claramente al arrepentimiento, al juicio y a la resurrección de Jesús sin comprometer el mensaje.

en: When Paul spoke of the resurrection, some Athenians mocked, some said 'We will hear you again on this matter,' and some believed, including Dionysius and Damaris. The mockers at least made their rejection plain. The delayers sounded polite and open-minded, but their answer was really a courteous no that put off the decision indefinitely. It is the most dangerous response because it feels safe, keeps the person comfortable, and hides refusal behind interest; there is no record that Paul ever preached in Athens again, so 'later' never came. The gospel calls for a response now, and postponing it is itself a decision.
'We will hear you again' is a polite no that postpones decision; it is dangerous because it feels harmless while the opportunity may never come again, as Paul never returned to preach in Athens.
es: Cuando Pablo habló de la resurrección, algunos atenienses se burlaron, otros dijeron 'Ya te oiremos acerca de esto otra vez', y algunos creyeron, como Dionisio y Dámaris. Los burladores al menos dejaron claro su rechazo. Los que postergaron parecían corteses y abiertos, pero su respuesta era en realidad un no educado que dejaba la decisión para nunca. Es la respuesta más peligrosa porque parece segura, mantiene cómoda a la persona y esconde el rechazo detrás del interés; no hay registro de que Pablo predicara otra vez en Atenas, así que el 'después' nunca llegó. El evangelio pide una respuesta ahora, y postergarla ya es una decisión.

en: In Corinth Paul joined Aquila and Priscilla, Jewish believers expelled from Rome by Claudius, and since all three were tentmakers they worked together making tents while Paul preached every Sabbath. The greatest theologian of the early church supported himself with his hands so he would not be a financial burden on the new churches, as he later reminded the Ephesian elders. This shows that bivocational ministry is honorable and biblical, not second-class. Pastors may rightly receive support, but there are times when working a trade protects the gospel from accusations of greed, eases the burden on young or poor churches, and keeps the minister close to ordinary working people. It also shows the value of lay partners like Priscilla and Aquila in ministry.
Paul worked as a tentmaker with Aquila and Priscilla so he wouldn't burden the young church; bivocational ministry is honorable and can protect the gospel and ease a church's load.
es: En Corinto Pablo se unió a Aquila y Priscila, judíos creyentes expulsados de Roma por Claudio, y como los tres eran fabricantes de tiendas, trabajaban juntos mientras Pablo predicaba cada sábado. El mayor teólogo de la iglesia primitiva se sostenía con sus manos para no ser carga económica para las nuevas iglesias, como luego recordó a los ancianos de Éfeso. Esto muestra que el ministerio bivocacional es honroso y bíblico, no de segunda categoría. Los pastores pueden recibir sostén, pero hay ocasiones en que trabajar en un oficio protege al evangelio de acusaciones de codicia, alivia la carga de iglesias pequeñas o pobres y mantiene al ministro cerca de la gente trabajadora. También muestra el valor de colaboradores laicos como Priscila y Aquila.

en: Paul came to Corinth, a city notorious for immorality, in fear and trembling, and after being thrown out of the synagogue he could have been discouraged. The Lord appeared to him at night and told him not to be afraid but to keep speaking, because He was with him and had many people in that city. God knew His people in Corinth before Paul knew their names, and Paul stayed eighteen months. This encourages discouraged pastors and missionaries that results do not depend on them alone; the Lord is present with them and already has people He intends to save in their city. They should keep preaching faithfully and stay, trusting that He will gather those who are His.
The Lord told Paul not to fear because He was with him and had many people in Corinth; discouraged ministers can keep preaching, trusting that God is present and has people to save in their city.
es: Pablo llegó a Corinto, una ciudad famosa por su inmoralidad, con temor y mucho temblor, y después de ser expulsado de la sinagoga podía estar desanimado. El Señor se le apareció de noche y le dijo que no temiera, sino que hablara y no callara, porque Él estaba con él y tenía mucho pueblo en esa ciudad. Dios conocía a su pueblo en Corinto antes de que Pablo supiera sus nombres, y Pablo se quedó dieciocho meses. Esto anima a los pastores y misioneros desanimados: los resultados no dependen solo de ellos; el Señor está con ellos y ya tiene personas que va a salvar en su ciudad. Deben seguir predicando con fidelidad y permanecer, confiando en que Él reunirá a los suyos.

en: On the second journey the gospel crossed from Asia into Europe for the first time, planting churches in Philippi, Thessalonica, and Berea in Macedonia and in Athens and Corinth in Achaia. Several strategic lessons emerge. First, follow the Spirit's guidance, even through closed doors, as with the Macedonian vision. Second, adapt the setting while keeping the message: Paul preached to women at a riverside, to a jailer in prison, to Jews in synagogues, to philosophers in the marketplace, and to the council on Mars Hill, always proclaiming Jesus and the resurrection. Third, build households and local leaders, like Lydia, the jailer, and Crispus, and partner with lay workers like Aquila and Priscilla. Fourth, endure suffering with worship and stay where God has many people, as in Corinth. Finally, train believers to be Bereans who test teaching by Scripture.

The gospel entered Europe through Spirit-led steps, contextual preaching to every class without changing the message, household conversions, lay partnerships, and perseverance in suffering, lessons that still guide missions.
es: En el segundo viaje el evangelio pasó por primera vez de Asia a Europa, plantando iglesias en Filipos, Tesalónica y Berea en Macedonia, y en Atenas y Corinto en Acaya. Surgen varias lecciones estratégicas. Primero, seguir la guía del Espíritu aun ante puertas cerradas, como en la visión macedonia. Segundo, adaptar el contexto sin cambiar el mensaje: Pablo predicó a mujeres junto al río, a un carcelero en la prisión, a judíos en sinagogas, a filósofos en el mercado y al concilio en el Areópago, siempre anunciando a Jesús y la resurrección. Tercero, alcanzar familias y formar líderes locales, como Lidia, el carcelero y Crispo, y trabajar con colaboradores laicos como Aquila y Priscila. Cuarto, soportar el sufrimiento adorando y permanecer donde Dios tiene mucho pueblo. Por último, formar creyentes que, como los de Berea, examinen todo con las Escrituras.

en: Apollos was an eloquent Alexandrian, mighty in the Scriptures and fervent in spirit, but he knew only the baptism of John and had not yet heard the full message of the cross, resurrection, and Spirit. Aquila and Priscilla did not rebuke him publicly or attack him; they took him aside and explained the way of God more accurately in private. As a result he became one of the most useful preachers in the early church and a colleague of Paul. Today, when a gifted teacher has gaps in his theology, the right approach is humble, private, generous correction that preserves his dignity and builds him up, rather than public criticism that shames him or drives him away.

They privately and humbly explained the way of God more fully to Apollos instead of shaming him publicly; gifted but incomplete teachers today should be corrected the same way, which can make them far more useful.
es: Apolos era un alejandrino elocuente, poderoso en las Escrituras y ferviente de espíritu, pero solo conocía el bautismo de Juan y no había oído todo el mensaje de la cruz, la resurrección y el Espíritu. Aquila y Priscila no lo reprendieron en público ni lo atacaron; lo tomaron aparte y le expusieron más exactamente el camino de Dios. Gracias a eso llegó a ser uno de los predicadores más útiles de la iglesia primitiva y colega de Pablo. Hoy, cuando un maestro dotado tiene vacíos teológicos, lo correcto es una corrección humilde, privada y generosa que respete su dignidad y lo edifique, en vez de una crítica pública que lo avergüence o lo aleje.

en: When Paul asked the twelve men in Ephesus whether they had received the Holy Spirit, they said they had not even heard there was a Holy Spirit; they had only received John's baptism of repentance. They were sincere, had repented, been baptized, and tried to live godly lives, yet they had not heard or believed in Jesus, the One John pointed to. Once Paul explained, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus and received the Spirit. This teaches that repentance, baptism, moral seriousness, and religious emotion are not the same as salvation. Without Christ himself, religious practice, however earnest, leaves people short of the gospel.
They had repented and been baptized into John's baptism but did not know Jesus or the Spirit; religious practice and sincerity without faith in Christ do not save.
es: Cuando Pablo preguntó a los doce hombres en Éfeso si habían recibido el Espíritu Santo, respondieron que ni siquiera habían oído si había Espíritu Santo; solo tenían el bautismo de arrepentimiento de Juan. Eran sinceros, se habían arrepentido, se habían bautizado y procuraban vivir piadosamente, pero no habían oído ni creído en Jesús, a quien Juan señalaba. Cuando Pablo les explicó, fueron bautizados en el nombre del Señor Jesús y recibieron el Espíritu. Esto enseña que el arrepentimiento, el bautismo, la seriedad moral y la emoción religiosa no son lo mismo que la salvación. Sin Cristo mismo, la práctica religiosa, por sincera que sea, se queda corta del evangelio.

en: The Didache, the earliest Christian teaching manual, begins by saying there are two ways: the way of life and the way of death. The lesson applies this to the Ephesian disciples, who were on John's road, a real, holy, and necessary road that pointed to Christ but did not end where the way of Jesus ends. Like Edison finding many ways not to make a light bulb, there are many ways not to be saved. The danger of a road close to the gospel is that it looks right from a distance, so people feel safe while they are still lost; they may have repentance, baptism, emotional experiences, or Bible knowledge, yet lack Christ. Only Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life, so we must make sure we and others are actually on His road.
There are only two ways, life and death; a road near the gospel, like John's baptism or religion without Christ, is dangerous because it feels safe while still not leading to salvation.
es: La Didajé, el manual de enseñanza cristiana más antiguo, comienza diciendo que hay dos caminos: el de la vida y el de la muerte. La lección lo aplica a los discípulos de Éfeso, que andaban por el camino de Juan, un camino real, santo y necesario que señalaba a Cristo, pero que no terminaba donde termina el camino de Jesús. Como Edison descubrió muchas maneras de no hacer una bombilla, hay muchas maneras de no ser salvo. El peligro de un camino parecido al evangelio es que de lejos parece correcto, y la gente se siente segura aunque sigue perdida; puede tener arrepentimiento, bautismo, experiencias o conocimiento bíblico, pero no a Cristo. Solo Jesús es el camino, la verdad y la vida.

en: After leaving the synagogue, Paul taught daily in the lecture hall of Tyrannus, possibly from eleven to four during the hottest part of the day, and he kept it up for two years. Luke says that as a result all who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks, heard the word of the Lord. Faithful, patient, everyday teaching in one rented room, multiplied through the disciples who carried the message out, reached an entire region. This teaches that we should not despise small, steady, unglamorous work; sustained daily instruction that trains believers can have far greater reach than occasional big events.
Two years of daily teaching in a rented hall spread the word through all Asia, showing that patient, consistent teaching and training of disciples can reach a whole region.
es: Después de salir de la sinagoga, Pablo enseñó cada día en la escuela de Tirano, posiblemente de las once a las cuatro, en la hora más calurosa, y continuó así durante dos años. Lucas dice que como resultado todos los que habitaban en Asia, judíos y griegos, oyeron la palabra del Señor. La enseñanza fiel, paciente y diaria en un salón alquilado, multiplicada por los discípulos que llevaban el mensaje, alcanzó a toda una región. Esto enseña que no debemos menospreciar el trabajo pequeño, constante y poco vistoso; la instrucción diaria y sostenida que forma creyentes puede llegar mucho más lejos que los grandes eventos ocasionales.

en: The seven sons of Sceva tried to cast out a demon by invoking 'the Jesus whom Paul preaches,' using His name like a magic formula without belonging to Him. The demon answered that it knew Jesus and knew Paul but did not know them, and then overpowered them and drove them out naked and wounded. This shows that the spiritual world recognizes only two kinds of people: those who truly belong to Christ and those who do not. Borrowing Christian vocabulary, quoting verses, or saying 'God bless' at public events gives no spiritual authority. What matters is a real relationship with Christ, being His blood-bought people, not using His name secondhand.
Using Jesus' name without belonging to Him has no power; the demons recognize genuine believers, not people who merely borrow Christian words.
es: Los siete hijos de Esceva intentaron expulsar un demonio invocando 'a Jesús, el que predica Pablo', usando su nombre como fórmula mágica sin pertenecerle. El demonio respondió que conocía a Jesús y sabía quién era Pablo, pero no a ellos, y luego los dominó y los hizo huir desnudos y heridos. Esto muestra que el mundo espiritual reconoce solo dos clases de personas: las que realmente pertenecen a Cristo y las que no. Tomar prestado el vocabulario cristiano, citar versículos o decir 'Dios te bendiga' en actos públicos no da autoridad espiritual. Lo que importa es una relación real con Cristo, ser comprados por su sangre, no usar su nombre de segunda mano.

en: After the Sceva incident, fear of the Lord fell on Ephesus, and many believers confessed their magical practices and burned their expensive occult books publicly. Luke records the value as fifty thousand pieces of silver, roughly a hundred and fifty years of a laborer's wages, an enormous fortune. It represents costly, visible repentance: they valued an honest relationship with Christ more than wealth and did not simply sell the books to others. Modern equivalents might include getting rid of occult objects or horoscopes, pornography, gambling apps, dishonest business income, or anything else we treasure that competes with Christ, even when it costs money.
Fifty thousand silver pieces showed costly, real repentance; today it could mean getting rid of occult items, pornography, or sinful sources of income, whatever the cost.
es: Después de lo ocurrido con los hijos de Esceva, el temor del Señor cayó sobre Éfeso, y muchos creyentes confesaron sus prácticas de magia y quemaron públicamente sus costosos libros de ocultismo. Lucas calcula su valor en cincuenta mil piezas de plata, unos ciento cincuenta años de salario de un jornalero, una fortuna enorme. Representa un arrepentimiento costoso y visible: valoraron una relación honesta con Cristo más que la riqueza, y no vendieron los libros a otros. Hoy podría equivaler a deshacerse de objetos ocultistas u horóscopos, pornografía, aplicaciones de apuestas, ingresos deshonestos o cualquier cosa que compita con Cristo, aunque cueste dinero.

en: Demetrius made silver shrines of Artemis (Diana), and he warned the other craftsmen that Paul's teaching that gods made with hands are not gods was hurting their prosperity and would also bring the temple into disrepute. His order is revealing: the trade came first, the goddess second. He stirred up a riot in the theater where thousands shouted 'Great is Diana of the Ephesians,' many not even knowing why they were there. This shows that the gospel threatens economic interests built on sin and idolatry, and that organized opposition often has money behind it even when it uses religious language. Today the gospel can still challenge industries like pornography, occult practices, corruption, or exploitation, and if our message never costs the marketplace anything, we should ask if we are preaching Paul's gospel.
Demetrius opposed Paul mainly because the gospel hurt his idol-making business; the gospel still threatens profits built on sin, and opposition is often driven by money disguised as religion.
es: Demetrio fabricaba templecillos de plata de Diana, y advirtió a los demás artesanos que la enseñanza de Pablo, de que no son dioses los que se hacen con las manos, perjudicaba su prosperidad y además desacreditaría el templo. Su orden es revelador: primero el negocio, después la diosa. Provocó un tumulto en el teatro, donde miles gritaban '¡Grande es Diana de los efesios!', muchos sin saber por qué estaban allí. Esto muestra que el evangelio amenaza los intereses económicos basados en el pecado y la idolatría, y que la oposición organizada a menudo tiene dinero detrás aunque use lenguaje religioso. Hoy el evangelio sigue desafiando industrias como la pornografía, el ocultismo, la corrupción o la explotación.

en: At Troas, on the first day of the week, Paul preached until midnight in a hot upper room full of lamps, and a young man named Eutychus, whose name means 'fortunate,' fell asleep on the windowsill and dropped three stories to his death. Paul went down, embraced him like Elijah with the widow's son, said his life was in him, then went back up, broke bread, and kept talking until dawn, and the church was greatly comforted. Luke tells it with gentle humor, and the lesson notes that preachers can put people to sleep. Pastorally, it reminds preachers to be mindful of their hearers' limits, yet also shows God's grace covering human weakness on both sides: the sleepy listener is restored and the church's fellowship continues. It also shows the early church gathering on the first day of the week to break bread.
Paul's long sermon put Eutychus to sleep and he fell, but God raised him; preachers should be mindful of their listeners, and the Lord graciously covers human weakness.
es: En Troas, el primer día de la semana, Pablo predicó hasta la medianoche en un aposento alto caluroso y lleno de lámparas, y un joven llamado Eutico, cuyo nombre significa 'afortunado', se durmió en la ventana y cayó desde el tercer piso, muerto. Pablo bajó, lo abrazó como Elías al hijo de la viuda, dijo que su vida estaba en él, luego volvió a subir, partió el pan y siguió hablando hasta el amanecer, y la iglesia fue muy consolada. Lucas lo cuenta con humor suave, y la lección reconoce que los predicadores pueden hacer dormir a la gente. Pastoralmente, recuerda al predicador tener en cuenta los límites de sus oyentes, pero también muestra que la gracia de Dios cubre la debilidad humana de ambos lados. Además muestra a la iglesia reuniéndose el primer día de la semana para partir el pan.

en: At Miletus Paul called the Ephesian elders and reminded them how he had served with humility, tears, and trials, teaching publicly and from house to house. 'The whole counsel of God' means he did not hold back any part of God's revealed truth, including the hard or unpopular parts, but declared everything they needed for salvation and godly living. He charged them to guard themselves and the flock, which God purchased with His own blood, against savage wolves who would come from outside and even rise from among them. 'Warning everyone night and day with tears' describes the heart of true pastoral ministry: constant, personal, compassionate concern for each person's soul. Like Moody after the Chicago fire, a pastor should preach with urgency and tears for the lost and the flock.
'The whole counsel of God' means teaching all of God's truth without avoiding hard parts; 'warning with tears' describes persistent, compassionate, urgent care for every soul in the flock.
es: En Mileto Pablo llamó a los ancianos de Éfeso y les recordó cómo había servido con humildad, lágrimas y pruebas, enseñando públicamente y por las casas. 'Todo el consejo de Dios' significa que no retuvo ninguna parte de la verdad revelada, incluso lo difícil o impopular, sino que anunció todo lo necesario para la salvación y la vida piadosa. Les encargó cuidar de sí mismos y del rebaño, que Dios ganó con su propia sangre, contra lobos rapaces que vendrían de afuera y aun de entre ellos mismos. 'Amonestar con lágrimas noche y día a cada uno' describe el corazón del verdadero pastorado: un cuidado constante, personal y compasivo por cada alma. Como Moody después del incendio de Chicago, el pastor debe predicar con urgencia y lágrimas.

en: On the way to Jerusalem, believers at Tyre warned Paul through the Spirit, and at Caesarea the prophet Agabus tied his own hands and feet with Paul's belt, saying the Jews would bind its owner and hand him to the Gentiles. Everyone, including Luke, begged Paul not to go. Paul replied that their weeping was breaking his heart, but he was ready not only to be bound but to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus. The church then stopped pleading and said, 'The will of the Lord be done.' This models courage that knows the cost and goes forward anyway because of a clear call, and it models submission both in Paul, who surrendered his life, and in the church, which surrendered its wishes to God's will.

Paul knew chains awaited him but was ready to suffer and even die for Jesus, and the church yielded saying 'The will of the Lord be done'; true courage obeys God's call despite the cost and submits to His will.
es: Camino a Jerusalén, los creyentes de Tiro le advirtieron a Pablo por el Espíritu, y en Cesarea el profeta Agabo se ató las manos y los pies con el cinto de Pablo, diciendo que los judíos atarían al dueño de ese cinto y lo entregarían a los gentiles. Todos, incluso Lucas, le rogaron que no subiera. Pablo respondió que su llanto le quebrantaba el corazón, pero que estaba dispuesto no solo a ser atado, sino a morir en Jerusalén por el nombre del Señor Jesús. Entonces la iglesia dejó de insistir y dijo: 'Hágase la voluntad del Señor'. Esto muestra una valentía que conoce el costo y sigue adelante por un llamado claro, y una sumisión tanto en Pablo, que entregó su vida, como en la iglesia, que rindió sus deseos a la voluntad de Dios.

en: James warned Paul that tens of thousands of Jewish believers were zealous for the law and had heard false rumors that Paul taught Diaspora Jews to abandon Moses and circumcision. He proposed that Paul join four men completing a Nazirite vow and pay for their sacrifices, publicly showing he still honored the law.
